News.title: Pavarotti’s tailor in £550k ‘mouldy’ wine legal fight with fridge fit firm after claiming leaks damaged £1m collection
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

NESSUN TRAUMA Pavarotti’s tailor in £550k ‘mouldy’ wine legal fight with fridge fit firm after claiming leaks damaged £1m collection

A MULTI-millionaire tailor claims leaky fridges at his posh apartment led to mould on his £1million French wine collection.

Tom Reimer, who once kitted out Luciano Pavarotti, is suing the firm that put them in for £550,000.

Wine lover Mr Reimer claims the value of his 1,500 bottle collection was ruined by faults on three wine chillers installed for £23,000 in a refurb of his £8million flat in Marylebone, London.

He says a 1cm gap in the doors led to temperatures widely varying from the 12-13C wine fridges need to be.





This is claimed to have led to mould on labels and some vintages “probably” becoming corked.

The tailor’s firm created a white silk tailcoat for Pavarotti in the 1990s.

He is suing International Food Services Equipment Ltd of Croydon, South London, which fitted the chillers in 2021.

He is seeking £500,000 for wine damage plus £50,000 costs at Central London county court.

His barrister Ololade Saromi said the faults led to a “loss of environmental control, excessive condenser operation, vibration, overheating, condensation and damage to the wine collection”.

But the firm’s barrister ­Matthew Winn-Smith said the doors were “part of a standard unit and the airgap complained of is a necessary element of sliding doors”.

He claimed the damage came from repeatedly turning off the coolers if neighbours complained about the noise.

The trial continues.

News.title: Can I water my plants during a hosepipe ban?
News.content:
MILLIONS of households across the UK are facing hosepipe bans after an exceptionally warm and dry spring.

Major water companies have rolled out Temporary Use Bans (TUBs) across large parts of the country to protect dwindling water levels.

Breaking a hosepipe ban can trigger a hefty £1,000 fine at a magistrates’ court under The Water Industry Act of 1991.



But with sprinklers silenced and hosepipes tucked away, how can green-fingered Brits keep their gardens blooming?



Can I water my plants during a hosepipe ban?

When a hosepipe ban is declared, using a hosepipe connected to the mains water supply to water your garden is strictly forbidden.

But the restriction specifically targets hosepipes, sprinklers, and pressure washers — not tap water itself.

As such, the good news is that yes, you can still water your garden during a hosepipe ban.



To do so, you’re going to need to grab a trusty watering can or bucket, as this is the main way to keep your garden legally thriving.

You’re allowed to fill up watering cans or buckets from your outdoor tap and carry them to your flowerbeds, borders, and pots.

Can I use a hosepipe to water any plants?

While general hosepipe use is off-limits, many water suppliers make specific legal exemptions for certain plants and situations.

For example, you can water fresh lawn turf with a hose for up to 28 days after it has been laid.



Saplings, hedges, and trees planted within the recent planting season (usually up to 6–12 months) can also be watered with a hose.

If you’re growing fruit and vegetables at home or on an allotment, they can often be watered with a hose if carrying heavy watering cans is not practical.

To double-check the exact rules where you live, simply pop your postcode into Water UK’s online supplier checker to be directed to your local water provider’s guidelines.

If you have a Blue Badge or are registered on your water supplier’s Priority Services Register (PSR), you are exempt from the restrictions.

This allows you to use a hosepipe to water your garden if carrying heavy watering cans is physically unsafe or unmanageable.



Even if you qualify for an exemption or the plants in your garden “allow” you to use a hosepipe, you should try to use a watering can where possible to help protect local water levels.

Are there other ways to water plants during a hosepipe ban?

If lugging heavy cans sounds like hard work, you don’t necessarily have to abandon automated garden watering.

But standard lawn sprinklers, misters, and spray guns attached to a hose are strictly banned.

Instead, you can use a drip or trickle irrigation system, provided it meets the criteria required by water companies.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The system must drip water directly onto or beneath the soil surface right at the plant roots, rather than spraying water into the air.



It must also have an automatic timer installed so it cannot run continuously, and include a pressure-reducing valve to limit flow.

News.title: Jimothy the viral racoon may not be alone, experts say as spate of sightings suggest MORE short-spined critters run amok
News.content:
JIMOTHY the viral raccoon may not be alone after a string of reported sightings.

The unusually-shaped animal took the internet by storm last week due its particularly short spine.



Experts have now claimed there may be more than one deformed raccoon roaming the streets of Seattle.

As the mutant’s popularity grows, many have questioned whether it’s the same Jimothy, or if there are multiple animals suffering from the condition.



Local resident Rebecca Sorenson told Fox 13 Seattle: “There’s posts now that say he was born a year ago and then other people with posts that saw him in 2017.

“I’m curious now if there are more than one?”



Jimothy reportedly suffers from short spine syndrome – a rare congenital condition that affects “almost zero” per cent of animals.

Animal keeper Wendi Mallo said she’d be surprised if it was the same animal that some claimed to have spotted nearly 10 years ago.



“Yeah that seems like a very long-lived raccoon to me for the wild,” she said.

Mallo added that raccoons managed in proper conditions typically live much longer than those in the wild.

“In the wild, 3 to 5 years would be doing really well,” she said.

“A lot of raccoons don’t even make it through their first year.”

Consequently, Mallo said it’s hard to know whether Jimothy is that old or if there is more than one patient out there.



Despite the apparent deformities, Mallo said Jimothy appeared to be in good condition.

“I’m amazed at how well he’s done and I’m amazed at the magic that’s in our own backyards,” the animal keeper said.

“I think that it’s a nice little wakeup call for us to kind of notice what’s back there and pay attention.”

Kiana Hall, 33, was enjoying a late-night walk with her partner when she first caught a glimpse of the animal.

“I got very confused at what I was seeing. I just have never seen any other animal like it,” she said.



Hall was able to deduce the grey-furred creature was a raccoon from its facial marking, but suspected it suffered from some sort of genetic defect.

She continued: “I just hope Jimothy continues to live his life freely and I hope he can be healthy.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The extraordinary creature has now become a regular feature of Seattle subreddits, including popular forum Weird and Creepy.

One user wrote: “He needs to be protected at all costs.”

News.title: Shocking moment drunk driver leaves road and flies through air before crashing Land Rover into lamppost
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment a drunk driver leaves the road and flies through the air before crashing his Land Rover into a lamppost.

Horror footage captures offshore worker Alistair Thompson, 34, while under the influence on the evening of November 14 last year.



In a stunning clip, the Land Rover can be seen racing into view as it mounts a grass embankment in Aberdeen, Scotland.

The plush motor then veers off at speed and is momentarily airborne before crashing back down onto the tarmac.



Thompson’s car then careers across the road and smashes head-first into a lamppost, bringing the vehicle to a stop.

The lamppost can be seen crashing to the ground as the car’s hazard lights blare.





Thompson’s girlfriend was a passenger as the chaos unfolded with the crash leaving her injured.

But she has since made a full recovery.

Thompsonnhas now been sentenced at Aberdeen Sheriff Court for driving while under the influence and driving dangerously.

The footage of the crash was shown in court and was subsequently released by the Crown and Procurator Fiscal Service.

Sentencing, Sheriff Johnston said he was more than twice the legal limit when he was tested after the crash.



She said: “This could have been so much worse for other members of the public.

“The fact that you made that decision in light of a previous conviction of drink driving in 2018 shows an astounding degree of arrogance on your part.”

Thompson, of Aberdeen, was sentenced to 300 hours unpaid work.

He was also slapped with a driving ban for 40 months.

News.title: Shocking moment idiots prise open window and base jump from top of Blackpool Tower in ‘extremely dangerous’ stunt
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment idiots prise open a window and jump from the top of Blackpool Tower in an “extremely dangerous” stunt.

An investigation into the groups brazen antics has been launched after they leapt from the window in the iconic landmark on Sunday.



Video footage of the stunt shows the group entering Blackpool Tower posing as paying customers.

They queue with other members of the public before heading for the top floor of the massive 158 metre tower.



On the upper levels, the group can be seen testing various windows to see if they’ll open.

The fools cover their faces in the video with silver skulls as they look for a spot to jump from and the public mills around them.

One of them eventually manages to pull a window open – telling a man in the tower “sorry mate, just doing a window inspection.”

After getting the window open the base jumper immediately leaps from it and plunges towards the ground.



He then releases his parachute and glides towards the nearby beach as stunned onlookers watch on.

Another man then follows suit – leaping from the still open window as children watch.

He also deploys a parachute before landing on a nearby rooftop.

A third man then jumps from the window and deploys a parachute before landing on the beach alongside his companion.

The trio then pack up their parachutes and make their way away from the beach.



Blackpool Tourism Ltd the jump could have had “catastrophic consequences for both those involved and members of the public.”

The organisation added that it had contacted police.

All three of the men who leapt from the tower are reportedly members of LMSD [Lets Make Stupid Decisions].



They are understood to have used a special tool to unlock the windows.

Blackpool Tourism Ltd said the windows in the tower were securely locked and denied that the trio were able to open them easily.

A full internal inquiry is reportedly underway with Lancashire Police involved.

LMSD, however, said the “windows were far from secure.”

The group added that: “safety and meticulous planning sit at the absolute core of everything we do.”



A Blackpool Tourism Ltd spokesperson told the BBC: “On Sunday morning, three individuals posed as paying visitors to the top of The Blackpool Tower before parachuting onto a nearby building and the promenade.

“While the footage may give the impression that they were able to open a window with ease, this was not the case.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“All windows at the top of the tower are securely locked. However, the individuals brought a specialist tool which enabled them to discreetly unlock one of the windows. This followed failed attempts at several other windows.”

The Sun has contacted Lancashire Police for comment.

News.title: Twisted dad jailed for life after rape and murder of son’s friend, 8, during sleepover while his child slept feet away
News.content:
BEAST CAGED Twisted dad jailed for life after rape and murder of son’s friend, 8, during sleepover while his child slept feet away

A SICK dad who raped and murdered his eight-year-old son’s friend during a sleepover has been jailed for life.

Daniel Jamneck, eight, was attacked while staying at his friend’s home in Peerless Park North, a residential suburb of Cape Town in South Africa.



The youngster was sleeping on a double bed beside the 49-year-old father, while the man’s own son slept just feet away on a bunk bed.

The father was handed two life sentences at Western Cape High Court on Wednesday.



Despite pleading his innocence, the twisted criminal was convicted of the rape and murder of the young boy.

Prosecutors presented harrowing forensic evidence including bite marks, abrasions, adult pubic hair and nail marks on Daniel’s neck.



The father cannot be named to protect the identity of his son who was the key witness during the trial.

Handing down the sentence, acting Judge Sue Smith said the man had shown “no remorse for his actions at any stage”.

He was also sentenced to 10 years in prison for the rape of a woman in 2005 and eight years for the sexual assault of Daniel, with all sentences ordered to run concurrently.

The court heard the father was a repeat sex offender who had entered into a plea agreement after the 2005 rape conviction.



He was then placed under a three-year correctional supervision programme, from which he later absconded.

The judge ordered that his details be added to South Africa’s National Register for Sex Offenders.

He has also been permanently banned from working with children and prohibited from possessing a firearm.



Daniel’s mother Maria Jamneck and Caryn Brown, the survivor of the 2005 rape, were granted the right to make representations to the parole board should he ever become eligible for release.

Maria and Caryn held hands in solidarity as the sentence was handed down, as the accused was seen weeping in the dock.

Speaking outside court after the sentencing, Maria said: “Nothing will ever bring back my son, so that feeling of grief, it lives with you.

“So no sentence will ever be harsh enough.”

Maria described Daniel as her “absolute light”, saying he dreamed of becoming a vet and adored his younger sister.



It comes after a wicked uncle who kidnapped and murdered his three-year-old niece was jailed for life.

Yusuf Aydemir was found guilty of the deliberate murder of Leyla Aydemir after locking her in a cold storage unit before dumping her body beside a stream in rural Turkey.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The callous criminal protested his innocence right to the end, saying in his final statement: “I swear by oath that I have committed no crime.

“They have deemed this fate proper for me simply because I wept over her death.”

News.title: Slayed Brit’s husband tells of ‘relief’ at arrest of ‘love rival’ over stabbing after sleuths suspected his involvement
News.content:
‘HOW WRONG THEY WERE’ Slayed Brit’s husband tells of ‘relief’ at arrest of ‘love rival’ over stabbing after sleuths suspected his involvement

THE husband of a Brit mum who was knifed to death in France has blasted sleuths who thought he was a suspect following the arrest of a 70-year-old woman.

Karen Carter, 65, was killed last April in the sleepy village of Tremolat – with her murder left shrouded in mystery until a breakthrough this month.



Cops said the tragic mum-of-four was stabbed eight times in the vicious assault – with one slash “penetrating the aorta”.

It was revealed yesterday that a 70-year-old woman has now been arrested and charged in connection with Karen’s death.



Following the announcement, Karen’s estranged husband Alan has hit out at those who accused him of being involved in her murder.

The couple were going through a divorce at the time of Karen’s death on April 25, 2025.



Alan, who currently lives in South Africa, told The Times: “I am aware that there were some people who suspected I was involved in Karen’s death, which exacerbated the sense of shock and bereavement, and I hope this goes some way to showing how wrong they were.

“Obviously we are relieved that there’s been some progress in the case after more than a year, even though it is not a trial or conviction.



“We are grateful to the police who have put in a huge effort to get to this point.”

He also told the Daily Mail: “We are relieved that, after more than a year, the investigation has progressed to the formal investigation of an individual believed to be responsible for the death of our beloved wife, mother, sister, and friend, Karen.”

Alan added: “We remain united in our hope that the full truth will come to light, and that justice will ultimately be served for Karen.”



And he told The Telegraph that he hoped “the full truth will come to light” in the wake of the new arrest.

Karen, 65, was stabbed to death in what cops described as a “frenzied attack” in the driveway of her own home.

Detectives and prosecutors believe the killer lulled the Brit expat into a false sense of security before launching the meticulously planned knife attack.

The charged suspect is yet to be formally identified by prosecutors but she is believed to have been neighbour Marie-Laure Autefort.

Prosecutors revealed the prime suspect was originally taken into custody for two days in 2025 as part of preliminary inquiries.



The woman detained at the time was named as Autefort – who was also involved in an alleged love feud with Karen and her partner.

At the time of her death, Karen had been on the verge of divorcing Alan.

But she had also been seeing Jean-François Guerrier, a 75-year-old retired executive who lived close to her French property.

This was believed to have upset Autefort, who was allegedly “madly in love” with Guerrier.

Sources close to the initial investigations have now claimed that the woman’s alibi appeared solid at first which led to her being released.



But as cops continued to look into her story they found “significant holes”.

An investigating source said: “Her alibi was centered on helping to look after other people in Trémolat, and it appeared very credible.

“She had spent much of her adult life as a care worker, was highly respected in the community, and has no criminal record.

“Beyond this, she did not appear to have the physical strength to carry out such a violent attack, and so was initially released.”

But, on July 2 this year – 15 months after the horror slaying – the suspect was finally charged with premeditated murder.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The investigating source added: “The inconsistencies were exposed after her story was checked out by police, and this took a long time.”

Jacques-Édouard Andrault, the state prosecutor in nearby Périgueux, said the suspect remains in custody and that she faces a possible life sentence.

News.title: Military helicopter crashes leaving at least one dead after ‘Venom’ chopper carrying five troops goes down in Czechia
News.content:
CHOPPER DOWN Military helicopter crashes leaving at least one dead after ‘Venom’ chopper carrying five troops goes down in Czechia

A MILITARY helicopter has crashed in Czechia leaving one soldier dead and another four injured.

The Czech military confirmed the tragedy after the US-built “Venom” chopper went down at an airbase around 125 miles southeast of Prague on Thursday afternoon.



Five troops were on board when the aircraft crashed at the 22nd helicopter base in Namest nad Oslavou.

The military said one soldier had died and four others were hurt.



In a statement, it said: “Our absolute priority now is to provide all possible care and support to the injured soldiers and their loved ones.

“We are also in contact with the family of the deceased serviceman, to whom we are providing all necessary assistance.”



It has now grounded its entire fleet of 12 American-made helicopters – eight Venoms and four AH-1Z Vipers – while the cause of the crash is investigated.

Following the tragic incident, the surviving troops were rushed to hospitals in Brno and Jihlava by land and air, a regional emergency services spokesman confirmed.



Czechia Defence Minister Jaromir Zuna called it “an immense tragedy that affects us all deeply” and confirmed a probe is under way.

The Czech army only recently started flying the Venoms, after signing a deal with the US in 2019.

American instructors had been training Czech crews up until last year.

The choppers are being brought in to replace the country’s ageing fleet of Soviet-designed Mi-class helicopters.

Czechia is also in line for eight more of the helicopters, due to arrive in 2027 and 2028, as part of a deal linked to military aid sent to Ukraine.



The crash comes just months after two of the country’s Venom choppers were deployed on their first foreign mission, guarding Polish airspace against Russian drone incursions as part of Nato‘s eastern flank.

Those aircraft, along with their crews and technicians, remain stationed in eastern Poland near the border with Belarus.

News.title: Andy Burnham backs a good night out, saying pubs and clubs are 'beating heart of Britain'
News.content:
Musicians and nightclub promoters are already dancing to Andy Burnham’s tune, after the new Prime Minister announced a 20% cut to business rates for pubs, clubs and music venues. Speaking exclusively to the Mirror, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said: "I'll be honest, I grew up on nights out in Manchester, from the Haçienda to the little rooms where the next big act cuts its teeth.

"Those places gave people like me somewhere to belong, and I've watched too many go dark. For too long governments have stood by while they've been boarded up and handed to developers one by one. Not anymore.

"From April we're cutting business rates for nearly 32,000 pubs, clubs and live music venues, real money back in their tills. These places are the beating heart of our communities. We're bringing hope back to every high street. Get this right and there's good growth, and a night out worth having, in every town in Britain."

View 7 Images The Hacienda main dancefloor, Manchester 1989 (Image: Avalon via Getty Images)

‌



While he was still Mayor of Manchester, he also backed calls to cut the VAT rate for hospitality businesses from 20% down to 10% - although this has not yet been announced as Government policy.

And with TicketSource reporting that 48% of live music and entertainment venues launched in 2025 have already closed, any financial relief can’t come soon enough. Rapper Tinie Tempah, whose music has provided the soundtrack to numerous nights out, thanks nightclubs for launching his career. He says: “Venues are closing at an alarming rate. As an artist, they’re where I earned my stripes.”

One in four late night venues have closed since 2020, with a further 4% decline into 2026, according to the latest Night Time Economy Market Monitor. Legendary LGBTQ+ bar Circa, which opens until 1am in London's Soho, recently announced it is closing after 15 years. While the closure of Popworld and Ark made a big dent to Manchester’s Deansgate Locks, which was once one of the most thriving places in the city.

And the same pattern of closures is being repeated nationwide. Tinie Tempah, who found fame with Pass Out in 2010, and recently performed at Rounday Festival in Leeds, has returned to music after an eight year hiatus and is fighting to keep nightclubs open.

‌



View 7 Images Tinie Tempah performs during Roundhay Festival (Image: Redferns)

He says: “My music works incredibly well in a nightlife setting. The reason I'm still here to this day is because of my slog around the UK, playing all of the little grassroots venues from when I was a lad aged 16, building that connection with audiences. I played all sorts and went through the highs and lows of a sold-out venue to 12 people being there, a stiff crowd.”

Gigging at nightclubs was once the way that artists found a fan base. Tinie says: “Being able to do a gig every weekend, for an independent artist, was definitely like a game-changer. If we're on the verge of losing this as a culture, what does that mean for the next generation of artists?”

Berlin’s techno scene was officially added to the German UNESCO list of Intangible Cultural Heritage in March 2024, according to Tinie. He says: “A protective label was placed over the techno scene and some of the more significant venues in Berlin. Why are we not trying to do that in the UK?

‌



View 7 Images Clubbers enjoy the closing party at Turnmills, a legendary club that closed its doors in 2008 (Image: Universal Images Group via Getty Images)

“We've birthed so many exciting genres from this tiny island, partly down to these grassroots music venues that have gone on to resonate and influence people all over the world. Historic venues are being given over to property developers - just look at the Manchester Hacienda. Why are we allowing this to happen?”

The star argues that hitting the dance floor is good for the body and the soul. He says: “It’s good for you physically, and dancing releases endorphins, serotonin.”

Nightclubs are also a good place to mix and make friends, says Tinie. He adds: “Post-pandemic we got into a mindset of staying away from each other. But connecting with someone, regardless of their race, age, background, sexual orientation, over a song, is so powerful.

‌



“It was great what Andy Burnham did in Manchester, now the Government does need to step in and do something about nightlife.”

View 7 Images Fatboy Slim, real name Norman Cook, performing at a sell-out gig at the 60-person capacity venue The Pipeline in Brighton (Image: Lee London Photography/PA Wire)

Another star, Norman Cook aka DJ Fatboy Slim, teamed up with charity Music Venue Properties and bought Brighton punk rock venue The Pipeline, which was facing closure. He says: “It now belongs to the community and I'm very proud to be part of that community. I played here two weeks ago and it was fabulous.”

British music promoter and entrepreneur Sacha Lord, who co-founded The Warehouse Project club night and Parklife festival in Manchester, was Greater Manchester’s Night Time Economy Adviser under Mayor Andy Burnham from 2018 to January 2025.

‌



He says: “Andy was once in Freight Island next door to The Warehouse Project and his kids wanted to come in. So he messaged me and I was like, ‘you've got to come as well, Andy.’ He told me, ‘no, it's not my thing, it's not my thing.’ Anyway, I took him on stage and he absolutely loved Chic with Nile Rodgers. Angela Rayner has been in too, and Bev Craig, who is set to be the new Mayor of Manchester. They all like a little boogie.”

View 7 Images Sacha Lord, king of the dancefloor, who founded Warehouse Project and Parklife (Image: Darren Robinson Photography)

Praising Mr Burnham for cutting the business rate, he says: “He absolutely gets it. He loves live music. He loves gigs. He's not one of these people who likes to stand in a sanitised corporate box. He's going to be a nightmare for Special Branch, because he will still want to sit in his seats at Everton. He won't want to sit in the Chairman's Lounge.

“A few weeks ago when James played at the Co-op Live, the venue heard he was coming via his office, and said, ‘oh, we'll give you a box.’ And it's like, ‘well, no, I want to be on the floor with everybody,’ and he took his son, Jimmy.”

‌



But Mr Lord says a VAT reduction must also come soon. He says: “The bottom line is that night clubs have been absolutely crushed. No one's making any money at the moment, so that VAT reduction would make a big difference.”

View 7 Images Stu Margetts (right), one half of DJ duo ARKO // STU and co-founder of Ibiza Revival Events (Image: MatthewK Photography)

Marc Carter, founder of clubbing institution Ultravegas, agrees, saying: “The cost of venues, artists, security, production, insurance and marketing has increased enormously. That makes every event a financial risk and leaves promoters working incredibly hard right up until the doors open.

“The cost-of-living crisis has clearly affected people too. The saddest part is that when clubs and events disappear, we lose far more than businesses. Nightlife creates friendships, relationships, memories and communities. It gives people somewhere to escape the pressures of everyday life and express themselves. It also gives emerging DJs, artists, performers and promoters somewhere to learn their craft.”

‌



Stu Margetts, one half of DJ duo ARKO // STU and co-founder of Ibiza Revival Events adds: “The industry needs meaningful government support. Local authorities also need to recognise nightlife as an important part of our culture. My message to Andy Burnham would be, ‘take the approach you championed in Manchester onto the national stage.’”

News.title: Daughter blasts 'lowest of the low' who stole part of her parents' gravestone
News.content:
Daughter blasts 'lowest of the low' who stole part of her parents' gravestone

Lynne Brown had been visiting her parents' grave at Lambhill Cemetery in Glasgow on what would have been her mum's 85th birthday when she found pieces of granite had been stolen from the site

View 2 Images Lynne Brown was left heartbroken after finding parts of her parents' grave had been stolen (Image: Newsquest / SWNS)

A daughter has been left heartbroken after a part of her parents' gravestone was stolen for granite which can be sold on the black market.

‌



Lynne Brown was visiting her parents at Lambhill Cemetery in Glasgow on what would have been her mum's 85th birthday. Lynne was horrified to see three large pieces of granite kerbing, which had been cemented to the ground around the grave were gone.

‌



Lynne, 48, said she believes these were "stolen" and that it would not have been a "quick job" as two of the three pieces of granite measured 6ft long. People steal granite due to it being highly valuable, durable and easily reproposed. It also commands a high resale price on the black market.

‌



Lynne, from Glasgow, said: “When I went up and saw what had happened, there was a real mixture of emotions. It went from really upset with all these things going through my head, like ‘Who would do this? Why have they done it? Why this grave?’ to complete anger.

“I know these are desperate times for people, but that really is the lowest of the low to do that to somebody’s resting place. They would have had to have been dug out because they were cemented in.

"After speaking to a couple of people, I reckon it would probably have taken a couple of hours to do that. Lambhill Cemetery is not super busy, but there are always passing cars or people out with dogs. There had to have been people passing, I’m confident of that.

‌



“Understandably, they might have just assumed it was somebody there doing work on the grave. The holes have been covered with the gravel that was on top of the grave, and it’s very neatly dug out, which makes me feel like it’s been somebody who knew what they’re doing.”

View 2 Images Lynne said she felt a real mix of emotions (Image: Newsquest / SWNS)

After Lynne discovered the kerbing was missing, she said she got in touch with staff at the cemetery and reported it to Police Scotland. Officers said they received a report of theft from the cemetery and that enquiries were ongoing.

‌



A Police Scotland spokesperson said: "On Friday, June 26, 2026, we received a report of a theft from a cemetery in Glasgow. Enquiries are ongoing."

Lynne said that she just wants to know what happened and to have the granite returned, as it will cost more than £1700 to replace. She added: “I contacted someone at the council who did come back to me with an apology for what had happened and assured me that they would investigate, but I’ve not heard anything else from them.

“I also called 101 and was sent a link to send over photographs of before and after, but I’ve not heard anything else from the police. I feel kind of in limbo just now.

‌



"I feel quite torn because we would do anything for my parents, but I feel like if we go ahead and get the money together to get this done [have the granite replaced], is it going to be stolen again? That’s a worry, and I suppose the other thing is I just want a bit of justice here. I want to understand what has happened and who has taken this.

“I just feel like there must be somebody out there who will know something to help me get to the bottom of this and get the kerbing back.” Lynne stated that she and her brothers had the grave renewed in 2017 after their mum, Anne, passed away from Alzheimer’s disease.

Her dad, Denis, had sadly died 17 years earlier. Lynne added: “I was only 22 when my dad passed away. It was a really tough time and completely unexpected.

‌



“We didn’t have much money, and a friend of the family kindly offered to pay for the headstone. When my mum passed away 17 years later, after a six-year battle with Alzheimer’s disease, my brothers and I got a different headstone.

“The stone mason had said to us, ‘Oh, this particular headstone is one of a kind’, and we thought, that’s it. A few weeks later, when they fitted the kerbing, I remember feeling so emotional. It felt like we had done them justice.

“We take a lot of pride in it.” A Glasgow City Council spokesperson said: “We are aware of this issue and we are saddened to learn of the upset experienced by Ms Brown.

Article continues below

"Our staff have spoken directly to her and assisted her as far as possible. Any theft should be reported to the police, and we will support fully any investigation into this incident."

News.title: UK weather maps show heatwave reaching 37C in seven counties within six days
News.content:
UK weather maps show heatwave reaching 37C in seven counties within six days

Temperatures could surge to 37C in the UK next week as weather models suggest another heatwave is on the cards - Met Office forecasters say 'very hot' conditions may return soon

View 3 Images Anomaly maps show above-average temperatures are on the cards next week (Image: WXCHARTS)

Weather forecasting models suggest temperatures could rise as high as 37C next week.

‌



The Met Office says temperatures are expected to be above average as July ends and August begins, and could potentially turn “very hot” again. Another scorching spell would constitute the UK’s fourth heatwave of 2026.

‌



The GFS weather model shows temperatures rising to 33C in eastern and southern areas on Tuesday, with 30-32C possible quite widely across England and Wales. Areas as far north as Yorkshire could hit 32C.

‌



Temperatures could then reach 37C on Wednesday, the data suggests, with the warmest conditions coming in western and southern England. The maps show sizzling 36C highs are possible from London right up to Yorkshire.

View 3 Images Maximum possible temperatures (C) at 6pm on July 28 (Image: WXCHARTS)

UK weather maps show 39C heatwave and hottest day of year as 10 counties hit 38C READ MORE :

Met Office names 7 areas facing wet weather this week as 15mm of rain forecast READ MORE :

Anomaly maps show the UK - particularly England and Wales - shaded in areas of deep red and black. This indicates where conditions will rise well above the seasonal average.

‌



GFS model maps show temperatures hitting 37C in seven counties. They are all in England.

UK counties facing 37C next week

Staffordshire

Shropshire

Worcestershire

Gloucestershire

Warwickshire

Oxfordshire

Berkshire

View 3 Images Maximum possible temperatures (C) at 6pm on July 29 (Image: WXCHARTS)

‌



Met Office weather forecast

The Met Office says conditions could turn “very warm” again by the start of next month. There is also a risk of showers in places.

The Met Office forecast for July 27 to August 5 states: “A changeable period is likely overall, with many areas likely to see a mixture of bright or sunny spells and some rain at times. Northwestern areas are more likely to see the focus of rainfall, but southeastern areas should also see some showers.

“Confidence becomes lower into the start of August, but there are hints that high pressure could return for a time, which would mean dry conditions resuming, especially in the south. Winds will be mostly light or moderate, but occasionally fresh or strong around some coasts, mainly in the north and west.

Article continues below

“Temperatures will be near or above normal, warmest in the south, and perhaps becoming very warm again by the start of August.”

News.title: Andy Burnham tells SNP leader second Scottish independence referendum is 'off limits'
News.content:
Andy Burnham tells SNP leader second Scottish independence referendum is 'off limits'

In his first meeting with John Swinney since becoming PM, Mr Burnham insisted the focus must be on delivering growth and helping families with the cost of living

View 2 Images The pair met in Glasgow on Thursday (Image: Getty Images)

Andy Burnham has told the First Minister of Scotland another independence referendum is “off limits”.

‌



In his first meeting with John Swinney since becoming PM, Mr Burnham insisted the focus must be on delivering growth and helping families with the cost of living.

‌



The Makerfield MP met with the SNP leader in Glasgow ahead of the Commonwealth Games, and offered to work more closely together on devolution to help improve the lives of Scots.

‌



As well as the Scottish leader, Mr Burnham also met with Wales' First Minister Rhun ap Iorwerth during the visit.

Should Andy Burnham introduce a wealth tax? Take our poll and have your say READ MORE :

View 2 Images Andy Burnham also met with Wales' First Minister Rhun ap Iorwerth (Image: Getty Images)

Speaking after the meeting, a Downing Street spokesperson said: "The Prime Minister began by congratulating the First Minister and the city of Glasgow for hosting the Commonwealth Games, especially at short notice, and said he was looking forward to watching the opening ceremony later that evening.

‌



"The conversation then turned to how the Prime Minister and First Minister can work more closely together to build a model of devolution to improve people's lives across Scotland.

“The Prime Minister reiterated his belief that deeper devolution could make a real difference in helping communities across the UK to re-industrialise - creating jobs, transforming high streets and reviving local economies - and welcomed the First Minister's willingness to engage with that process.

"The Prime Minister stated up front that another referendum on independence was off limits because it would take our focus away from growing the economy and helping families with the cost of living.

‌



"More broadly, the Prime Minister said this was a moment for both sides to work together in a constructive relationship. He looked forward to regular engagement with the First Minister in the months ahead."

Consecutive PM’s have repeatedly refused to grant another vote on independence, and the UK Government's position is that the issue is settled after the 2014 referendum.

Mr Burnham has vowed to deliver growth in every postcode, empower communities, and restore hope across the UK.

Article continues below

The Scottish Government issued their own statement after the meeting, saying the First Minister would continue to argue for independence, citing the May elections and recent vote in Scottish parliament.

They also claimed the former Greater Manchester Mayor made a commitment “not to bypass the Scottish Parliament and Scottish Government in further devolution of powers”.

News.title: Huge blaze near Alexandra Palace as dozens of firefighters rush to tackle flames
News.content:
Huge blaze near Alexandra Palace as dozens of firefighters rush to tackle flames

People in London have been urged to avoid the area with an investigation under way into the cause of the blaze

View Image London Fire Brigade crews rushed to the scene (stock image) (Image: PA)

Around 40 firefighters have tackled a massive blaze near Alexandra Palace in north London.

‌



The incident was first reported at around 12.40pm today as six fire engines were sent to the scene of the grass fire in Wood Green. London Fire Brigade (LFB) said around half an acre of compost and garden waste was involved in the blaze but no one was injured.

‌



Road closures remained in place throughout the afternoon in the area surrounding the popular music venue. While the fire was under control by 3pm, firefighters remained at the scene to damp down hot spots, and people have been urged to continue avoiding the area.

‌



The cause of the fire is under investigation. A spokesperson for LFB said: "During periods of dry and sustained extreme heat, the chance of wildfires spreading rapidly is high. The Brigade is ready and prepared to respond to all types of incidents, but we urge everyone to play their part to prevent incidents, such as wildfires, which can be time-consuming to resolve and have devastating impacts on livelihoods, occurring in the first place.

Iran issues horror threat to attack UK and chilling warning to Royal Family READ MORE :

"If you’re planning to enjoy the weather over the coming days either in a park or other open spaces, please don’t take a disposable BBQ with you. They pose a significant fire risk as the heat can be retained for many hours, even after a barbecue has been put out.

‌



"It’s also important to make sure that smoking materials are discarded of properly and either dispose of your rubbish in the appropriate bins or take it home with you if none are available. For those having a BBQ at home, avoid doing so on a balcony and ensure your BBQ is away from flammable materials like fences and sheds.

"You should also avoid setting up your BBQ on any decking you may have in your garden." The warning comes as drought has been declared in North Wales and the Upper Severn following prolonged dry conditions, heatwaves, wildfires and dwindling rivers, Natural Resources Wales (NRW) said.

The announcement was made due to "continued lack of significant rainfall and sustained high temperatures, which are increasing pressures on rivers, wildlife and habitats". This is the first part of the UK where drought has been declared this year.

Article continues below

Various parts of England remain under prolonged dry weather status as the country only received 3 per cent of its average rainfall so far this month. Around 23 million customers are facing hosepipe bans as a result, with restrictions potentially staying in place all summer.

Wildfires have also been burning around the UK, with a massive one in the Cairngorms in Scotland in recent days. Yellow heat health alerts have been issued by UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) for six regions in England.

These will come into place tomorrow at 9am and remain until 9am on Sunday. The areas affected are East Midlands, West Midlands, East of England, London, South East and South West.

News.title: Thrillseekers soar over Swiss Alps on huge mountain swing 2,000 metres above sea level
News.content:
Thrillseekers soar over Swiss Alps on huge mountain swing 2,000 metres above sea level

A giant mountain swing is sending visitors soaring more than 2,000 metres above the Swiss Alps as ski resorts look for new ways to attract visitors beyond the winter season

View 3 Images The Balanc'Air swing opened earlier this month (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Thrill-seekers can now soar over the Swiss Alps on a giant mountain swing that launches riders over the edge of a cliff.

‌



Visitors to the Villars ski resort can now brave the BalancAIR swing, a 12-metre-high attraction perched 2,110 metres above sea level that sends up to three people at a time soaring out above a dramatic Alpine drop. Riders are strapped into saddle-style seats fixed to a structure resembling an Alpine Ibex before being hauled backwards to a 90-degree angle and released high above the valley below.

‌



Alexandra Henchoz, 37, admitted she was nervous before testing the attraction with her husband and 10-year-old daughter. She said she: “I had a bit of a pit in [her] stomach" before she was strapped in to the harness.

‌



View 3 Images One rider said the ride was so scary, he didn't even scream (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

UK ranks worst in Europe for mental health, says AXA report READ MORE :

West Mersea beach tragedy as woman and girl die despite heroic actions of local teens READ MORE :

“But once it is happening, it is just incredible. You feel like a bird flying," Alexandra added.

The swing, which opened earlier this month, forms part of the resort’s efforts to attract more visitors outside the traditional ski season as Alpine destinations adapt to the effects of climate change. Martin Deburaux, head of the Villars-Gryons-Diableret ski area, said: “We are really trying to diversify our offering.”

‌



The 12-metre swing “provides us with a source of attraction that can function independently of snow conditions”, he said. Although the resort has enjoyed record winter visitor numbers over the past two seasons, Martin said warmer conditions meant planning for the future was essential.

View 3 Images The Balanc'Air swing sits 2,110 meters above sea level (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

He added: “But we know we are facing climate change. We are looking for substitutes to conserve jobs, the dynamism and the tourist economy built up around our ski lift facilities.”

Article continues below

The resort currently welcomes more than 700,000 visitors during winter but around 100,000 over the summer, now busses hope the new attraction will help draw more visitors outside the ski season in a bid to boost off-season tourism.

Among those giving it a go was Marc Truffer, 70, who admitted the experience left him both frightened and amazed. He said: "It was so scary… I didn’t even scream.

“It took my breath away going down, but then the view was magnificent.”

News.title: Extreme heat killing off camels as temperatures soar past 50C in deserts
News.content:
Extreme heat killing off camels as temperatures soar past 50C in deserts

Camels are struggling in sweltering temperatures as regions across Africa and the Middle East soar past 50C and take a massive toll on the famously hardy animals

View 3 Images Camels are known for their hardy nature (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

The extreme heat is killing off famously hardy camels as deserts bake in rising temperatures.

‌



Experts have been alarmed as temperatures surge beyond 50 degrees in Africa and the Middle East, with the vital animals known for their survivability in hot conditions now feeling the heat. Scientists have observed camels facing dehydration, fatigue and disease prevalence due to the extreme heat in the regions.

‌



Farmers in northern Africa and the Horn of Africa rely on the animals to transport salt and other items across the desert. They switched over from cattle to camels due to their resilience to the heat and capability to survive drought conditions.

‌



View 3 Images Camels are struggling in the heat (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

Europe weather chaos as Spain faces 49C heatwave and 'firenado' seen in France READ MORE :

Cockroach infestations boom across UK thanks to summer heatwaves as locations most at risk revealed READ MORE :

Camel herder Ali Umer, living in north-eastern Ethiopia, said he could see many of his 500 camels suffering in the heat. "They get blisters on their feet, their eyes become watery and the hot sand burns their skin and eats up their hair when they are sitting," he told The BBC.

‌



"They get blisters on their feet, their eyes become watery and the hot sand burns their skin and eats up their hair when they are sitting," said the 40-year-old who owns around 500 camels. Within the past one month I have lost eight camel calves because of the extreme heat, it has become much more intense and difficult."

View 3 Images Camels are vital for many farmers in northern Africa (Image: Getty Images)

Experts said camels are able to live relatively comfortably in conditions up to around 40C and are able to allow their bodies to regulate temperatures by a few degrees. Their coat allows them to stave off the worst of the sun and their ability to avoid sweating too much had played a vital part in their ability to survive in tough conditions.

Article continues below

UN Food and Agriculture scientist Dr Mohammed Bengoumi added: "But camels can also experience heat stress when temperatures rise beyond their comfort range. In many parts of the Sahara, summer temperatures now frequently exceed 50C, increasing the risk of severe heat stress, particularly when accompanied by reduced vegetation cover, water scarcity, and limited access to shade."

Many camel herders in Ethiopia have moved or are moving the animals from the northern part of the country to the south where there is more water and vegetation. Bengoumi stressed the move was not temporary and that it could be a permanent shift for the herders due to drought and extreme heat.

News.title: Haigh, Rayner and Powell likely to regularly work from No 10 North
News.content:
Senior ministers and aides close to Andy Burnham are expecting to regularly work from No 10 North, which the prime minister has said will be the "dominant driver of the UK's economy".

Education Secretary Lucy Powell, Housing Secretary Angela Rayner, and Louise Haigh, who is overseeing No 10 North in her role as Chancellor of the Duchy of Lancaster, are planning to work there.

The new branch of Downing Street is currently operating from Heron House in Manchester city centre, whilst a brownfield site is redeveloped.

A blueprint for No 10 North produced by the think tank Re:State recommends a workforce of as many as 300 staff within 18 months.

Burnham aims to base himself at No 10 North at least one day a week and is expected to start work there for the first time in coming days.

He will be joined by his closest adviser, Kevin Lee, the director of his mayoral office, who will move to No 10 North after next week's Greater Manchester mayoral election.

Lee is one of at least seven Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) employees, including four senior managers, to have been recruited by Burnham and are already moving into No 10 North.

Chief executive Caroline Simpson is moving to become Downing Street deputy chief of staff based at No 10 North, Directors John Wrathmell and Claire Norman will also move across.

Some London-based civil servants have voiced concerns about the uncertainty surrounding the plans, with most details expected to be announced in the weeks ahead.

In the weeks before Burnham became prime minister, the BBC has been told that senior officials were summoned to calls informing them that a significant programme to move staff out of London was being developed.

News.title: Rayner rules out repaying severance cash after making cabinet return
News.content:
A lump sum, equivalent of 25% of the annual ministerial salary, is payable when a minister stops holding office. Departing ministers who are aged over 65 or are reappointed within three weeks do not qualify.

The 2025/26 accounts, external for the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government record the severance payment for Rayner.

In her first interview since returning to government, Rayner was pressed on whether she would return the money.

She told Matt Chorley on BBC Radio 5 Live: "No, my severance payment was given to me at the time, I had worked in government for a period of time and then I came out of government for just under a year."

She added: "I will be delivering in government again."

Rayner earlier said her criticism of the Conservatives over severance payments came at a time when there was a "revolving door" which saw ministers return to government "after 40-odd days".

The Conservatives earlier this week said Rayner had "quit in disgrace and took a Â£17k payout" last year.

The party added: "Now she's got her old job back, will she return the cash? Or is it one rule for Labour, and another for everyone else?"

Rayner's departure last September came after the prime minister's ethics adviser, Sir Laurie Magnus, said she had "acted with integrity" but concluded that she had breached the ministerial code.

Sir Laurie said she did get legal advice when buying the property, but failed to seek further expert tax advice as recommended.

In May, Rayner resolved her tax affairs with HMRC following an investigation, settling Â£40,000 in unpaid stamp duty.

The MP for Ashton-under-Lyne said she had been "exonerated" of the accusation that she had "deliberately sought to avoid tax".

Rayner told Matt Chorley: "The situation I went through last year was really difficult, it was difficult for my family, but I felt I'd let people down and I never want to let people down, I want to fight for them."

Rayner also said she has "unfinished business" in government, including on building council houses and supporting local government.

Burnham has said he wants to deliver "the biggest council house building programme since the post-war period".

Asked for details to explain what this will look like, Rayner said she would not provide an "exact figure" or provide a date for when she considers the post-war period to have ended.

She said: "We want to aspire to get as far as possible and what we've done as a government is put more investment in that, the Â£39bn for social and affordable housing grant funding that we want to get out the door."

News.title: Wildfires and record dry conditions trigger drought in parts of Wales
News.content:
"We've had really dry weather but also it's been really hot - and those things combined if you're a livestock farmer means excessive pressure on livestock," said Abi Reader, president of NFU Cymru.

"You have to make sure they have enough water and shade, and we are getting farms with springs and streams drying up," she told BBC Walescast.

"If you're an arable farmer the heat and dry weather have also forced a lot of the crops to come to ripening a lot earlier than they normally would.

"It's unprecedented early harvesting this year and farmers are going to see lower crop yields."

Welsh Water emphasised that NRW's drought declarations were different to its own announcements.

The company has already brought in a hospipe ban for 33,000 properties in west Wales.

"NRW's drought status reflects environmental conditions, including factors such as rainfall, river flows and groundwater levels," a spokesperson said.

"By contrast, Welsh Water's Temporary Use Ban is an operational measure based on local water demand and our ability to replenish service reservoirs with drinking water at the same rate, or faster, than customers are using water.

"It is driven by the capacity of the local treatment works and distribution network to keep up with sustained demand.

"This means different parts of Wales can experience different operational pressures, even if they are not in the same environmental drought category declared by NRW."

Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability, Llyr Gruffydd, said: "This is an environmental drought classification. It's about the state of water levels in our rivers.

"It does not speak to public water supplies which I can assure people are there, there is sufficient supplies but we would of course urge people to be careful and diligent in their use of water so that that can be protected."

News.title: Gary Lineker among millionaires asking Andy Burnham to tax them more
News.content:
Millionaires including former footballer Gary Lineker and music producer Brian Eno have written to new prime minister Andy Burnham asking to be taxed more.

In an open letter, 120 well-off Britons told Burnham: "We can afford it. We're not talking about higher taxes on those who get up and go to work for their income every day, but on the very richest whose income is derived from the wealth they hold."

Organised by Patriotic Millionaires, the letter said it would lead to a more equal society, and urged a "devolution of wealth and power from the very richest".

People can already give money or stocks voluntarily to the Treasury using a donation facility.

Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said Lineker is "very welcome to pay more tax he can write a cheque to the Treasury, no one is stopping him."

Patriotic Millionaires support a 2% tax on wealth over Â£10m.

"Millionaires are a patriotic bunch," the letter states. "We love this country and we want it to succeed.

"But success requires investment and a primary source of untouched capital investment is sitting with us, in untaxed potential."

Other signatories include Richard Curtis, who wrote the film Notting Hill, and Ian Gregg, the former managing director of Greggs and son of the bakery chain's founder. Scottish crime writer Val McDermid and former financial trader-turned-equality campaigner Gary Stevenson also signed the letter.

Chief Secretary to the Treasury Emma Reynolds said she would welcome UK millionaires increasing the amount of tax they pay but said any major changes would be announced during a Budget.

"I welcome the fact that people of good means are saying that they want to pay more. They can pay more," she said and pointed to the Treasury's donation link.

The renewed call for higher tax on the wealthy follows a similar campaign in previous years.

Burnham did not rule out a wealth tax when asked about it by Lineker - formerly the BBC's highest paid presenter - a few days before he became prime minister.

He suggested he may have "to ask for a little more" tax at some point.

Lineker was paid around Â£1.3m a year before he left the BBC. He is worth a reported Â£30m.

In 2023, Lineker won his appeal against HMRC over a Â£4.9m tax bill, after the UK tax authority pursued him over taxes on income from both the BBC and BT Sport, from 2013 to 2014, and 2017 to 2018.

The latest call from Patriotic Millionaires said there is a "need to embrace a new kind of devolution of wealth and power, from the very richest in order to reinvest back into our greatest asset in every region".

It added that in its own poll, the majority of millionaires wanted a higher tax on themselves.

"There are a few people left with outdated economic thinking and few others desperate to hold onto every penny they can... Those that can't see past the end of their own self interest have no place in designing a Britain for the future," the letter said.

Musician Brian Eno told BBC Radio Lincolnshire the tax system was "very generous to rich people".

"If you're wealthy you don't pay very much tax but hire a clever bunch of accountants who somehow get you off that," he said.

He also dismissed the idea that lots of millionaires would leave the UK if they were taxed too much.

News.title: Pubs cheer business rates relief while other firms 'left out in the cold'
News.content:
Keith Bott, who runs the Titanic Brewery and nine pubs across the Midlands, said the government was "finally recognising the plight of the hospitality industry and trying to help".

He said pubs had been hit by a mix of employer National Insurance increases, the rising minimum wage, high inflation and the climbing cost of living.

Meanwhile, the sector is "heavily taxed", with around 35-40% of turnover going to the Treasury, he added.

"What I really liked in this announcement is they are recognising we need to look at a fairer tax system so we can all contribute to society," Bott told the BBC. He said online retailers that operate out of warehouses pay a "ridiculously low" amount of business rates in comparison, and "we need to make the system fair".

And Bott urged the government to go further in supporting the industry, cutting the duty on draft beer to target drinks sold in pubs.

News.title: Police failed to check Manchester synagogue attacker's phones despite arresting him twice
News.content:
A police chief has apologised after admitting phones were twice seized from the Manchester synagogue attacker months before the car and knife assault but they were not examined.

Jihad Al-Shamie, 35, was on bail for an alleged rape when he carried out the attack on Heaton Park Synagogue in Crumpsall on 2 October 2025, in which two Jewish men were killed.

His devices, which contained evidence of his extreme views, were seized after he was arrested in February and September but not analysed.

Greater Manchester Police Chief Constable Sir Stephen Watson said he was "deeply sorry", conceding that "the information contained within these devices would have inspired further investigative action".

Sir Stephen said the end of legal proceedings against Mohammad Bashir, who has been jailed for life with a minimum term of 17 years for plotting a separate attack with Al-Shamie, meant rules around sharing information about a live criminal case had been lifted.

He said: "In conducting an internal review, it became apparent that GMP had seized Al-Shamie's mobile devices, at the point of each arrest.

"The significance of the data contents of these devices was substantial in respect of evidencing an extremist mindset.

"I am disappointed at the prospect of adding to the distress of all of those affected by the terrible events last October.

"For this, I am deeply sorry."

News.title: Johnson-Thompson and Asher-Smith out of Commonwealths
News.content:
Olympic silver medallist Katarina Johnson-Thompson has pulled out of the Commonwealth Games because of injury.

Dina Asher-Smith and 400m Olympic silver medalist Matt Hudson-Smith, who were both set to run relays for Team England in Glasgow, have also been replaced, as has Asher-Smith's sprint team-mate Daryll Neita and 400m runner Amber Anning.

Johnson-Thompson, 33, was due to compete in her third Commonwealth Games heptathlon, having won gold on the Gold Coast in 2018 and at Birmingham in 2022.

But she said she has "not been able to get back to the level" needed to compete and will instead focus on being fit for the European Championships next month.

"Missing a championship is never easy, but I know it's the right decision," she said.

Johnson-Thompson has been replaced in England's squad by Niamh Emerson, who took bronze behind Johnson-Thompson in 2018.

The withdrawal of such high-profile names is a significant blow to the event on the day the opening ceremony takes place.

Renee Regis, Ebuka Nwokeji, Tara Simpson-Sullivan and Tom Keen have all been added to England's athletics squad in Glasgow. The track and field competition begins on Monday.

News.title: Airport drop off fees up by a third - here's how to avoid unexpected charges
News.content:
Drop-off fees at the UK's major airports have risen by a third on average since last summer, new analysis has found.

The RAC motoring group looked at the cost of pulling up to the closest point to terminals at the 20 busiest airports, 16 of which had put up their prices since last year.

London airport Gatwick topped the list by charging a "farewell fee" of Â£10 for 10 minutes, after lifting it by Â£3 from last year. Stansted also charges Â£10 but drivers are allowed 15 minutes at its "express set down" outside departures.

Airports UK, the trade body, said that free drop-offs were available and fees were part of airports' business models and climate change objectives.

The RAC said that the price of dropping people off in "kiss-and-fly" areas rose by an average of Â£1.70 to Â£7 compared to this time last year.

London City Airport, which only started making people pay this year, is the most expensive on a per-minute basis. Its Â£8 charge for five minutes works out at Â£1.60 per minute.

There have been increases in Northern Ireland too. At Belfast International Airport, it is now Â£5 for 10 minutes in the drop-off zone, up Â£2 on last year.

In contrast, none of the top 10 airports in the EU charge for drop-offs, according to RAC research.

News.title: Shapps blocked from standing again for the Conservatives
News.content:
Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch has told the BBC she leads "a brand new party full of new people" - after it emerged in the Spectator, external that the former cabinet minister and Tory party chairman Sir Grant Shapps has been rejected as a Conservative Party parliamentary candidate.

Sir Grant, who has declined to comment, served in nine ministerial roles in government as well as co-chairing the party.

In cabinet, he served as home secretary, defence secretary, transport secretary, business secretary, energy secretary and net zero secretary.

He was also a Foreign Office Minister, housing minister and international development minister, external.

He lost his Welwyn Hatfield seat to Labour's Andrew Lewin in 2024 by 3,799 votes after representing it since 2005.

But his application to stand again for the Conservatives at the next general election has been declined.

One party source told the BBC "it reflects badly on Kemi's temperament. North Korean purges don't work in British politics".

Badenoch told a news conference in central London: "We don't treat our former MPs or our candidates like tittle-tattle for Westminster gossip.

"What I will say is that we're going to be announcing candidates shortly, and you will see that this is a very different party from the one that was removed from government in 2024."

News.title: Love Island: All Stars winners Molly Smith and Tom Clare marry
News.content:
Sharing more from their marriage ceremony, Molly posted a photo to her Instagram story of her hand on top of Tom's.

The snap showed their wedding rings along with a bouquet of flowers, with the caption: "Husband and wife".

The couple first got together two years ago, when they met on season one of Love Island: All Stars.

All Stars is a spin-off of the hit dating show, which sees past contestants return for a second chance at finding love in the villa.

During the reality dating show, the pair beat Molly's ex-boyfriend Callum Jones and his partner at the time, Jessica Gale, who finished as runners-up.

Molly previously starred in series six in 2020 and left the show with Callum, who she was in a relationship with for three years before they split.

While Hyde United footballer Tom previously came third place on the second winter edition of Love Island in 2023 with former partner Samie Elishi.

Earlier this year, Tom and Molly took over hosting duties of the NearlyWeds podcast from radio presenters and reality stars Jamie Laing and Sophie Habboo.

Fellow Love Island stars were among those to congratulate the couple, including former winner Casey O'Gorman who described it as the "best day".

Sophie Piper, who came third on their All Star season, and TikTok star GK Barry also shared their support with the newly weds.

News.title: MI5 to pay damages for illegal surveillance of journalist's phone
News.content:
MI5 and the Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) have been ordered to pay Â£20,000 in damages to a journalist, after they illegally obtained his phone records.

Former BBC Journalist Vincent Kearney took a case at the Investigatory Powers Tribunal (IPT) in London.

It is believed to be the first time that MI5 has been directed to pay compensation to a journalist.

Kearney was the subject of secret operations aimed at discovering his confidential sources while he worked at the BBC in Belfast.

In a statement welcoming the judgement, Kearney said: "I am delighted the court has penalised those responsible for breaking the law.

"The fact it decided to award damages reflects the seriousness of the case.

"It is important that agencies charged with upholding the law know that they are not above the law and will be held to account."

The BBC, which brought the case alongside Kearney, said: "Today's findings are welcome, necessary and significant.

"We hope that their effect will be to protect journalists and their freedom to report and investigate stories into the future."

Kearney worked for BBC Northern Ireland for 18 years until 2019, when he joined RTÃ, where he is currently its northern editor.

There were multiple operations targeting him between 2006 and 2014, when he was a BBC correspondent covering policing and security issues.

Four of them were run by the PSNI, who also created a "profile" on him, which included car registrations and the names of his wife and mother-in-law.

He suspects it was for surveillance purposes.

News.title: Marathon runners compete on drifting sea ice at North Pole
News.content:
Twenty-three runners from seven countries took part in races at the Arctic's geographic North Pole, organisers have said, in an event they dubbed as the "world's coolest marathon".

The races took place on drifting sea ice at the geographic North Pole in the Arctic, with competitors arriving from Norway aboard the French polar vessel Le Commandant Charcot.

They disembarked the ship to run laps of a 1,055 metre loop on the ice below, wearing thermal gear and life vests as a safety requirement, while armed guards kept watch for polar bears around the perimeter.

Denmark's Rikke Dam won the women's title with a time of 6:54:02 and Wang Shengxian of China won the men's race in 3:52:22. Organisers said the course disappeared with the ice just hours after the races ended.

News.title: 'A 10-goal thriller': England fans react to 6-4 win over France
News.content:
England supporters in Miami have been celebrating the team finishing third in the World Cup, after victory over France. The win secured England's best-placed finish in the tournament since lifting the trophy in 1966.

Three Lions fans were left disappointed when England lost their semi-final with Argentina on Wednesday, failing to secure a spot in Sunday's final at the New York New Jersey Stadium.

However, England fans who stayed with the team for the match with France were treated to a thrilling 10-goal match.

England dominated the first half to lead 4-0, but France's resurgence in the second half saw the Three Lions edge out a 6-4 victory.

News.title: Donning protective kit for a first glance at the Bayeux Tapestry
News.content:
The British Museum is preparing to put the Bayeux Tapestry on display, after the 70m-long 11th Century embroidery was brought to London from northern France last week.

It was chaperoned by police guard from a secret location to the museum, under the cover of darkness. The priceless work is set to go on show in September.

It is the first time the artefact, which depicts events leading up to the Battle of Hastings and Norman Conquest of England in 1066, has returned to the UK in more than 900 years. It's believed to have been created here nearly 1,000 years ago.

The BBC's Culture Editor Katie Razzall visited the British Museum for a sneak peek.

News.title: 'Good day to drown a few sorrows,' says King as he pours pint
News.content:
King Charles III has hinted at England's World Cup semi-final loss to Argentina as he poured a pint in a pub.

"Maybe it's a good day to drown a few sorrows," he said to laughter, while Queen Camilla smiled as she stood next to him at the Hall & Woodhouse Badger Brewery in Blandford, Dorset.

News.title: Why the UK is dithering over what to do about e-scooters
News.content:
When I step out of Southampton Central railway station, it takes me just seconds to spot an e-scooter. In this city, these devices have become a normal part of the transport ecosystem, along with e-bikes.

"It's just the most convenient way to commute from home to the station and back," says Keith Reed, who I speak to as he arrives at the station to catch a train to London. Keith says uses rental e-scooters twice a week. His alternative option would be his bike, but he'd then have to worry about where to leave it.

Around the city, there are parking areas for bright orange rental devices everywhere - but they're not necessarily a permanent feature. Southampton hosts one of the numerous government-backed trials around England. This one has been going on since 2021.

Law & Order is set to welcome a new senior detective to the force — while waving goodbye to another.

Reid Scott, who has played Senior Detective Vincent Riley for three seasons, is set to leave the long-running police procedural.

The 48-year-old Veep and The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel star reportedly had one year left on his contract, but Deadline reports that he made the decision to exit early due to his family living in California while the show shoots in New York.

Scott is set to be replaced by James Badge Dale, who will star as a new Senior Detective.

Dale, also 48, is best known for film roles including 13 Hours: The Secret Soldiers Of Benghazi.

open image in gallery Reid Scott (left) is set to be replaced by James Badge Dale on the next season of 'Law & Order' ( Getty )

He made his film debut in a 1990 adaptation of Lord of the Flies, while back in 2002 he appeared in an episode of Law & Order: Special Victims Unit. His new character is not expected to be related to his previous appearance in the franchise.

Scott will give his character a proper send-off, and is currently filming his final episodes. No date has yet been announced for his last episode, and it has not yet been revealed how Dale’s character will take over his role in the show.

Fans have reacted with disappointment to news of Scott’s departure, with many pointing out his rapport with castmate Hugh Dancy.

One X user wrote: “Oh no! Reid Scott is leaving Law & Order! Now I'm sad. Hugh and Reid had such good chemistry...”

While another added: “Aww, Reid Scott is leaving Law & Order this season! Although apparently his departure will not be reduced to one line of dialogue in the season premiere, but instead, he will be back for a few episodes before being replaced.”

One user expressed excitement about Dale joining the cast, saying: “For the last couple of seasons L&O can’t keep detectives. But I do love James Badge Dale and excited to see him on one of my fav shows. If you have not seen him in Hightown, go watch now.”

This is just the latest casting shake-up for the show in the last few years, with another fan observing “The constant cop-centric shakeups on Law and Order have been a bummer,” before listing recent departures and adding: “Totally get why Reid would exit, but it's hard for that portion to get a rhythm going.”

open image in gallery Reid Scott (right) with ‘Law & Order’ cast mates Maura Tierney, Tony Goldwyn, Odelya Halevi and Hugh Dancy at the Empire State Building ( Getty )

Law & Order, which initially ran for 20 seasons between 1990 and 2010 before being revived in 2021, is known for its ”revolving door” casting policy that has led to many changes over its lengthy run.

However, some characters do manage to remain on air for decades. Last September, fans were up in arms after a character was killed offscreen after 35 years.

NYPD captain Donald Cragen, played by 75-year-old Dann Florek, first appeared in the original Law & Order series and subsequently starred in spin-off Law & Order: Special Victims Unit.

In the season 27 premiere of Special Victims Unit, which is TV’s longest-running live action series, Olivia Benson (Mariska Hargitay) paid tribute to her former leader, calling him the best boss she’s ever had.

“Everything I know about being a captain, I learned from him,” she said.

Fans were shocked by the revelation of Captain Cragen’s death, with one writing: “What do you mean we didn’t even get a proper goodbye scene between Captain Benson and Captain Cragen?? He is just gone???”

Another wrote: “Was excited for Law and Order: SVU to come back and they killed off Cragen?!?!?” while an additional fan said they are “so sad” by the decision.
