A New York City woman is suing McDonald’s after allegedly sustaining “serious and severe personal injuries and burns to [her] mouth and tongue, as a result of being served extremely hot fries,” according to a civil complaint obtained by The Independent.

In it, Catherine Luongo blames the March 5 incident, which occurred at a McDonald’s restaurant across the street from Manhattan’s Bryant Park, on the employees who “fail[ed] to provide [her] with a safe order of fries.”

Her purported physical trauma was “due solely… [to] the carelessness, recklessness and negligence” of the unnamed workers who prepared the fries in question, which the complaint describes as “overheated and not safe for human consumption.”

Luongo should never have been “permitt[ed] and allow[ed]” to “be served and consume extremely hot and overheated fries,” the complaint states. It contends that Luongo was not given ample warning of “the dangers to be encountered” when tucking into the fries, and that “the aforesaid occurrence was due solely by reason of the negligence of the Defendants,” and “through no fault or lack of care” on Luongo’s part.

On top of Luongo’s alleged mouth and tongue injuries, she also endured “a severe shock to the nervous system,” “suffered great physical pain and mental anguish,” and “was confined to bed and home and caused to abstain from usual duties and activities,” according to the complaint, which was filed July 21 in New York State Supreme Court.

open image in gallery A New York woman is suing McDonald's over injuries she claims she suffered while digging into an order of allegedly superheated fries ( Getty )

It says Luongo was “forced to seek medical aid and attention,” which she had to pay for herself, and claims her fry-related health issues “may be permanent and lasting.” The complaint does not provide further details of Luongo’s alleged injuries.

McDonald’s did not respond to a request for comment.

In 2013, the chain was hauled into court by a Massachusetts mom who sued after her 3-year-old daughter suffered first- and second-degree burns on her thighs from an order of “unreasonably and dangerously hot” fries.

“As a direct and proximate cause of the unreasonably and dangerously hot French Fries, M.C. is now disfigured and scarred,” the lawsuit claimed. “M.C. is undergoing surgery due to the disfigurement and scarring.”

That same year, a Florida woman was awarded $800,000 after her 4-year-old daughter received second-degree burns from a “dangerously hot” Chicken McNugget that fell from its packaging and became wedged between the child’s leg and her seat belt. Philana Holmes used her iPhone to record the girl’s screams, which were played in court.

Lawyers for McDonald’s unsuccessfully argued that the McNugget had to be heated to a certain temperature to stave off the possibility of salmonella poisoning, and, as PBS reported at the time, that the nuggets “were not meant to be pressed between a seat belt and human flesh for more than two minutes.”

A similar suit, this one filed in 2009, involved an order of “dangerously hot” Dunkin’ Donuts hash browns and a Boston-area toddler, who they said received “serious and permanent burn injuries” when the hot potatoes fell from his mouth onto his neck. Before Robin MacLeod gave her son the hash brown, she checked it and found it “lukewarm,” the family’s complaint said.

open image in gallery Catherine Luongo claims she was injured by an order of scaldingly hot fries she purchased at a McDonald's on East 42 Street in Manhattan ( Google Maps )

However, the hash brown had been heated “unevenly,” according to the filing, which claimed the inside of the item was so hot, it was “unsafe for public consumption.”

Beyond the fast-food realm, a Philadelphia man sued Frontier Airlines in 2024 after sustaining third-degree burns and being “left with disfiguring scars on his genitals and thighs” after a flight attendant allegedly spilled hot tea on his lap.

As The Independent first reported, Sean Miller’s complaint detailed the “highly unsightly and embarrassing discoloration,” along with “significantly decreased sensation,” “post-traumatic stress disorder,” and “lack of self-esteem,” plus at least one herniated disc he suffered while writhing in distress.

Upon landing, the 56-year-old was rushed to an area burn center for specialized treatment “due to the severity” of his injuries.

Such lawsuits, including Luongo’s, bring to mind the well-known and widely misunderstood case of 79-year-old Stella Liebeck, who was maligned for bringing a “frivolous” lawsuit over a blisteringly hot cup of McDonald’s coffee, but which turned out to be anything but trivial.

Liebeck suffered horrific third-degree burns across six percent of her body and led to permanent tissue damage after the cup’s superheated contents spilled on her, causing what her physician called one of the worst scalding cases he had ever seen. The New Mexico resident spent a week in the hospital, three weeks recovering at home, and was then hospitalized again to undergo painful debridement and skin grafts.

Liebeck offered to settle for the costs of her medical treatment, about $20,000, and only sued when McDonald’s, which had in fact gotten hundreds of burn complaints before this one, refused to cooperate.

A jury awarded Liebeck $2.7 million in punitive damages for her injuries, which a judge later reduced to $480,000, for what he deemed “willful, wanton, reckless” and “callous” conduct on the part of McDonald's.

Food service establishments have argued that a reasonable adult is aware that certain foods and beverages are hot, and that a potential burn is an “open and obvious” risk they knowingly assume. At the same time, if a product is so hot that normal use could land someone in the hospital, the seller is required to provide an explicit warning to all.

Luongo’s suit says she “has been damaged in a sum which exceeds the jurisdictional limits of all lower Courts,” and is seeking money damages to be determined at trial

Andy Burnham has announced he is pausing the early release scheme for prisoners after it emerged that two people involved in the death of Andrew Harper could be freed within months.

The new prime minister vowed that “no prisoners will be let out under this policy” pending an “urgent review”, saying he would do everything he can “to minimise risk to the public”.

Some 5,000 prisoners were due to start being released from September as part of a policy, introduced under Sir Keir Starmer, to ease the overcrowding crisis in prisons.

But a row broke out about the policy on Wednesday after it was revealed that two of those responsible for the death of Pc Harper could be eligible for automatic release under the scheme.

The police officer was 28 years old when he sustained fatal injuries after getting caught in a strap attached to the back of a car as three teenage suspects fled the scene of a burglary in Berkshire in 2019.

Under the scheme, Henry Long, then aged 19, the driver of the car who was sentenced to 16 years, would not be eligible for the early release. But Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers, who were both 18 at the time and handed 13 years in custody in 2020 for Pc Harper’s manslaughter, could be.

Announcing the pause on Thursday, the prime minister said: “Keeping the public safe will always be my top priority.

“I am working closely with the new justice secretary and have instructed my team to put a pause on the changes that were due to start in September.

“No prisoners will be let out under this policy until we have conducted an urgent review and done everything we can to minimise risk to the public. Where changes are needed, we will not hesitate to make them.”

Lissie Harper, Pc Harper’s widow, on Wednesday described the scheme as “deplorable” and accused politicians of “making decisions from behind a desk that will have real and lasting consequences” for the families of victims. T

open image in gallery Prime minister Andy Burnham has paused the early release scheme ( PA Wire )

She said: “It has taken me years to rebuild a life that was torn apart in a matter of moments. Years to pick up the pieces left behind by three men whose actions robbed Andrew of his life and stole our future.

“Now – once again – politicians are making decisions from behind a desk that will have real and lasting consequences for victims’ families like mine.”

She added: “It is deplorable to me that we have reached a point where releasing prisoners early is even considered acceptable. We speak of justice, accountability and standing with victims, yet decisions like this do the opposite.”

PC Harper’s mother also described the news that two of his killers could be released halfway through their sentences as an “insult”.

Debbie Adlam told ITV News: “It’s not enough. It’s a good start, and it really is a good basis to begin working on some sensible alternatives and looking at options for going forward, because there’s so many people this affects, it’s not just us.

“It’s incredibly personal to us, but it’s not just us.“And I think it really needs a good looking at, not just a quick meeting and ‘that’s it, we’ll move on’.

“It needs to be looked at thoroughly and that’s what I’m hoping for. We want to see some results from it.”

Meanwhile, the chief constable of Thames Valley Police, Jason Hogg, said it “feels wrong” for the killers to leave prison early. If they were being sentenced today, they would be handed life sentences under Harper’s Law, which was introduced in 2022 following a campaign from the officer’s family.

Mr Burnham said on Wednesday he wanted to make sure “everything has been looked at” before the policy goes ahead as planned in September.

“I can’t say that I can change the policy completely, but I will look at it in detail before we go further forward,” he said.

open image in gallery PC Andrew Harper with his wife, Lissie ( Thames Valley Police )

Prison overcrowding has forced successive governments into making emergency releases, with the Conservative administration’s End of Custody Supervised Licence scheme, launched in 2023, releasing over 10,000 inmates between 18 and 70 days early.

This was followed by Labour’s SDS40 scheme, which has seen 56,323 offenders released after serving 40 per cent of their prison term between September 2024 and December 2025.

Reforms in the Sentencing Act came after prisons came close to running out of space entirely last year, risking the “total breakdown of law and order” which would leave police unable to make arrests and courts unable to send offenders to custody, the then justice secretary Shabana Mahmood said.

It is based on a package of measures set out in David Gauke’s Independent Sentencing Review, which urged the government to take “decisive action” to ensure they are never forced to rely on the emergency releases again.

Unlike SDS40, the Sentencing Act reforms do not exclude those convicted of sex offences, domestic abuse and serious violent offences. However, those serving life sentences, extended sentences and imprisonment for public protection (IPP) jail terms will not be eligible.

Florida Republican Representative Kat Cammack says she “wouldn’t feel comfortable” with her daughter working on Capitol Hill due to the “culture of creepiness” — an issue that has taken center stage due to a recent push within Congress to ban relationships between members and House staffers.

A bipartisan House task force on sexual misconduct is weighing whether to recommend banning romantic relationships between lawmakers and staffers as part of an effort to reduce harassment on Capitol Hill.

“Listen, if you’re looking for love, I suggest you look elsewhere,” Cammack, 38, told MeidasTouch Tuesday on Capitol Hill. “Maybe join, I don’t know, what are the apps these days? eHarmony? Match? Grindr? Tinder? Swipe right? Swipe left? I’m not quite sure, but I think we’d be better off if members were more focused on their work than enhancing their love life.”

When asked if she had heard staffers complain about sexual misconduct by members, the congresswoman laughed and said: “I’m trying to think of another way to say eff-yeah without using that word, but yeah, it’s a really big effing problem.”

“I think that it’s ridiculous that people don’t recognize the power imbalance that exists here on Capitol Hill, and it’s extraordinarily inappropriate if you are the member and you are trying to put the moves on your own staff,” she continued.

open image in gallery Florida Rep. Kat Cammack acknowledged the ‘culture of creepiness’ on Capitol Hill, as a bipartisan group of lawmakers works on a proposal to ban relationships between House lawmakers and staff ( Reuters )

Commack added: “People don’t recognize that even if it’s another staffer in another office, you still have a tremendous influence over that Congressional staffer’s career.”

The congresswoman then addressed the situation in a personal light.

“Listen, I don’t want the government involved in people’s love lives, but what we have seen is, like I said, a culture of creepiness where you have members that are soliciting staff, they’re approaching staff, they’re putting them in very awkward situations, and that’s just wrong. And so, I wouldn’t feel comfortable sending my daughter to work here on Capitol Hill, and until I feel like that has changed, we’re gonna keep going to try to figure out ways to make Capitol Hill a safe place to work.”

When asked to clarify if she would tell parents to send their children to work on Capitol Hill, Cammack responded: “Not in this environment, no.”

Cammack’s blunt comments come as efforts to reduce harassment and sexual misconduct on Capitol Hill have reached a fever pitch. A bipartisan group between Republican and Democratic women’s caucuses was formed this spring to target reforms that would make Congress a safer and more professional place for women.

open image in gallery The issue of whether members of Congress should be allowed to date staffers — including staffers outside of their office — has been at the center of a debate over how to eradicate sexual harassment on the Hill. It comes after Democrat Eric Swalwell (pictured) and Republican Tony Gonzales resigned in April, over separate allegations of sexual misconduct ( AFP/Getty )

The issue of whether members of Congress should be allowed to date staffers — including staffers outside of their office — has been at the center of a debate over how to eradicate sexual harassment on the Hill. It comes after Democrat Eric Swalwell and Republican Tony Gonzales resigned in April, over separate allegations of sexual misconduct.

Swalwell, from California, also faces allegations of sexual assault. Gonzales, from Texas, admitted to having an affair with a staffer, who later died by suicide.

House Speaker Mike Johnson, a Republican, weighed in on the issue Tuesday, saying he didn’t think members of Congress should be romantically involved with any House staffers.

“I can’t believe it would be acceptable in any situation,” Johnson said at a press conference. “I think we should, as a bare minimum in Congress, have rules and traditions that are adhered to in corporate America, so that is an easy one for me.”

It is currently against House rules for members to pursue or date their own staff, but his comments may help the bipartisan group pushing for greater restrictions. It was not immediately clear how potential changes to the rules for lawmakers would go forward, but it would require a revision to the House Code of Official Conduct, according to Politico.

open image in gallery Former Rep. Tony Gonzales, from Texas, admitted to having an affair with a staffer, who later died by suicide ( Getty )

Cammack, who is part of the working group, told CNN Tuesday that they were about “70 percent” there on a list of proposals. She noted that one difficulty the group was facing was coming up with ideas for addressing lawmakers who break the rules.

“You have to balance the constitutional role that we have in protecting people back home and their right to representation and bad behavior up here on Washington in on Capitol Hill,” Cammack said.

“That to me is probably one of the most frustrating things, is if constituents back home knew how their member was operating up here on Capitol Hill, the people back home would take care of business in the following election. But unfortunately … we don’t wear body cameras up here.”

Away from the general classification battle on the Tour de France there are a dozen other skirmishes going on. For American world Tour team EF Education-EasyPost, it’s the fight for stage wins which is most significant. The team’s Tour de France squad includes two of the most instinctive racers of this era, Ben Healy and Richard Carapaz, as well as other riders noted for their ability to get into breakaways and make moves stick against all odds, like Kasper Asgreen.

The eight riders travelling through France are shepherded by a host of sports directors, mechanics, soigneurs and other support staff, with the whole operation masterminded by ex-pro and general manager, Jonathan Vaughters, all in the hope of that rare beast, a stage win in cycling’s most prestigious race.

Speaking to The Independent, Vaughters likens running a cycling team to a military campaign: “There’s the behind-the-scenes people that are essentially your supply line for your front line, the riders, there’s a chain of command going on and there’s communications from the coaches up to the riders during the race, there’s an overall strategy that is dictated by me. So it’s a mobile logistics operation where we’re going out and, you know, fighting a battle every day.”

That “battle” analogy feels fitting: EF as a team specialise in the kind of swashbuckling, attacking riding that is increasingly being squeezed out of cycling. The Independent speaks to Vaughters on the morning of stage 10, a tough, hilly day finishing in Le Lioran, where Jonas Vingegaard pipped Tadej Pogacar in a sprint finish in 2024.

EF manage to get the in-form French rider Alex Baudin, who finished fourth from the breakaway on stage nine in Ussel, into the day’s break. But UAE Team Emirates-XRG, the team of race leader Pogacar, give fierce chase behind and keep the escapees on a tight leash, while Dutch powerhouse Mathieu van der Poel is unstoppable in the finish.

Is UAE’s dominance a source of frustration for other teams? Vaughters is pragmatic about it: “To get frustrated about it is a waste of time. But I would say it magnifies an issue that the sport has, which is, quite simply, like a team like UAE can afford whatever the rider they want on the transfer market because their payroll budget is essentially unlimited.”

UAE’s squad is built around Pogacar but also contains a serious podium contender in Mexican starlet Isaac del Toro, who was second in last year’s Giro d’Italia and currently sits third overall.

The financial disparity is enormous: Vaughters is confident that UAE’s eight-man Tour de France squad are earning nearly double EF’s entire 30-man team. According to La Gazzetta dello Sport, budgets for a team like UAE are around or above €50m (EF have previously said their own budget is average for the World Tour, so around half that figure).

open image in gallery General manager Jonathan Vaughters ( Ashley & Jered Gruber/Gruber Images )

Vaughters estimates that for most teams rider salaries account for around 50 per cent of a team’s budget, which is likely to be closer to 60 per cent for UAE, “simply because their logistics costs are not going to rise exponentially or parallel to the rider costs”. It gives them a staggering amount to spend on accruing, and keeping, top talent.

So how do you compete against a team like that? You try to acquire some financial muscle of your own. Education First, the Swedish education and language company, which is EF Education-EasyPost’s primary sponsor, is open to relinquishing the team’s naming rights in the hope of securing more extensive financial backing. That, hopefully, will take the team closer to UAE budget-wise – to more like 75 per cent of their budget, Vaughters estimates, as opposed to where they currently are, operating at around 40 or 50 per cent.

Another thing Vaughters is hopeful cycling could introduce is some kind of financial fair play system, to try to even the playing field behind those teams with “government money” like UAE and those still run the more traditional way, with sponsorship by large but not state-funded companies. Vaughters points out that the huge wealth disparity, and dominance by one team, “detracts from the fan experience”.

But will anything really change? Cycling is a deeply traditional sport with power concentrated in the hands of companies like Tour de France organisers ASO, who own the majority of the sport’s top races and are known for a conservative approach, and trying to get the myriad stakeholders, teams, governing bodies and riders’ unions to agree is much easier said than done.

Vaughters says: “I think a lot of times cycling loses out because of infighting amongst the various parties inside the sport. In theory, the teams should all be pretty aligned in what their interests are in this, but that's not entirely the case.”

open image in gallery Irish rider Ben Healy has struggled to match his exploits from last year's Tour ( Ashley & Jered Gruber/Gruber Images )

Which brings us onto another issue which seems to be permanently up for debate: the calendar, which as it stands is a mish-mash of races which often clash or overlap. Vaughters says: “Cycling has spent 100 years of growing very organically, and it has not grown strategically.”

He contrasts it to Formula One, which has a straightforward season-long narrative, with drivers and teams accruing points throughout each race that contribute to an overall championship. “That's a lot easier for fans to follow, and the season builds on itself. It's the same people battling week in, week out, which really establishes a consistent fan base. F1 clearly is designed to be an audience-friendly sporting event. I think for cycling to be competitive with these other sports, the calendar needs to be redesigned in a strategic sense, not in an organic sense.”

The counterpoint to this is that cycling, held on open roads in the world’s biggest and most accessible arena, doesn’t struggle for fans. But there are other reasons why the calendar may need a redesign: one of the big stories of this Tour, and one which can no longer be ignored in the wider sport, is the existential threat of extreme heat and the climate crisis.

A 40C heatwave in central France in the opening week forced stage nine to be shortened, while wildfires meant the finale of stage three had to be raced with no spectators at the roadside. Pogacar has been among those to call for the calendar to be changed to avoid racing in the summer months, with broiling temperatures putting riders and crowds at risk.

open image in gallery Carapaz won the most combative rider award on stage 14 but was denied a stage win by Pogacar ( Reuters )

As with anything in the sport, progress, if it happens at all, will be slow. Vaughters says: “Short term, maybe there’s some simpler measures, [moving] the races either quite a bit earlier or quite a bit later in the day [to avoid the worst of the heat].” Even that would run into opposition: “I know there's commercial interests that don’t align with that, from a television audience standpoint.”

The heat is having a bigger impact on certain riders than others: Irishman Healy was the animator of last year’s Tour, taking the yellow jersey and winning a stage while lighting up breakaways, but his season has been hampered by injury and illness, and the searing heat has done him no favours. “He’s kind of waking up every day hoping it’s going to rain, and so are we,” Vaughters jokes.

Four stages remain on this Tour, and for all EF’s efforts, that stage win remains elusive. But a trio of gruelling mountain stages offer more opportunities to get up the road and try to stave off UAE. For the underdogs, it’s the sort of chance they relish. And by the time the next Tour rolls around, rather than trying to undercut Pogacar, they could be competing on a level playing field.

Charlie Woods’ run at the U.S. Junior Amateur came to a frustrating end Wednesday after a spectator’s camera click disrupted a crucial playoff shot, costing the 17-year-old golfer a chance to advance to match play.

The son of 15-time major champion Tiger Woods was competing at Saucon Valley Country Club in Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, where he entered a sudden-death playoff with 13 other players battling for the final two spots in the tournament’s match-play round. Woods finished stroke play Tuesday tied for 63rd after shooting rounds of 76 and 70 across two courses for a 5-over total.

But on the first playoff hole Wednesday, Woods tried to reach the par-5 green in two shots. However, he came up short and landed in the rough. As he lined up his third shot, the loud sound of an iPhone camera shutter went off during his backswing.

“Really, dude? I mean, come on,” Woods said after the missed shot.

“Right in the middle of his swing,” someone else from the crowd added.

Charlie Woods, 17, was eliminated from the U.S. Junior Amateur Wednesday after a spectator’s phone camera made a noise during a crucial shot ( AP )

Woods was unable to recover from the distraction, eventually making a bogey that ended his tournament run. Eli Wessel and Hudson Kutchma went on to claim the final two spots in match play.

The tournament was Woods’ third appearance at the U.S. Junior Amateur, and despite the disappointing finish, he showed improvement from previous years. He has continued to build his amateur career while verbally committing to play college golf at Florida State University for the recruiting class of 2027.

The incident comes after a challenging stretch for Tiger Woods, who completed an inpatient rehab program in Switzerland before returning to the U.S. in mid-June following a rollover crash and DUI arrest in Florida.

Since then, the golf icon has slowly started making public appearances again, including a stop at a PGA Tour event on June 23. His legal case tied to the March crash is still ongoing.

News.title: Listen carefully to Karoline Leavitt. She’s revealing Trump’s scariest plans
News.content:

Whether it's investigating the financials of Elon Musk's pro-Trump PAC or producing our latest documentary, 'The A Word', which shines a light on the American women fighting for reproductive rights, we know how important it is to parse out the facts from the messaging. If you took Karoline Leavitt’s words at face value, you’d be a deeply confused, extremely alarmed person. For one thing, you’d believe that “literal self-proclaimed communists” are “winning elections” and “claiming to be the new leadership” of the Democratic Party. This fact, the White House press secretary told the room gravely on Thursday, could end up making America look very much like the “failed state” of Cuba.

It’s not exactly unusual for Republicans to call Democrats communists, but it is interesting how the words “literal” and “self-proclaimed” have now lost all their meaning in MAGAland.

It’s interesting, too, that the left-of-center Democrats who have recently won elections — such as Zohran Mamdani in New York — did so after campaigning on affordability, a word that both Trump and Leavitt have an ongoing issue with. Trump, nonsensically, has said before that “affordability is a Democrat scam” and a “hoax,” and Leavitt today echoed that when she attacked the “Democrat solution to, quote, affordability”.

But if you keep saying “affordability” like it isn’t a real word or a real issue, it doesn’t stop people noticing when their groceries aren’t affordable. Skyrocketing prices of fertilizer that then impacted food prices across the country happened because of Trump’s war in Iran. Skyrocketing prices of oil that then impacted gas prices across the country happened because of Trump’s war in Iran.

No amount of claims about “the economy” being fantastic or Trump “setting up workers to thrive like never before” will make Americans stop believing the numbers on their credit cards.

( Reuters )

This was a short White House press briefing, but it was telling. When asked about the nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia, Leavitt first read out a Truth Social post made by Trump the night before (a bizarre choice in itself.) She then suggested that the reason Saudi Arabia gets a civilian nuclear deal and Iran doesn’t is because the Saudi deal gives “priority access to American companies” and “puts America first.” It’s extremely ‘we went to war for their oil’-adjacent reasoning, and it’s the type of thing even the world’s least scrupulous leaders tend not to say in public.

The administration limps on in Iran, repeatedly justifying death and destruction by saying that “Iran must never have a nuclear weapon”. Trump has even recently stated, without evidence, that the 17 American service members who have died in the conflict so far personally told him that that’s a belief they each individually held dear.

And yet, here we are, signing sudden deals with another country in the region that allow, according to some insiders, for Saudi to escalate its nuclear ambitions with no international oversight. It’s an incredibly risky thing to do from a geopolitical perspective. The justification — that it will make American corporations money and that’s why the country isn’t being bombed into oblivion like Iran — should be genuinely shocking.

Perhaps it would be, if the zone weren’t being flooded with claims about literal self-proclaimed communists and voter scams. Leavitt’s answer about New Jersey, where it was recently found that 6600 non-citizens had been erroneously added to voter rolls and then identified and removed, was effectively that there’s a conspiracy afoot, that the New Jersey governor can’t be trusted, and that the president has a feeling about all that so it’s probably true.

“All of a sudden this governor put out a press release saying President Trump was right… it’s not a coincidence,” Leavitt said, her voice rising.

“She says it’s 6600, we suspect it’s a heck of a lot more,” she continued, adding that “the president is hellbent on getting to the bottom of this.”

The president is sanctioning nuclear expansion in Saudi Arabia and you can read about it on Truth Social if you want to know the details. The president thinks the election won’t be fair while his approval ratings are dropping. The president will not allow communism to rein in America. The president says the economy is doing great, and that the word ‘affordability’ doesn’t exist. The president got loud applause in Georgia this week, which proves he’s actually more popular than the lamestream media would have you believe.

Karoline Leavitt is much more cogent than the president, but she still accurately communicates the chaos of his mindset. So yes, if you took her words at face value, you’d be a deeply confused, extremely alarmed person. In other words, you’d be exactly where MAGA would prefer you to be.

News.title: Why a Trump ally’s ‘criminal’ case against Jack Smith is going to fall apart
News.content:

Whether it's investigating the financials of Elon Musk's pro-Trump PAC or producing our latest documentary, 'The A Word', which shines a light on the American women fighting for reproductive rights, we know how important it is to parse out the facts from the messaging. The top Republican on the House Judiciary Committee is referring Jack Smith to the Department of Justice for criminal prosecution, escalating Donald Trump’s war with the man who investigated his attempts to overturn election results and keep classified documents at Mar-a-Lago.

Trump’s Justice Department, now led by the president’s former criminal defense attorney, will ultimately decide whether to open an investigation into Smith, who Trump has publicly demanded be thrown in jail.

But the referral from Rep. Jim Jordan appears to rest on a flimsy premise.

Smith is accused of misleading members of Congress during his testimony about the special counsel’s investigation into Trump’s efforts to reverse his loss during the 2020 presidential election. Smith “gave the impression” that he did not access “privileged text messages” from Republican lawmakers, according to Jordan. “We now know this to be false,” Jordan wrote.

Jordan says Smith provided “half truths” to the committee by not explaining where those text messages came from. But the panel never asked him that, and the messages were already in the possession of the National Archives.

open image in gallery House Judiciary Committee chair Jim Jordan is referring Jack Smith to the Department of Justice for criminal prosecution over his alleged ‘half truths’ to members of Congress, which Smith’s legal team has flatly denied ( AFP/Getty )

A crusade from Trump’s Republican allies in Congress to prosecute Smith kicked off last year, when Senate Republicans falsely accused the former special counsel and FBI investigators of “tapping” their phones.

Instead, Smith’s team sought a “preliminary toll analysis” of nine senators’ phone records, which only include what numbers were called and when and for how long. They do not include the contents of messages or conversations, which would require a court-approved wiretap.

Agents were pulling data from the days immediately before and after January 6, 2021, when Trump and his allies were scrambling to derail a joint session of Congress to formally certify Joe Biden’s election.

That call analysis appeared to be part of the FBI’s “Arctic Frost” investigation, which was opened one year earlier by Timothy Thibault, former assistant special agent in charge of the FBI’s Washington field office. That investigation was then assigned to Smith.

The “Arctic Frost” probe examined a “multifaceted conspiracy” to overturn election results in states that Trump lost, according to an unclassified memo outlining the investigation.

Nevertheless, Senate Republicans have labeled the investigation a “modern Watergate” and pushed for legislation that would allow them to sue for up to $500,000 for each record that was legally obtained.

open image in gallery Jordan’s letter is addressed to Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche, the president’s former criminal defense attorney who sought to end the special counsel’s investigation into then-candidate Trump while working as his personal lawyer ( AFP/Getty )

Last week, Republican senators released documents showing Smith’s office also pulled messages from 44 members of Congress, including at least 11 Republican senators and six Republican House members.

Smith’s team, however, obtained those records from the National Archives, which maintains a record of messages and calls from all administrations, including Trump’s.

None of the lawmakers whose messages were obtained by Smith’s team were the targets of a record request, which sought communications from White House figures from October 2020 through Jan. 20, 2021.

The messages were discovered on the phones of several figures at the center of the special counsel’s investigations, including former White House chief of staff Mark Meadows, Trump-allied attorney Rudy Giuliani and other chief aides.

Nobody on the House Judiciary Committee ever asked Smith how he got hold of those messages.

Instead, Smith was asked if he ever asked for a “search warrant for the content of any text messages from members.”

“No, I don’t recall that,” Smith said during a deposition in December.

He also was asked about whether the “toll records” included the content of lawmakers’ phone calls or text messages.

“No,” Smith replied.

Jordan now says Smith “willingly and knowingly made false representations” to the committee and wants the Justice Department to open an investigation to determine whether he did so to "obstruct the committee’s oversight.

open image in gallery Rep Jamie Raskin, the top Democrat on the House Judiciary Committee, said the referral should be ‘laughed out of court’ ( Reuters )

Trump applauded Jordan’s letter in a post on his Truth Social account at 5:31 a.m. Thursday.

“Justice at last???” he wrote.

Lawyers for Smith said in a letter responding to the letter that Jordan’s referral is based on a “spurious claim.”

“The referral is made not because Mr. Smith made a false statement, which the letter concedes, but because he did not proactively disclose information that was not responsive to a question asked,” they wrote, according to a copy of a response obtained by The New York Times.

Rep. Jamie Raskin, the committee’s top Democrat, said Jordan’s letter “will get laughed out of court.”

“The Republicans fault Mr. Smith for not reading the minds of congressional investigators and for not volunteering information they didn’t ask for,” he said in a statement. “This is absurd. Mr. Smith may be telegenic but he’s not telepathic.”

A successful prosecution isn’t necessarily Republicans’ goal, according to Raskin. Instead, the criminal referral “is meant to please their Fox News viewership” and “whitewash their own participation in a scheme to overthrow our elections.”

Raskin also accused Republicans of distracting from the Senate Judiciary Committee’s confirmation vote for Todd Blanche, who the president has nominated to serve as U.S. Attorney General after defending the president during his criminal prosecutions.

The Congressional Integrity Project, a nonprofit watchdog, slammed Jordan for decrying the “weaponization” of the federal government only to use his committee to target an opponent.

“Using a congressional gavel to threaten a prosecutor for testifying honestly is exactly the weaponization Jordan claimed to hate,” spokesperson Jeremy Funk said. “His referral is revenge on behalf of Donald Trump, nothing more.”

News.title: Ebola death toll passes 1,000 as outbreak shows no signs of slowing
News.content:
More than 1,000 people have now died in the outbreak of Ebola in the Congo, as medics struggle to curb the fastest-growing epidemic of the virus.

Dozens of deaths are being recorded each day and modelling has forecast that, in a worst case scenario, it could become the worst Ebola outbreak in history.

The outbreak, centred on the north east of Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), passed the four-figure death milestone little more than two months after it was first declared.

By contrast, the worst outbreak of the haemorrhagic fever on record, which struck West Africa from 2014 to 2016, took eight months from the first case to reach 1,000 deaths. It went on to kill 11,000 people.

The latest figures from the DRC’s national public health institute show 2,536 confirmed Ebola cases and 1,033 deaths, with at least 738 patients in isolation or hospitalised.

News.title: Inflation fall a ‘false dawn’, Burnham warned
News.content:
Falling inflation is a “false dawn” for Andy Burnham, economists warned after the pace of price rises slowed in June.

The consumer prices index (CPI) fell from 2.8pc in May to 2.6pc last month, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS), beating economists’ expectations of a drop to 2.7pc to mark the lowest rate in 15 months.

Lower petrol and diesel prices drove the slowdown amid a short-lived peace deal between the US and Iran, while price pressures from chocolate, oils and fats, dairy and meat also weakened.

However, economists warned a rise in household energy bills in July may already have pushed inflation back up above 3pc.

Suren Thiru, chief economist at the Institute of Chartered Accountants, said: “June’s slowdown is a false dawn as it may have already been reversed this month with higher energy bills, following Ofgem’s energy price cap rise, likely to have lifted inflation above 3pc.”

July’s 13pc increase in the energy price cap has pushed typical annual bills to around £1,862, while renewed fighting between the US and Iran has reignited concerns over oil and gas supplies.

Mr Thiru said elevated inflation would create a fresh headache for John Healey, the newly appointed Chancellor, by squeezing household budgets, raising government borrowing costs and limiting his room for tax cuts or spending increases.

Charlotte O’Leary, at the National Institute of Economic and Social Research, said: “June’s peace deal and the subsequent reduction in oil and gas prices helped cool consumer price inflation. This will be a welcome figure to start the new Prime Minister’s premiership, but the honeymoon period will be short-lived.”

The Bank of England will also be watching closely as it weighs further interest rate cuts, though economists warned renewed instability in the Middle East and higher energy bills could keep inflation close to 3pc for the rest of the year.

Mr Healey said: “Falling inflation is news families want to hear, but there is much more to do to give people the breathing space they need.”

News.title: Russia destroys Ukraine HIV warehouse
News.content:
A Russian missile strike has destroyed $2.6m (£1.9m) worth of HIV prevention supplies in Ukraine, according to an international aid group.

The Alliance for Public Health said the attack on Sunday night near Kyiv hit a warehouse holding 62 million prevention items earmarked for Ukraine’s harm reduction programmes next year. It includes syringes, needles, alcohol wipes, and condoms intended to support more than 300,000 people.

“This is not just another strike. It is an attack on 300,000 Ukrainians who depend on HIV prevention services and on their fundamental right to health,” said Andriy Klepikov, executive director of the Alliance for Public Health.

Efforts to prevent the spread of HIV rely heavily on harm reduction programmes that supply sterile syringes and needles to people who inject drugs, alongside condoms and other supplies that help curb sexual transmission.

Mr Klepikov said the destruction of the warehouse would not immediately disrupt services, because his organisation had moved its supplies for the rest of the year out of central storage and into regional distribution centres several weeks ago as part of contingency planning.

“Russia failed,” he said, adding that the Alliance had notified international partners and appealed for urgent support to rebuild next year’s inventory.

News.title: Private sector pay suffers worst growth since Covid
News.content:
Private sector wages are growing at their slowest pace since the pandemic, piling pressure on Andy Burnham as he enters Downing Street facing a fragile economy and strained public finances.

Salaries rose by 2.9pc in the three months to May, the first time growth has dipped below 3pc since October 2020 and only narrowly ahead of inflation at 2.8pc.

The slowdown was most acute in key industries, with wages in finance and business services up just 2.3pc, manufacturing at 2.5pc and construction earnings falling by 0.2pc over the year.

In contrast, public sector pay accelerated to 5.5pc after striking workers secured higher settlements, widening the gap between state and private sectors.

The cooling labour market came as borrowing overshot official forecasts, leaving John Healey, the new Chancellor, with a £2.7bn gap against expectations.

The Government borrowed £57.6bn between April and June – less than a year earlier but still ahead of projections – pushing public debt to nearly £3tn, or 94.9pc of GDP.

Mr Healey said: “The Prime Minister and I have talked about how we will work in lockstep to meet the fiscal rules with a buffer against uncertainty and how we’ll make life more affordable for working people right across the UK.”

However, Sir Mel Stride, the shadow business secretary, said: “If Andy Burnham and John Healey are really serious about the future of our economy then they must get borrowing under control.”

News.title: Scammers stole $114 billion as Southeast Asia’s crime gangs go corporate
News.content:
Scam gangs stole up to $114 billion from people in Asia-Pacific alone in 2025, the UN has warned, as crime syndicates rapidly professionalise their tactics to evade law enforcement in Southeast Asia.

By way of comparison, the sum dwarfs the $85 billion the UK spends each year on defence.

The Asia-Pacific region has emerged as an epicentre for massive cyber fraud operations since the Covid pandemic. Scammers – some willingly, others under duress – are now stealing billions from internet users across the world via fake romance and cryptocurrency investment schemes.

In 2025, these fraud operations stole between $88.3 and $114.1bn from just people across East Asia, Southeast Asia, Australia and New Zealand, according to a report on Tuesday from the UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC).

Those figures are triple the estimated losses in 2023, between $18 and $37bn, and don’t account for victims in Europe or the US.

The scam centres – which began in fortified compounds but are now increasingly housed in innocuous office blocks and villas – are found across the region, but have especially exploited power vacuums caused by war, corruption and weak governance in Cambodia, Myanmar and Laos.

Although the scammers initially targeted people in China, they have dramatically expanded their ambitions. The UNODC said people from at least 80 countries and territories had been identified in compounds, with recruiters seeking people from outside Asia as they look to expand new markets.

News.title: UK borrowing costs rise at fastest pace in G7
News.content:
Britain’s borrowing costs rose at the fastest pace in the G7 after Andy Burnham said he would take a “flexible” approach to the UK’s fiscal rules.

In his maiden speech as prime minister, Mr Burnham on Monday signalled he could bend the rules underpinning Britain’s finances, spooking financial markets fearful of higher government spending.

UK gilts – a benchmark for how much the Government pays on its debt – saw yields rise 0.08 percentage points to an eight-week high of 5.03pc for the 10-year bond. Thirty-year gilts also pushed higher.

The rise was the fastest in the G7, excluding Japan, whose markets are closed for a national holiday.

After markets closed on Monday, Mr Burnham surprised the City by picking John Healey as his next Chancellor.

Mr Healey, who quit over defence funding rising too slowly, will now be tasked with finding billions of pounds in Britain’s stretched public finances.

Shabana Mahmood, the Home Secretary, had widely been expected for the role. Ed Miliband, the former Energy Secretary, was also in contention.

Mr Healey will replace Rachel Reeves, who resigned on Monday.

The appointment of Mr Healey, a veteran of the Blair-Brown government, may calm fears in the City after Mr Burnham pledged to stretch the fiscal rules by using “flexibility” within them.

Speaking in Downing Street, Mr Burnham said: “I’ve said we’ll stick to the fiscal rules, and by that I mean the existing fiscal rules, and use obviously any flexibility within them.”

James Athey, a fund manager at Marlborough, said: “It’s not a good start because bandying around the words fiscal rules seems to be believed within government circles to be a sufficient condition to get financial markets on side, and that just misunderstands an element of the problem.”

He added that investors were watching closely for any signs that the Government will increase borrowing.

Matt Amis, investment director at Aberdeen, said Mr Burnham’s comments had “got the markets’ attention.”

He said “It just shows this week in particular the language from the Burnham administration, the new chancellor, is going to be key here. The gilt market is on edge.”

Mr Burnham, who has become the UK’s seventh prime minister in just a decade, has inherited a troubled economy as businesses grapple with low confidence and strained public finances.

Monday’s comment suggests the new prime minister will use measures to raise borrowing while keeping the additional sums off the Government’s book.

The Resolution Foundation, a think tank, said he could do this by expanding the remit of institutions like the National Wealth Fund, an arms-length government investment vehicle.

His plan to use “flexibility” in the fiscal rules comes after Ms Reeves altered the main indicator of government debt in 2024.

She tweaked the primary measure of the UK’s debt to Public Sector Net Financial Liabilities, meaning that when public financial institutions borrow to invest in a private business it does not count towards the government’s fiscal rules.

However, the think tank warned that boosting the financial capacity of public financial institutions like the National Wealth Fund by £16bn would cost around £400 million a year in debt interest.

Helen Miller, director at the Institute for Fiscal Studies, warned that challenging public finances will mean Mr Burnham will be forced to make tough choices on spending.

She said: “While chancellors come and go, the underlying fiscal constraints remain the same. Public debt, borrowing and debt-interest costs are all high. One in every £12 the government spends currently goes on debt interest.”

Higher borrowing costs threaten to increase the Government’s debt interest bill, which is already forecast to hit £111.2bn for the financial year - equivalent to 8.3pc of public spending.

Mr Burnham said he would announce a set of measures on Tuesday to give households “breathing space” to help with the cost of living.

“I will set out some of those measures starting tomorrow, including how we pay for them,” he said.

“We will help more young people into education... and we will build more council homes. That is the fair and sustainable way to bring the welfare bill down, to meet our fiscal rules and to honour our commitments on defence to our international partners.”

Mr Amis said: “Tomorrow we’re getting some cost of living news. [Burnham] said he was going to state where that funding’s come from. I think that’s key, any unfunded spending from here would get the market’s attention.”

News.title: India approves first dengue vaccine as cases surge in South Asia
News.content:
India has approved its first dengue vaccine as cases of the mosquito-borne disease surge in South Asia.

Japan’s Takeda Pharmaceutical’s dengue vaccine QDENGA has been approved by India’s drug regulator, the Centre Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO).

The global threat posed by dengue has been rising for years, as climate change, urbanisation and international travel aid the spread of the mosquitoes that transmit it.

The approval comes as hospitals across South Asia grapple with a surge in dengue infections.

In Sri Lanka, health authorities reported 2,652 new cases on Sunday alone, taking the total to 76,044 dengue cases so far this year. At least 53 people have died.

Bangladesh is also suffering a major outbreak with over 9,000 cases and 30 deaths that has piled pressure on its health system even as it battles a measles epidemic.

Dengue is transmitted to humans through the bites of infected Aedes mosquitoes.

Its symptoms include fever, severe muscle pain, and in severe cases, shock and internal bleeding that can be fatal.

Although mortality is relatively low, outbreaks place a substantial burden on health systems.

Takeda’s QDENGA jab is a live-attenuated tetravalent vaccine designed to protect against all four dengue virus serotypes. It can be given regardless of previous dengue infections.

“The approval comes at a critical time for public health, as reported dengue cases in India have increased 11-fold in the past two decades,” the company said in a statement.

Sports.title: Elliot Anderson takes huge dig at Man Utd as England World Cup star reveals why he joined Man City in £116m transfer
Sports.content:
ELLIOT ANDERSON believes he is joining the ‘Kings of Manchester’ after opting for a move to City – despite interest from United.

The Red Devils were tracking the England ace in recent months as Michael Carrick looked to revamp his midfield.



However it became clear the former Nottingham Forest man favoured a move to the Etihad and a £116million fee was agreed.

The deal was done during the World Cup but Anderson headed to the North West to officially signed his five year contract – worth around £300,000 per week.



Asked why he chose City, Anderson said: “They’re winners, they’re relentless. And that’s the sort of team I want to be a part of – champions and people who win trophies.

Anderson has signed a deal which keeps him at the Etihad until 2031 with the option of a further 12 months at the end of it.

He will get an early chance to see what he turned his back on when his new team-mates travel to Old Trafford on September 13.

Sports.title: Premier League owner reveals club’s entire transfer plans on Twitter in unprecedented move after ‘false rumours’
Sports.content:
HULL CITY owner Acun Ilicali has bizarrely taken to social media to clarify the club’s transfer business.

The Tigers are back in the Premier League for the first time in nine years and want to add to their squad this summer.



Hull have made three signings so far, bringing in defender Matt Targett, goalkeeper Jack Butland and midfielder Oscar Zambrano.

But Ilicali is “disturbed” and unhappy by media reports that Hull have been rejected for other targets.



The Hull owner therefore took the unique approach yesterday (THU) of posting a cryptic shortlist on social media of the club’s transfer targets.

Butland, Targett and Zambrano were all listed with a green tick by them, but underneath were 11 unnamed players.

Ilicali used flag emojis and percentages as clues for fans, with several matching of them players that Hull are after.

Target No4 was listed as a Japan flag with 99 per cent by it and is likely a nod to midfielder Hidemasa Morita being set to join as a free agent.

There was also a Greek flag that indicated a huge deal is “90%” done – and that is surely for Olympiacos’ highly-rated goalkeeper Konstantis Tzolakis, who SunSport understands is set to move to the MKM Stadium for £17m once his club find a new No1.

Posting on X, formerly known as Twitter, Ilicali wrote: “We are reading dozens of false transfer rumors in many places.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“We are disturbed by the claims that we have been rejected and by the use of our club’s name to gain attention.

“We have been working intensively for two months. I believe we will build a team that we will all be proud of.

“To prevent false speculation and to give you more information, I am leaving you with our latest transfer situation, which includes some clues.”

Sports.title: Topless Vinicius Jr’s girlfriend shows off tanlines while covering up in bed after World Cup star undergoes chin surgery
Sports.content:
BRAZILIAN influencer Virginia Fonseca has given fans another glimpse into her reunion with partner Vinicius Jr after sharing a cosy late-night update from bed.

The social media star, who boasts more than 56 million Instagram followers, posted a video to her Instagram Story tucked beneath a blue blanket while showing off the tan lines she picked up during her recent holiday with the Real Madrid superstar.



Virginia appeared makeup-free as she relaxed for the evening and wished her followers goodnight after spending time in Brazil.

She wrote alongside the clip: “Amo voce e ate daqui a pouco se Deus quiser,” which translates as: “I love you, and see you soon, God willing.”



That caption was accompanied by the words: “I’m already here, all ready to go to sleep. So, good night to you all. Sleep with God’s blessing. I love you all. Thank you for everything, always, and I’ll see you again very soon, God willing. Kiss.”

Earlier stories showed Virginia enjoying time in São Gonçalo – Vinicius Jr’s hometown in Rio de Janeiro – including snaps of the pair partying together.



The posts came after the couple appeared to rekindle their romance following a brief split before the World Cup.

Virginia had previously revealed they had gone their separate ways, but the pair have since been pictured together again, embracing as she officially opened a new gym.

Their reunion also comes after Vinicius underwent cosmetic surgery immediately following the World Cup, where Brazil‘s campaign ended in the last 16 following a 2-1 defeat to Norway.

The 26-year-old forward was pictured with dermatologist Dr Alessandro Alarcao after the procedure, with his chin appearing noticeably more defined than before.



While the exact cost of the treatment has not been disclosed, similar cosmetic procedures in the UK can range anywhere from around £3,000 to more than £14,000 depending on the type of surgery performed.

Vinicius joined Real Madrid from Flamengo in 2018 after progressing through the Brazilian club’s academy.

Since arriving in Spain, he has made 375 appearances for Los Blancos, scoring 128 goals and establishing himself as one of world football’s biggest stars.



He will now begin a new chapter under Jose Mourinho at Real Madrid, with the pair hoping to put behind them the controversy surrounding last season’s Champions League clash against Benfica.

During that tie, Benfica midfielder Gianluca Prestianni was accused of abusing Vinicius after the Brazilian scored a stunning winner in Lisbon, although the player was later handed a six-match ban for homophobic conduct after investigations concluded he allegedly used the Spanish slur “maricón” rather than the initially reported racist term.

Speaking after the match, Mourinho defended his own players while insisting Vinicius had played a part in the confrontation.

He said: “These talents are able to do these beautiful things, but unfortunately was not just happy to score that astonishing goal. When you score a goal like that, you celebrate in a respectful way.”

Now, with both back at Real Madrid, Mourinho and Vinicius will look to leave the controversy behind as they prepare for the new campaign, with the Portuguese coach aiming to recreate the success he enjoyed when he famously toppled Pep Guardiola’s Barcelona during the 2011/12 LaLiga season.

Sports.title: Christos Tzolis: How Arsenal's new £34m signing went from Norwich flop to Champions League star
Sports.content:
It says everything about the evolution of Christos Tzolis that Arsenal's newest signing accrued more goal contributions last year than he made league appearances across an ill-fated spell at Norwich City.

The reason Tzolis will play for the newly minted Premier League champions is because, at 24, he is now every inch the clinical, cold-blooded attacker that Europe's elite believed he would become back when he was a teenager. Barcelona were among his illustrious courters back then as heavyweights flocked to observe a prodigious talent. But it was Norwich, rather than Barcelona, who clinched the youngster's sought-after signature.

The Tzolis hype train was already in full flow when the formalities of his £8.8million transfer from PAOK was confirmed back in the summer of 2021. At 21, Tzolis was already a full Greece international; for a Norwich side who were back in the big-time after romping to the Championship title under Daniel Farke, the winger's capture had all the hallmarks of a transfer coup.

And yet, things deteriorated rapidly. After scoring twice in a 6-0 win over Bournemouth in the Carabao Cup on his debut, Tzolis soon fell out of favour. By early November, Tzolis had seen the manager who signed him sacked by the club, just hours after recording Norwich's first league win of the season.

‌



Dean Smith's appointment as Farke's successor proved to be the catalyst for the change of shape which effectively killed Tzolis' Norwich career.

Alex Scott transfer twist as Bournemouth star ‘keen’ on rivals amid Arsenal and Man Utd race READ MORE :

Arsenal respond to Morgan Rogers transfer snub as £34m signing flies in for medical READ MORE :

“It was the hardest year of my career,” Arsenal's newest attacker conceded to Het Nieuwsblad back in 2024. “The first time I didn’t play with the first team, but with the second [reserves], I was very disappointed. That was the lowest point of my career.

“My agent and my family had to convince me not to give up. And life off the pitch wasn’t easy back then.”

In total, Tzolis made just 27 appearances for Norwich before leaving the club permanently in the summer of 2024. The first of two loan spells designed to resurrect his career, with FC Twente, fell flat due to a knee injury. It was in the second tier of German football with Fortuna Dusseldorf that the youngster finally rediscovered his killer instinct, plundering more than 20 goals.

‌



From there, he never looked back. Unsurprisingly, Dusseldorf triggered their option to sign him permanently for just £3m. But it was Tzolis' next move which put the teen prodigy back on the path to superstardom.

Club Brugge swooped in to offer Dusseldorf the chance to effectively double their money instantly. They accepted and, in Belgium, Tzolis has flourished, accumulating more than 20 goals in successive seasons. Not only did he score 22 times last term, he registered a staggering 29 assists to break out as one of the biggest stars in the Belgian Pro League.

View 3 Images Christos Tzolis has transformed into a different player with Club Brugge (Image: JASPER JACOBS, BELGA MAG/AFP via Getty Images)

Tzolis returns to these shores not only hardened by the challenges of his stint in Norfolk, but brimming with confidence. Deadly with his right-foot, he has thrived in a left-sided attacking role and is viewed as the successor to the revered Leandro Trossard, who completed a move to Besiktas last week.

‌



Speaking to The Telegraph, Norwich's sporting director at the time Tzolis was signed, Stewart Webber, cites the physicality of the Premier League as one of the reasons behind the young attacker's failure to live up to expectations. “He was very young, coming into the hardest league in the world where the physicality is off the charts,” said Webber.

“It didn’t work out because we [Norwich] were a struggling team in an unforgiving division. Attacking players don’t get 100 touches of the ball when they are playing for Norwich. If he’d been at an Arsenal he would have probably been successful straight away.”

Tzolis returns to the Premier League a different beast. Naturally, he has grown physically and looks more robust than the twinkle-eyed teenager who was swatted aside both figuratively and literally at Norwich. The numbers he has put up consistently elsewhere in Europe, albeit at a level which is not elite, are eye-catching. His previous experience, although chastening, should give him some form of advantage when it comes to adapting to the rigours of Premier League life this time around.

“I’m a direct player, I go for goals or assists,” Tzolis told Arsenal’s website. “That’s my point of view as an attacker, as a winger. I’m always hungry to score or to give the final pass to my teammates. And I can say I work hard for the team, also in the defensive part.”

‌



View 3 Images Christos Tzolis struggled previously in the Premier League for Norwich City (Image: Ryan Pierse)

Arsenal went into the summer with designs on levelling up their attack, particularly on the left side. A deal for Morgan Rogers is now off the table, and Tzolis will not be the only acquisition in that area. Whereas at Tzolis organically became the main man at Brugge, his role at Arsenal will be significantly different.

There is, of course, the risk that Tzolis' exceptional record in Belgium does not translate to the Premier League. Even with the additional experience and nous under his belt.

In a transfer market where the Premier League's heavyweights have focused on domestic signings for inflated transfer fees this summer, the signing of Tzolis is somewhat of an outlier.

‌



But considering the transfer fee, the prospective upsides to the deal and the fact Arsenal are still after a ceiling-raiser signing for the left wing berth, you can see why signing Tzolis is a risk they feel is worth taking.

Sports.title: 'Kings of Manchester' - Elliot Anderson taunts Man Utd as City unveil £116m signing
Sports.content:
Elliot Anderson hasn't even kicked a ball in anger on behalf of the blue side of Manchester.

But the England superstar has guaranteed that most of the fury will belong to those on the red half, having pinned his colours well and truly to the Manchester City mast. Anderson snubbed Manchester United in favour of becoming City's most expensive signing in a £116m deal. And he's wasted no time in making it clear why he chose one neighbour over the other.

“I think they're winners. They're relentless - and that's the sort of team I want to be a part of," said Anderson. "Champions and people who win trophies. Over the last 10, 12 years, they've dominated, so that's why I wanted to join.

"For as long as I've known Manchester, City have been the kings of Manchester."

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Manchester United pull out of Alex Scott transfer race after learning asking price READ MORE :

Rodri to Real Madrid transfer truth as Man City contract stipulation revealed READ MORE :

Anderson’s comments will rile his new neighbours and echo the time when City taunted United with a giant ‘Welcome To Manchester’ poster depicting the face of Carlos Tevez, having lured the Argentine from Old Trafford in 2009.

United might have spent months attempting to land Anderson themselves, but the player insists Sir Jim Ratcliffe & Co were wasting their time.

Former United boss Sir Alex Ferguson once labelled City the ‘noisy neighbours’. But City have gone on to dominate the landscape of English football in the last decade.

‌



View 2 Images Carlos Tevez was welcomed to Man City in quite the fashion (Image: PA Archive/Press Association Images)

Anderson said: "Manchester City are one of the biggest clubs in the world and the squad they have is amazing - so strong in every position. As soon as I knew they wanted me, I was absolutely determined to make this move happen. As a footballer, you want to test yourself at the highest level. Being at City means I have that opportunity.

"From the outside looking in, City are a club that treats its players well and provides the perfect environment to excel. The success they have had, and the way they have played the game in the last 10 to 15 years has been extraordinary. It’s a privilege to be given the chance to be part of that."

Anderson's rise to the top has been rapid and phenomenal. In the space of four seasons he has gone from being on-loan with Bristol Rovers to helping England reach a World Cup semi final, via becoming the most expensive footballer in Britain.

‌



But taking the next step at club level is something Anderson is relishing, because he knows he has joined a machine made to be successful.

He said: "It's happened quite quick, but I think I always believed that I could get to this point - and this is where I want to be. Now that I'm here, I'll keep pushing and try to take this club forward.

"It's a club built to win trophies and compete at the very top of the game. That is exciting for any footballer. I'm so happy to have been given this opportunity, and I am determined to repay the faith City have shown in me."

‌



Anderson, 23, grew up marvelling at the influence Kevin De Bruyne once had on City and English football. And he admits now finding himself on the same team De Bruyne used to grace with such distinction, feels like a dream come true.

He said: "I think Kevin De Bruyne is someone who I've hugely looked up to over the past seven or eight years.

"I've always grown up through the academy at Newcastle. I've always wanted to play like him. I've watched him all the time, and to be sat here in the team that he was doing it for is so special."

Pep Guardiola might now be gone, but Anderson is relishing working under Enzo Maresca. Not to mention the chance to prove he is worth the nickname the 'Geordie Maradona', given to him by Rovers fans during his time in Bristol.

‌



He added: "They started that and it sort of stuck everywhere I've been. It's a really good one.

"It makes me happy when I hear it on the pitch and yeah, it gives me real confidence.

"I think I bring a bit of everything. I bring quality, I bring physicality, energy. I'd like to think I'd get them (City fans) excited, get them off their feet and bring energy to the team."

The Argentina FA have weighed in on conspiracy theory suggestions from their World Cup final defeat to Spain after Lionel Messi's pre-match speech

View 2 Images Argentina's FA president has hit out at conspiracy theory claims after his side were beaten by Spain in the World Cup final (Image: (Photo by Hannah Peters - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images))

Argentina FA president Claudio Tapia has dismissed World Cup final conspiracy theories and said Spain deserved to win. In the wake of last Sunday's showpiece clash, a significant amount of controversy over the result and what may have happened ahead of the game has come to light.

‌



Head coach Lionel Scaloni and captain Lionel Messi both hinted at something impacting the team moments before the final which has resulted in a number of conspiracy theories emerging. Argentina supporters have also furiously demanded that the final is replayed.

‌



However, Tapia has attempted to draw a line under the game in a clear statement. He began by stating: "Don't be fooled by lies. They were superior, they beat us fair and square...", before adding "you shouldn't be swayed by schemes that only seek to destabilise".

‌



Furious Argentina fans launch petition to replay 'corrupt' Spain World Cup final READ MORE :

Norway to make formal Donald Trump complaint over 'serious' breach of World Cup rules READ MORE :

Ferran Torres grabbed the only goal of the game in extra-time but it was the ugly post-match scenes that stole the headlines with Leandro Parades, Nahuel Molina and assistant coach Roberto Ayala all captured appearing to punch Spain players. Tapia has also subtly seemed to hit out against that before praising the efforts of the nation.

His full statement read: "In sports, you also learn by accepting defeats with the same grace with which you celebrate victories. Yes, we lost a final. But it's also true that this group had just brought immense joy to the country. Argentina had celebrated a match earlier because this team once again demonstrated why it means so much to our people.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



"Losing hurts. It hurts because we are competitive, because we are the most successful team in history, and because second place is never enough for us. It hurts because we are used to fighting until the end and because we continue to be one of the two best teams in the world.

"But let's stop for a moment. Let's think about the sacrifice of these players, the coaching staff, and every person who worked for more than 50 days away from their families, with a single objective: to represent Argentina in the best way possible. We are Argentinians.

View 2 Images Lionel Messi was in tears after Argentina lost the World Cup final to Spain

‌



"We compete with grit, with passion, and with heart. We give everything in every training session and every match. We also represent all of the Americas with enormous pride. We defend our colours Our flag and our country on every pitch in the world.

"That's why you shouldn't be swayed by lies or by schemes that only seek to destabilize. Enough of trying to turn against those who have given so much to our football. Today is a time to give thanks, to support, and to recognize these players who once again gave their all for the shirt. Schemes come and go.

"The commitment, the work, and the heart of our National Team remain forever. There are no excuses here. Here, we play football. And this National Team will continue to represent Argentina with the same pride as always."

Sports.title: Ex-England star's son goes full Sol Campbell by leaving Tottenham for Arsenal
Sports.content:
Ex-England star's son goes full Sol Campbell by leaving Tottenham for Arsenal

Arsenal have prised away one of Tottenham's young talents and confirmed the signing of an 18-year-old defender, following in his father's footsteps

View 2 Images Sol Campbell caused uproar when moving from Tottenham to Arsenal (Image: Jamie McDonald/ALLSPORT)

Elijah Upson, son of former England international Matthew, has joined Arsenal from Tottenham. The Gunners have landed the 18-year-old after the defender chose not to sign professional terms with the Lilywhites.

‌



Upson's move sees him join Arsenal at the same age as his father. Upson Sr arrived at Highbury from Luton Town and spent six years at the club before moving to Birmingham City, following loans at Nottingham Forest, Crystal Palace and Reading.

‌



The youngster makes the controversial move across London 25 years after the most significant move across north London when Sol Campbell made the switch. Campbell came through the ranks at Tottenham before crossing the north London divide after more than a decade with the club.

‌



Alex Scott transfer twist as Bournemouth star ‘keen’ on rivals amid Arsenal and Man Utd race READ MORE :

Arsenal issue statement and confirm extent of worrying William Saliba injury problem READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

The 73-cap England international joined Arsene Wenger's side on a free transfer after being expected to extend his stay at White Hart Lane. Confirmation of Campbell's move came in a shock press conference as Tottenham fans ultimately labelled him Judas.

Upson's move is unlikely to cause as much controversy as he looks to make his name in football. The teenager was drawn to the environment Arsenal offered to aid his development.

‌



"It's a great feeling, really proud to be here," Upson said. "[It's] really nice to have all my family and everyone around it, it's been a great experience.

"My dad signed here around the same time as me, it's great to have someone with a good experience of the place. But at the same time, I'm definitely looking forward to building my own reputation and getting started.

"When I met the guys here recently and met all the team and staff, it just seemed like a really nice environment. That was probably the biggest factor, an environment where you feel you can hopefully learn and get better as a person."

‌



View 2 Images Elijah Upson has moved across north London (Image: David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

The pathway created by the likes of Bukayo Saka and Myles Lewis-Skelly in recent years was also a motivating factor behind the transfer. "That was also one of the big reasons for my decision," he said.

"Obviously, great exposure to some of these great players that have had a great season here and some real top quality. I'm excited to hopefully be around and work with these people.

Article continues below

"I think definitely the centre-back partnership in the first team that there is between Saliba and Gabriel, they're a good inspiration and really experienced, high quality players. They've had a great season, definitely two players that I'm really keen to learn from and expose myself to hopefully."

Sports.title: FA release statement after video of England team-mates fighting goes viral
Sports.content:
FA release statement after video of England team-mates fighting goes viral

A shocking clip showing two England Under-16 footballers violently fighting each other in a hotel room has gone viral on social media, forcing the FA to issue a statement in response

View Image The two England players were filmed fighting

The Football Association has been forced to release a statement after a video of young England players fighting in a hotel room went viral on social media.

‌



A 58-second clip showing two boys fighting while being filmed and encouraged by their team-mates surfaced on Wednesday. The violent brawl, in which punches and kicks are thrown, is made all the more shocking by the official England-branded clothing the boys are wearing.

‌



One version of the video has been viewed 12.4million times since being posted online on Wednesday. In the footage, one boy pushes the other into a bed while holding his neck before throwing punches.

‌



The aggressor is kicked off and the fighting continues stood up, with one getting the other in a headlock. The fighting is encouraged by those watching, with "f*** him up", "shut the door" and laughing heard.

Furious Argentina fans launch petition to replay 'corrupt' Spain World Cup final READ MORE :

Norway to make formal Donald Trump complaint over 'serious' breach of World Cup rules READ MORE :

The FA has now confirmed that the clip is genuine and shows players from the England Under-16s side. "We were made aware of an internal matter during an Under-16s camp in October 2025," an FA spokesperson said. "This was quickly resolved at the time."

‌



The clip has provoked widespread criticism, with many comments surprised that none of the others in the room tried to intervene.

England's U16s travelled to Turkey to play Turkey, Wales and Portugal in October and November last year. They are coached by Barry Lewtas, who previously spent 12 years working in Liverpool's academy.
