Sports.title: Manchester United pull out of Alex Scott transfer race after learning asking price
Sports.content:
Manchester United pull out of Alex Scott transfer race after learning asking price

Manchester United had been keen on Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott who has impressed with the Cherries and is being tipped for a big-money summer move

View Image Alex Scott of Bournemouth during a pre-season training session (Image: 2026 AFC Bournemouth)

Manchester United have been priced out of a move for England and Bournemouth star Alex Scott.

‌



United valued Scott in the £40m bracket, due to the fact he has still to win his first full England cap and hasn't played in the Champions League. But the Cherries are holding out for in excess of £70m for one of their prize assets.

‌



United are not prepared to meet the asking price - and will continue to look at alternative targets instead. Paving the way for top flight rivals Arsenal to land the midfielder, should they be able to agree a fee. It's understood Scott's representatives have held talks with several clubs, and that he will make a decision on his future in the next fortnight.

‌



Scott is said to favour a move to the Emirates, but is worried about how much game time he will get for Mikel Arteta's English champions. The 22-year-old has emerged as one of the brightest midfield talents in English football.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Rodri to Real Madrid transfer truth as Man City contract stipulation revealed READ MORE :

Norway to make formal Donald Trump complaint over 'serious' breach of World Cup rules READ MORE :

He was instrumental in helping the Cherries secure European football last season.

Scott was also named in Thomas Tuchel's England squad for games against Serbia and Albania last season, but didn't make an appearance. He was then asked to join Tuchel's men for their preparation camp in Florida ahead of the World Cup.

United have strengthened midfield with the signings of Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos in recent weeks.

Article continues below

Michael Carrick is still keen to add a third in this area, but United are not prepared to get into a bidding war with Arsenal over Scott.

Sports.title: Aston Villa confirm signing of Alejandro Garnacho with £43m Chelsea clause
Sports.content:
Aston Villa confirm signing of Alejandro Garnacho with £43m Chelsea clause

Chelsea have sent Alejandro Garnacho to Aston Villa ahead of this coming Premier League season, less than 12 months after signing the Argentina international from Manchester United

View 2 Images Alejandro Garnacho will spent this coming season on loan at Aston Villa (Image: Getty Images)

Aston Villa have announced the signing of Alejandro Garnacho on a season-long loan from Chelsea. Their deal includes a £43million conditional obligation to buy clause based on how many appearances the Argentina international makes.

‌



Garnacho, 22, moves on from the Blues less than 12 months after they spent £40million on signing him from Manchester United. They stand to benefit from a 10% sell-on clause should the move become permanent, with Chelsea believing that the conditions to do so are easily reachable.

‌



The winger made 43 appearances for them last season. However, just over half of those were from the start.

‌



Alex Scott transfer twist as Bournemouth star ‘keen’ on rivals amid Arsenal and Man Utd race READ MORE :

Maghnes Akliouche's transfer intention clear as Liverpool approach for star confirmed READ MORE :

Villa have form when it comes to these types of deals, with Harvey Elliott's loan from Liverpool not becoming permanent last season. They had an obligation to sign the England international for £35million obligation if he made ten appearances across all competitions, and only played him nine times.

Chelsea, too, have previously avoided having to sign a loanee permanently. They paid United a £5 million penalty fee 12 months ago so that they did not have to keep Jadon Sancho.

The winger went on to join Villa on loan last season. Garnacho now effectively replaces his former team-mate in Birmingham.

‌



View 2 Images Alejandro Garnacho spent less than a year at Chelsea (Image: John Walton/PA Wire)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

That succession of former United wingers joining Villa on loan goes back even further. Marcus Rashford spent the second half of the 2024/25 season under Unai Emery.

‌



Garnacho will hope the move works out more like Rashford's spell, rather than Sancho's. Rashford managed to get a move to Barcelona off the back of his time at Villa Park.

Sancho, meanwhile, is still without a club after his United contract expired at the end of last season. There is no such end in sight for Chelsea if Garnacho does not stay at Villa, with six years still left on his deal.

Emery has said in Villa's statement announcing the move: "We are delighted with Alejandro. He is so talented, young and he showed us his wish to help our project. We are really happy."

Article continues below

Villa teased the move on social media by saying: "We already knew claret and blue looked good on him…" That appears to be a reference to when Garnacho wore a Villa shirt with Rashford's name and number on the back last year.

Sports.title: Russell relieved as Mercedes resolve engine issues amid 'toughest psychological' battle
Sports.content:
George Russell is optimistic Mercedes have identified and resolved the glitches that have afflicted his car's power unit ahead of this weekend's Hungarian Grand Prix.

Russell slipped 50 points behind title-leading team-mate Kimi Antonelli last weekend at Spa-Francorchamps after making a lap-one exit from the race following contact from Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton.

However, the Briton felt that the race-ending collision, and his difficult weekend relative to an on-form Antonelli as a whole, had been heavily influenced by energy-deployment problems with his engine.

Russell had experienced one straight-line speed glitch over the event's first two days, hurting his car's performance at the end of the long Spa lap, while his race start was hampered by a separate issue which impacted all Mercedes-powered runners.

But Russell is hopeful Mercedes have managed to get to the bottom of what went wrong and, crucially, managed to resolve the issues ahead of the final race before F1's summer break this weekend.

"We're pretty confident we've got on top of the issues that we had in Spa and it should be easy to resolve," he said.

"We hope and we think we have got on top of it, so feeling more positive.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes driver George Russell spins after contact with Lewis Hamilton and his race ends on the opening lap, but was the Ferrari driver's penalty fair?

"At the time we were not sure what it was but the team have worked so hard to really dig deep.

"I think Spa gave us the right clues where we needed to look and it's only really when you look deep into the right place that you find the problem. Fingers crossed we hope the issue with the power unit has been resolved, but we'll find out this weekend."

Asked to clarify whether it had been anything to with the way he had been driving the W17, having initially worked through different approaches to tackling the sweeping Belgian lap in practice, Russell said: "We think it was a software bug. It wasn't the driving style that was contributing to the loss of power, so that's something at least.

"I think Spa gave us the right pointers of where to look for the problem. It's like getting a needle out of a haystack really and suddenly when you know where you've got to look maybe the problem you can find and I think we have.

"Time will tell but it wasn't an easy couple of weeks."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player David Croft questions whether George Russell can still win the world championship after he was forced to retire in Belgium, while Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli went on to win the race

'It is the toughest psychological battle I've had' - Russell opens up on 2026 ups and downs

Russell described his season, in which he started as the clear favourite for the world title, as an "emotional rollercoaster", amid inconsistency in his own form and some costly Mercedes reliability problems.

Asked if it had all contributed to the toughest psychological battle he had faced in his career on track to date, the 28-year-old said: "Yeah, I think it's probably fair to say it is the toughest psychological battle I've had just because it's been so many ups and downs, combined with things in my control that haven't been great and also with things outside of my control that have hampered progress and progression.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Craig Slater discusses the biggest talking points off the back of the Belgian Grand Prix, including if the title chase has been blown for George Russell

"But what doesn't kill you makes you stronger and I sort of feel proud of my resilience and three days later here at Spa I feel positive and excited for the weekend and I'm looking at the future prospects and not the past disappointment.

"I guess that's the good thing with racing, you've often got another opportunity just round the corner."

That next opportunity is the Hungaroring, where Russell has twice finished on the podium and claimed a first career pole position in 2022.

The Briton is aiming to regain the improved form he believes he had been showing when he won the Austrian Grand Prix three races ago.

"I felt some good momentum coming out of Austria and Barcelona, especially after Monaco," said Russell.

"Monaco was a very low point for me in my season and coming back in Barcelona, getting the pole, the P2 [in the race], getting the pole in Austria and getting the win, I felt a real good momentum building, which was halted in Silverstone and Spa.

"I hope I can continue from where we were in Austria."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch from onboard with George Russell as he crashes out of the Belgian GP after contact with Lewis Hamilton.

He added: I'm just looking forward to coming into Budapest. It's a circuit I like. It's going to be a real challenging weekend.

"We know it's one of the least power-sensitive circuits of the season. We've got Ferrari close behind. They have a better chassis than power unit at the moment, so of all of the circuits, you can expect them to be competitive here.

"Of course, Kimi's performing super well every single race weekend, so it's not going to be a straightforward weekend, but I'm excited for it."

He also insisted that nothing was lost yet in the race for 2026's world title.

"For sure [I can still win it]," added Russell.

"We're not even halfway through yet. It's just been so up and down this whole season. Four races ago I was a lot more points behind in the championship than I am right now even with the disappointments of Spa.

"So I am feeling a lot more positive, excited for the weekend ahead and hopefully now I can just focus on driving quick."

Sports.title: Hamilton: I really believe we can fight for 2026 title
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton says he 'really believes' Ferrari can enable him to fight for an eighth world championship title this season.

Hamilton is second in the standings, 45 points behind Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli going into this weekend's Hungarian Grand Prix - the 11th of the season's 22 currently-scheduled rounds.

It's the first time Hamilton has been in title contention since he was contentiously edged out by Max Verstappen in 2021, and the 41-year-old says he is loving being back in the mix.

"It's amazing," said Hamilton, who has impressed in 2026 following a difficult first campaign with Ferrari.

"It's a great feeling, especially when you look at the contrast of where we were last year here.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ahead of the British Grand Prix, Lewis Hamilton reveals he "won't stop" until he claims an eighth World Drivers' Championship.

"I'm really proud of the team for the curve and step we have taken collectively and I have to always acknowledge my own efforts and the work I've put in and the changes I've made to enable us to be where we are and I'm really proud of myself for that.

"There's still a lot of work to do and still a mountain to climb ahead of us on the second half of the season but I'm more focused than ever and I really believe we can fight."

Despite Antonelli's superb form, Hamilton is insisting that the Hungarian Grand Prix, the final race before the sport's summer break, is not make or break for his hopes of chasing down the 19-year-old Italian.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton claimed his first win in red at the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix

"We are continuing to develop, we are continuing to push," Hamilton said. "There's still a long way to go. I don't see this one or the next one as a break point. I don't know when it becomes the break point, if there is a break point.

"This is just the time for us to continue to hammer down and continue to double down on our development and continue to push.

"We have had two wins as a team, plenty of podiums - we are right there on their (Mercedes') tails and I think we are now able to compete with them more consistently for victories, which I think is positive."

'Mercedes still the car to beat in Hungary'

Ferrari have been touted by some as favourites at the Hungaroring due to an expectation the characteristics of their car will be suited to the circuit.

Ferrari have generally been unable to match the performance of the Mercedes power unit, but the high number of slow corners in Budapest should theoretically make the deficiency less of an issue.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton claims Sprint Pole at the British Grand Prix!

Despite that, Hamilton is taking nothing for granted, and insists Mercedes remain the 'car to beat'.

"I don't want to make assumptions," Hamilton said. "The last couple races, ultimately we should have won the last two races if we perfected the weekend. The car was able to have won.

"In Spa we were more competitive than we thought and I missed something on that weekend and that's not what I want to do this weekend.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Relive Lewis Hamilton winning a record EIGHTH Hungarian Grand Prix back in 2020

"We have got a car that can compete. I think Mercedes still have the car to beat, naturally, as they have won the most and they won't be easy to beat this weekend.

"But we have made subtle progress and hopefully can fight with them this weekend."

Sports.title: Domestic abuse reports reach record UK highs during 2026 World Cup
Sports.content:
The 2026 World Cup led to a rise in domestic abuse reports; in total, 2,322 incidents were reported to police, with domestic violence incidents making up 17 per cent; 93 per cent of reports occurred around England matches

Domestic abuse reports reached record highs in the UK during the 2026 World Cup, figures have shown.

In total, 384 domestic violence incidents were reported during the tournament - representing 17 per cent of the 2,322 incidents reported.

Ninety-three per cent occurred around England's matches and only Euro 2020 (held in 2021) recorded more.

The rise has been described as a worrying increase, with alcohol once again viewed as the lead contributing factor.

"The vast majority of it [incidents] we'd say were alcohol related and that's a real concern," Chief Constable Mark Roberts, the Football Policing National Lead in charge of policing football in the UK, told Sky Sports News.

"Increases in domestic abuse, increases in incidents around licensed premises. I think that's the thing that we've seen in a number of tournaments now and that's really going to be a focus for us as we go forward planning future tournaments."

The change of licensing hours just 48 hours before the kick-off of the Mexico vs England game was a particular cause for concern.

"We knew the fixtures from December," Roberts added. "It was pretty straightforward to map out the routes and potential hinge points with the engagements with Mexico and I just think that particular example where the licensing laws were extended in effect on the Friday before a fixture on the Sunday, that doesn't give us any chance to re-roster officers.

"Yes we accept the difficulties, but for myself, I made our representations to the government to say: 'Look, there's a perfectly adequate system here. We've got plenty of notices before fixtures, stick with the system'.

"Places can make an application if they're well run and no doubt they'll get the extension that they're after, but it just meant we couldn't limit it in particular areas so I think that was frustrating. If you know a fixture is potentially going to happen for seven months, we've got to do better than changing the law 48 hours before a game."

Second-highest levels of online hate incidents recorded

Elsewhere, online hate crime saw 293 incidents, which is is the second-highest recorded after Euro 2020 where police dealt with 393 online hate crimes. With online hate, police saw 750 referrals relating to England matches. All were reviewed, with 293 reaching the threshold for online hate crimes and prosecution.

Although the numbers are still being analysed, police believe a large proportion came from outside the UK.

Roberts said: "Some of this stuff is vile, it's unpleasant, but doesn't meet the legal threshold, but grossly offensive. So, we will identify those which meet the legal threshold.

"If we can identify the offender and they're based in the UK, UKFPU will send it to the [local] force and they will do the prosecution. At the recent Women's Euros, where the team was successful, there was the abuse of Jess Carter where we successfully prosecuted people.

"So, the process works. The difficulty is if it is from abroad as we're then dependent on foreign law enforcement to deal with it. Obviously there's different laws in different places and no one does it like we do it. There's no other law enforcement in any other country that takes it seriously. That deals with it, either for their own people or when we give reports across.

"We will encourage people to work with us and support and prosecute people abroad, but certainly in this country if we identify them they will be prosecuted."

Figures to help planning for Euro 2028

The 2026 World Cup data will aid the huge police planning process that is already under way for Euro 2028, which is being co-hosted by England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland.

Roberts said: "I think the key thing for us now is identifying things that we need to fix first so licensing will be an example. We need to be really clear and have a policy in place. In terms of the event itself, I think it will be fantastic. It will be an incredible spectacle."

He continued: "The world in two years will be different to what it is now so we need to stay alive to what those threats are; the geopolitical situations. We need to do the intelligence gathering to understand what threats come from other countries in the same way that we would always stress when our teams go abroad. Treat them on behaviour, not reputation.

"We need to understand the fans of some of the visiting countries are a lot more problematic than the fans here. So, we need to have those plans in place to be able to deal with them effectively. Whether that starts from not letting them in the country in the first place to managing them to make sure we've got processes in place.

"Each of the host cities needs to be really clear on their events, who is responsible for the ownership, what the licensing policies are locally. So, it's really working through all those things that we see as a potential threat, and making sure there's a plan in place."

Chief Constable happy with 'exemplary' travelling supporters

While issues in the UK continue to be analysed, Roberts was pleased with the behaviour of those who travelled over to the United States, Mexico and Canada for the World Cup.

Figures released by the Football Policing Unit reveal that just 22 police 'actions' occurred at the World Cup involving England supporters. It is a rise on the previous World Cup in Qatar where there were zero 'actions' and on the three in Russia in 2018.

But, given an estimated figure well in excess of 100,000 England fans attended games this year compared with 7,000 in Qatar and 5,000 in Russia, it has earned praise from the UK's top football police officer.

"I think the fans who travelled out there, almost exclusive, were an absolute credit," Roberts said.

"They enjoyed it. The support of the team was fantastic. I don't think anyone will ever forget the scenes of 'Wonderwall' with the fans and the players singing it. So, I think that behaviour was really good as expected. That was a real positive."

Particular praise related to the Mexico vs England last-16 fixture at the Azteca where police saw and heard from the Football Supporters' Association and England fans about the camaraderie between the two sets of supporters, including multiple examples of Mexican fans congratulating and wishing England good luck inside and outside the stadium.

The 22 police actions broke down into incidents of public order offences, unauthorised entry, assault, touting, intoxication, ejection and one case of sexual battery which after review did not necessitate prosecution. Alcohol was the contributing factor in the majority of the incidents.

Sports.title: 'Kings of Manchester' - Anderson sends Man Utd message after City move sealed
Sports.content:
Elliot Anderson has declared Manchester City the "kings of Manchester" after completing his £116m move from Nottingham Forest.

The England midfielder has signed a five-year contract at the Etihad Stadium with the option of a further 12 months.

The deal was agreed earlier this month but finalised this week following the player's return from the World Cup after helping the Three Lions to a third-place finish.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' Dave Reed assesses whether £100m-plus deals are becoming the new norm in the transfer market

Anderson said he was "over the moon" to be signing for "one of the biggest clubs in the world" and has his sights firmly set on winning trophies.

"I can't wait to play for this club," the 23-year-old said. "It's a club built to win trophies and compete at the very top of the game. That is exciting for any footballer.

"I think they're winners, they're relentless, and that's the sort of team I want to be a part of. Over the last 10, 12 years, they've dominated, so that's why I wanted to join."

The midfielder is already relishing the prospect of playing in the Manchester derby, with City due to face arch-rivals Manchester United at Old Trafford on September 13, live on Sky Sports.

Anderson, who was a Man Utd target this summer, said: "It's one of the biggest derbies in the world and for as long as I've known Manchester, City have been the kings of Manchester.

"It'll be a great fixture, and I can't wait to be involved in something like that."

'There's more to come from me'

Image: Anderson has signed a five-year deal at Man City

Anderson came through the youth ranks at Newcastle and made 55 first-team appearances for his boyhood club. Early in his career he also enjoyed a successful loan at Bristol Rovers, where he earned the nickname 'Geordie Maradona'.

He joined Forest in a £35m deal two years ago and played 92 times for the Reds. He earned his first England call-up last season and quickly established himself as a key member of Thomas Tuchel's side.

"I'm only 23, so I've got plenty of time to get to my best levels," he said. "I'm definitely not there yet and there's more to come from me.

"I think I bring a bit of everything. I bring quality, I bring physicality, energy. I'd like to think I'd get the fans excited, get them off their feet and bring energy to the team."

Anderson reveals admiration for De Bruyne

Image: Anderson signs his City deal alongside their transfer chief Hugo Viana

There is extra significance in the move for Anderson, as he grew up idolising former City star Kevin De Bruyne.

He said: "I think Kevin De Bruyne is someone who I've hugely looked up to over the past seven or eight years.

"I've always wanted to play like him. I've watched him all the time and to be sat here in the team that he was doing it for is so special."

Anderson is now enjoying a summer break and will link up with new manager Enzo Maresca's squad for pre-season training next month.

Director of football Hugo Viana said: "Elliot is one of the outstanding young midfield talents in world football. We feel he can become a complete midfielder."

Sports.title: Rangers confirm Dragojevic signing as seventh summer arrival
Sports.content:
Rangers have signed midfielder Vanja Dragojevic on an initial four-year deal.

The 20-year-old becomes the Ibrox club's seventh summer signing as new manager Derek McInnes rebuilds his squad ahead of the new season.

There is a 12-month option to extend the player's deal, as Dragojevic arrives from Partizan Belgrade for a fee in excess of £4m.

He was club captain at the Serbian side and was rated as one of the best defensive midfielders in the league, plus has two caps for his national team.

Alongside Cammy Devlin and Dan Neil, he is the third midfielder to join the club, in addition to other summer signings Lawrence Shankland, Ross McCrorie, Ben Godfrey and Ivor Pandur.

Image: Dan Neil is among the other midfielders to join Rangers this summer

Rangers had been in talks over a move for Tromso's Jens Hjertø-Dahl too, but have prioritised the move for Dragojevic.

He said: "It feels amazing, and I'm really happy and proud to be part of such a big club like Rangers.

"It's a big opportunity and I can't wait to get started.

"I first heard [the interest] three months ago, and when I heard it I already knew it was very interesting to me because I think the winning mentality that Rangers have is compatible with my mentality."

Image: Derek McInnes is hopeful of more signings ahead of the club's Premiership opener at Dundee Utd next Friday

McInnes added: "We are really excited to bring Vanja on board.

"He's got huge potential, really exciting attributes, and boasts the character to play in this environment. To captain a club the size of FK Partizan at such a young age tells you everything you need to know about the respect he commands and the leadership qualities he already possesses.

"I believe he will add a lot to our group, and I look forward to working with him in the years ahead."

Sports.title: Rodri to undergo back surgery and may miss start of Premier League season
Sports.content:
Manchester City's World Cup winner Rodri is to undergo minor surgery on his back, which means he may miss the start of the Premier League season.

The midfielder captained Spain in the World Cup final win over Argentina on Sunday and won the Golden Ball as player of the tournament. However, Sky Sports News understands the 30-year-old now needs a back issue addressed.

Rodri was not expected to be involved in the Community Shield against Arsenal following his exploits for Spain at the World Cup, but he is now a doubt for City's Premier League opener against Bournemouth on Sunday August 23, live on Sky Sports.

City are then due to face Crystal Palace (away), Coventry (home), Man Utd (away) and Sunderland (home) before the September international break.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player With the World Cup now over, which players are the standout contenders to win the Ballon D'or?

The news comes after an injury-hit couple of years for the 2024 Ballon d'Or winner. An anterior cruciate ligament injury in September 2024 led to Rodri featuring in just three Premier League matches in 2024/25, while further injury issues limited him to 21 top-flight outings last term.

Rodri has one year left on his City contract and has been linked with a transfer to Real Madrid. New City boss Enzo Maresca and the club want to keep him and want him to sign a new contract.

Reflecting on the challenges he had to overcome to achieve success with Spain this summer, Rodri said he hoped to be an inspiration and paid tribute to his own resilience.

"We're a bit shocked right now, even myself," Rodri told Fox Sports. "I cannot express with words. I think now we're like in a cloud but, for me, it's been a very tough time.

"I just want the new generations to see my example as an opportunity. When you go down, you can rise again. This is my philosophy for my entire life.

Image: Spain's Rodri and Argentina's Lionel Messi in action in the World Cup final

"Of course, sometimes things go well, things go wrong, but always the positiveness.

"I said to the lads before the game, 'we have to go for the game'. We need to face them, we have to look to their eyes. We want this game. And then life gives you the World Cup or not, but we were brave and I was brave in that moment I was down, so I want to thank all the people that helped me.

"But I want to thank myself, to be honest, in those moments."

Sports.title: Why Villa could offer Garnacho the perfect route to redemption
Sports.content:
At the age of just 22, Alejandro Garnacho's career is at a crossroads, but his move to Aston Villa, driven by Unai Emery, offers the perfect chance to get it back on track.

Despite his age, the initial loan move, with an obligation to make the switch permanent if certain conditions are met, could represent a make-or-break moment in the career of the Argentina international.

After missing out on the World Cup this summer and failing to make his mark among a congested Chelsea squad, Villa and Emery have stepped forward to offer a route to redemption, with a proven track record of polishing diamonds in the rough.

Here, Sky Sports analyses why it could be the perfect environment for Garnacho to finally flourish.

Garnacho's short but turbulent career thus far

So far, in his short but underwhelming career after scoring just 17 goals in 117 Premier League appearances, no manager has been able to harness his perceived potential.

Ralf Rangnick gave him his senior debut for Manchester United at just 17 and quickly urged him to "keep his feet on the ground" to deliver on his promise.

Erik ten Hag provided regular first-team opportunities to spark a frenzy over his potential but called for consistency and hard work to unlock the "X-factor" he showed in flashes.

Ruud van Nistelrooy's brief spell as interim boss at United had a short but profound impact on Garnacho. During his four games in charge, he left the starting line-up only once for rest, while scoring two goals and adding one assist.

Then came Ruben Amorim - and like his reign, the relationship was rocky. After being omitted from the group by the former United boss, his exit was sanctioned in a £40m move to Chelsea, with Garnacho describing the end to his career at Old Trafford as a "bad moment in life".

Image: Ruben Amorim gives instructions to Garnacho during his spell at Man Utd

Enzo Maresca said he needed time to adapt while Liam Rosenior cited his age but promised to help him get "to the top". New Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso wants to build a "strong culture" - and Garnacho is not part of those plans.

The exit door has been opened at Stamford Bridge just under a year after joining and it is Emery who has stepped forward to take the challenge on.
