The Villa boss is a long-term admirer of the forward and Sky Sports News reported the club's early interest in Garnacho last summer, but they were unable to meet United's asking price to sign him at the time.

Now, after 12 goal involvements in 43 appearances across all competitions for Chelsea, he makes the switch to Villa in yet another twist to a career that has been plagued by upheaval.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on the Transfer Talk Podcast, Henry Winter discusses why Aston Villa should be wary of Garnacho

Will Emery unlock Garnacho's potential?

A difficult question to answer but an early prerequisite will be that it will take two to tango. Questions have been raised regarding Garnacho's attitude, training levels and application in games throughout his career.

That will be quickly stamped out under the meticulous eye and guidance of Emery. Fresh faces have to earn his respect and trust, as Donyell Malen, Tammy Abraham, Evann Guessand, Harvey Elliott and Jadon Sancho all discovered relatively quickly.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A look back at Garnacho's top five Premier League goals

Training and preparations are rigorous. If an opportunity is not earned, it is simply not given.

Before leaving United, Garnacho sparked controversy when pictured wearing a Villa shirt with Rashford's name on the back, while also admitting he did "bad things" during his final six months at the club.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Garnacho opens up on his Manchester United exit, admitting he could have done things differently during his last six months before moving to Chelsea

Since Rashford worked with Emery in the 'Second City', he has gone on to play for Barcelona and was reintegrated into the England set-up, being named in Thomas Tuchel's squad at the World Cup.

The opportunity and tools for Garnacho to have a similar redemption arc will be there. It is up to the player himself to take them.

Where will Garnacho fit at Villa?

It will be a new-look Villa side for the 2026/27 campaign following Morgan Rogers' exit to Chelsea for £117m and Youri Tielemans' £35m move to United.

Villa have worked quickly and diligently in the window to acquire Johan Manzambi and Joao Gomes - and Garnacho is the latest recruit to bolster Emery's options going forward.

The exit of Rogers provides readily available minutes on the left wing for the new arrival. While he did not always explicitly start in the role, he occupied the spaces and Garnacho will now be one of the players tasked with filling the gap in output that his exit has created.

When at his very best, he offers something that Villa have lacked for some time now. Genuine width with his preference to hug the touchline, paired with a degree of pace that Emery's squad is not blessed with, and a fearlessness to drive at defenders.

In limited minutes within a congested squad at Stamford Bridge last season, Garnacho averaged more carries than any other player for Villa or Chelsea per game (11.9), as well as leading the way in chances created from those drives (1.35).

Garnacho ranks third in the league for the latter statistic, with only Manchester City's Jeremy Doku and Brighton's Brajan Gruda creating more from those scenarios each game.

Another important factor to note is that, unlike other stops in his career, Garnacho will have stable support at Villa. Since Emery was appointed in October 2022, the young forward has been overseen by seven different permanent bosses and six interim appointments.

Villa are entering a new era but Emery is ever-present. A calm figurehead to learn from who is well-versed in navigating difficult situations and getting the very best out of players.

Garnacho now has the guidance and opportunity to become a cornerstone of this new-look side, away from the focus clubs like Chelsea and United garner, but ultimately the onus will fall on the player himself.

Sports.title: Elliot Anderson lauds City as ‘kings of Manchester’ after £116m Forest transfer
Sports.content:
Elliot Anderson has called Manchester City the “kings of Manchester” after completing his £116m move to the club from Nottingham Forest.

The 23-year-old was a key part of England’s third-place finish at the World Cup, having been an ever-present for Forest in the Premier League last season. Before Morgan Rogers’ £117m transfer to Chelsea from Aston Villa on Tuesday, Anderson’s fee was the record for a British player.

The midfielder is taking a three-week break after his exploits in North America but is clearly relishing the prospect of playing for City, picking out the first Manchester derby of the new season on 13 September as a standout fixture. He may well be in line for a hot reception from the Old Trafford faithful given his claims about City’s superior status.

“It’s one of the biggest derbies in the world and for as long as I’ve known Manchester, City have been the kings of Manchester,” Anderson said in an interview on City’s website. “It’ll be a great fixture and I can’t wait to be involved in something like that.

“They’re winners, they’re relentless, and that’s the sort of team I want to be a part of – champions and people who win trophies,” Anderson said of his reason for signing for City.

“Over the last 10, 12 years, they’ve dominated, so that’s why I wanted to join. It’s happened quite quick, but I think I always believed I could get to this point and this is where I want to be. Now that I’m here, I’ll keep pushing and try to take this club forward.” Anderson’s rise has been rapid, with his England debut coming as recently as last September, in a 2-0 victory over Andorra.

The Tyneside-born player, who began his career at Newcastle before joining Forest for £35m in July 2024, believes there is much more to come. “I’m only 23, so I’ve got plenty of time to get to my best levels and I definitely think I’m not there yet,” he said.

The deal was agreed three weeks ago but finalised this week after the player’s return from the World Cup. Anderson has signed until 2031 and is City’s first major signing since Enzo Maresca succeeded Pep Guardiola as manager. He is looking forward to working with the Italian. “I’ve watched his teams over the past couple of years and spoke to a few of the lads from Chelsea and they all rate him very highly,” Anderson said.

“I like to be intense when I play and use lots of energy around the pitch and get the fans going. So, I think that’ll be good.”

Kevin De Bruyne, who departed City two summers ago, is an idol for Anderson. “Growing up through the academy at Newcastle, I’ve always wanted to play like him,” Anderson said. “I’ve watched him all the time and to be sat here in the team that he was doing it for is so special.”

Anderson led the Premier League last season in most touches (3,300), most duels won (297) and winning possession (306). “I think I bring a bit of everything. I bring quality, physicality, energy,” he said. “I’d like to think I’d get them [the City supporters] excited, get them off their feet and bring energy to the team.”

Anderson spent half a season on loan at Bristol Rovers in 2022 and became known as the “Geordie Maradona” among supporters. “They started that and it sort of stuck everywhere I’ve been,” he said. “It makes me happy and it gives me real confidence.”

Reflecting on the World Cup, Anderson added: “It was disappointing, but I loved it personally. We had the whole country behind us and we’ve done so well but just fell short. From a personal point of view, I thought I did pretty well.”

Sports.title: ‘Don’t become the protagonist’: Andoni Iraola on the secret of Spain’s success and his role at Liverpool
Sports.content:
Over coffee in Liverpool’s plush hotel in Chicago, Andoni Iraola presents his theory for the phenomenal success of Basque and Spanish coaches. It is a theory that will shape his entire approach to life as the Liverpool head coach and his attempts to bring the connection, the joy and the belief back to Anfield. It centres on the power of the collective.

The Champions League, the Premier League, the Europa League, the FA Cup, the League Cup, the European Championship and, as of Sunday, the World Cup: all currently in the hands of Basque and Spanish coaches, even if Pep Guardiola has since taken his leave from Manchester City. Next season, four men from the small Basque region of Gipuzkoa will manage four of the Premier League’s main contenders, Iraola included, alongside Mikel Arteta, Xabi Alonso and Unai Emery. There is, Iraola believes, a simple explanation for the rise of the guys from Gipuzkoa and for Spanish dominance across a global stage.

“They ask me why a lot of Basque managers especially have arrived to this level and why Spanish teams are winning a lot of things,” Iraola explains. “I always say that a sense of collectiveness is very important. Spain has never had the best athletes. If you analyse in swimming, boxing, track and field, Spain don’t normally win medals. But in collective sports they are very good. In football, basketball, handball, hockey, normally they have good teams. We always put the team first. An example is someone like Rodri. He didn’t score or make an assist but at the end they won the World Cup and he won best player of the tournament. Team-first was always integrated in how we were raised.”

Iraola, warm and friendly despite the jetlag at the start of Liverpool’s pre-season tour of the US, then gives an immediate example of how he embodies those values. He is asked about a letter he sent to Liverpool in January 2014 when, as captain of boyhood club Athletic Club, he rejected the opportunity to sign for Brendan Rodgers’s team. By all accounts courteous and apologetic, as well as highly unusual, the letter provides a telling insight into Iraola’s character. It is an open goal of a question to a new head coach wanting to win over a new fanbase. But Iraola declines to shoot.

Following a lengthy pause, he says: “I don’t know if I want to tell this story so early in my career here. I would like to win some games first. It is a nice story but if you remember me in some months, then you can ask me again. I don’t like to do this from the beginning. I just don’t want to. It will look like I am selling myself. We need some time, and to win some games.”

Iraola’s outlook is refreshing – “Don’t become the protagonist,” he says of his role – and one that Liverpool can easily identify with. Continuing with the theme of Spain’s collectiveness, he adds: “I think there has to be something in society. It cannot only just be about football. I think things work when we are not just selfish, no? When, in the end, you prioritise the situation of the one who has less. That happens also in football. The ones that don’t play, the ones who come from the academy, the ones who earn less. You can compare it with society.”

View image in fullscreen Andoni Iraola will hope to inspire Jeremie Frimpong this season after his disappointing debut campaign at Anfield. Photograph: Nick Taylor/Liverpool FC/Getty Images

But, and it is a “but” that needs saying given what Iraola hopes to achieve, there were few signs of togetherness at Liverpool last season as Arne Slot’s reign unravelled amid acrimony in the dressing room and in the crowd. The power of the individual took over, and the power of the team appeared secondary. Mohamed Salah’s frequent attempts to undermine his former, title-winning coach was not the only example of that last season.

“I cannot change the personality of the players,” says Iraola, who will manage for the first time as Liverpool head coach on Saturday against Sunderland in Nashville. “Some players are very different to me but they are great players. I don’t want to change everyone and what they think is the best way. But I think we need to think collectively in this game. As a player you are always selfish. You always want to play, you always want to get your stats, you always want to play all the minutes, but I think there has to be an understanding that this is not going to always happen and still I have to be helpful with my teammates and with the team.

double quotation mark I always say we are assistants to the players. They are the main part Andoni Iraola

“The first thing we have to do is try to play well, but it’s not just only about playing well. Supporters have to identify with what they see on the pitch. Sometimes it’s not about just putting one ball in the top corner. A lot of the time, the ones watching the game, OK, they cannot do that but they can run, they can fight for the balls, they can press, they can fight until the last line for every situation and when they see this from the players of their team it’s easier to get behind that team. I will encourage my team to give them these things.”

Iraola never came close to signing for Liverpool 12 years ago despite the best efforts of Michael Edwards, until recently the chief executive of football for the club’s owners, Fenway Sports Group. “I never really wanted to leave Athletic Club,” their former right-back admits. “For me, Athletic Club was the place to be. The only way of leaving was to go to the MLS [with New York City FC] and try something completely different. I didn’t want to become a problem for the club.”

The 44-year-old, however, does see parallels between his boyhood club and his new one. He explains: “This is one of the biggest clubs in the world and, in some way, the comparison to Athletic Club probably isn’t fair, but in a lot of ways I see a lot of similar things. This sense of belonging, of being a little bit different. This connection, also, with players from the academy. The atmosphere of Anfield.”

At his official unveiling in Liverpool last week, Iraola said he intends to immerse himself in the city and “take some pictures” of the tourist spots. The truth is he has already done so. He visited the city a few times during his playing days with Athletic and for a very simple reason. “It had the best flight connections,” he laughs. “The best connections were Manchester and Brussels and sometimes we only had two or three days so the main thing was to go somewhere quick. I remember the first time I went to Liverpool it was already the Christmas market so it was probably around the November international break. We had no kids at the time so we are talking about a lot of years ago but it was a lovely time with my wife.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

There has been no holiday this summer for Iraola and his family, now extended by two children. “I went home for one week in the half-term for the kids at the end of May,” he says. “That was once the season had ended. I have mostly been in Bournemouth but I also had some trips to Liverpool to sort the schools and the housing. This is the stuff I wanted to do before I started working officially.”

Iraola describes the process of leaving Bournemouth after three impressive years as “very, very clean” and claims he only started considering his next step once last season had ended with the club in Europe for the first time. The process of becoming Slot’s replacement “was actually quite fast”. He says: “Honestly. It was true that I was talking with some clubs [Milan, Bayer Leverkusen and Crystal Palace all made approaches]. I think it was the first or second week after the season ended. But it happened fast. They contacted me, and it didn’t take a lot [to say yes to Liverpool this time].”

View image in fullscreen Andoni Iraola answers questions in the US before Liverpool’s opening pre-season game against Sunderland on Saturday. Photograph: Anadolu/Getty Images

It hasn’t taken long for Liverpool fans to create a song in honour of their new head coach. Sung to the tune of Christy Moore’s Viva la Quinta Brigada, written about Irish volunteers who fought against Franco’s fascist forces in the Spanish civil war, the song went viral within days of Iraola’s appointment in June. He is genuinely astonished when told, almost spluttering over a second cup of coffee.

“A new one?” Iraola asks incredulously. “For me it is a strange situation because I always understand that football is about the players. At the beginning when I arrived in England, I remember the first few games I didn’t go with the players to clap the supporters after games. Tommy and Shaun [Elphick and Cooper, Bournemouth assistants who have followed Iraola to Liverpool] said I should join in. In Spain, normally you leave it to the players; they are the ones who have played the game and we are the ones who stayed behind. In England, managers are the ones who go to the fans, so I have done it every time.

“These are the cultural things you have to learn when you arrive in a new league. But I always say we are assistants to the players. They are the main part. Our main thing is to help them and they are the only ones who can give us success. We are not as important as they are, that is pretty clear.”

The Kop may dispute that theory, but not Iraola’s take on the power of the collective if restored to full working order.

Sports.title: Police call on English football clubs to ease security burden on taxpayers
Sports.content:
The number of football matches in England and Wales featuring incidents reported to police reached record levels last season, even as the number of arrests continued to return to pre-Covid figures.

According to an annual report by the Home Office, released on Thursday, there was a 4% increase in the number of matches with reports of “football-related anti-social behaviour, violence and disorder” during the 2025-26 season. Reports were made at 1,644 games, up from 1,580 the previous campaign.

Meanwhile, the Home Office calculated there were four arrests (or other actions such as voluntary police interviews) for every 100,000 people attending a men’s football match in 2025-26, with the FA Cup the most likely competition for arrests to be made. Across the women’s game, however, that number falls to four in total.

Quick Guide How do I 

The total number of arrests last season stood at 1,695, down from 1,744 in 2024-25 and a peak of 2,198 during the pandemic-affected campaign of 2021-22. Contained within these figures was an increase in the number of arrests and other actions related to public disorder, the most common type of offence.

This year’s figures in part reflect a change in the data being collected. Last season, for example, the crime of “unauthorised entry” was added to the Football Spectators Act 1989. There were 45 arrests made under the new law in 2025-26, meaning total arrests and actions would otherwise have declined by 4%.

New categories of “sexism and misogyny” and “violence against women and girls” were also added to the list of behaviours that can be reported by supporters, either to police or to bodies such as the FA or Kick It Out. The Home Office said 22 matches were reported for instances of sexist behaviour and 37 for violence against women. “The overall increase was therefore largely driven by the introduction of these new categories”, a Home Office statement said.

Of the incidents reported, the most common type was “hate crime”, which was reported at 491 matches. The second most common was reports of missiles being thrown (359 games) and then the use of pyrotechnics (316 matches).

In other data released by the Home Office, the number of football banning orders – a sanction that prevents someone convicted of a football-related crime from attending matches – issued was at its highest level since 2012. Currently there are 2,460 FBOs in place. This is up by 568 on the previous season, but a smaller rise than the 685 recorded in 2024-25.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Chief constable Mark Roberts, the lead for football policing in England and Wales, said the latest Home Office report showed the need to revisit the funding of football policing, with 46% of arrests and actions taking place outside of stadiums. “Football-related crime doesn’t simply stop when fans exit the stadium, but under the current system multibillion-pound football clubs do not have to pay a penny towards the policing outside their grounds,” Roberts said. “This means that taxpayers are left footing the £70m bill each season, which simply cannot continue.”

Sports.title: Aston Villa seal loan signing of Alejandro Garnacho from Chelsea
Sports.content:
Aston Villa have confirmed the loan signing of the Chelsea winger Alejandro Garnacho, as a summer of change continues at Villa Park.

The deal for Garnacho’s season-long loan includes a conditional obligation to buy a player who joined Chelsea last August from Manchester United in a deal worth £40m. Villa will be expected to pay a similar fee for Garnacho, who struggled to impress at Stamford Bridge despite featuring in 43 games in all competitions and scoring eight goals.

Garnacho has been allowed to depart Stamford Bridge after being informed he was not guaranteed regular playing time under the club’s new manager, Xabi Alonso. He did not report for duty when Chelsea players returned for pre-season, as pre-arranged.

It was agreed he would stay away from the training ground while any departure was finalised. Named in Argentina’s initial 55-man selection, he missed out on this summer’s World Cup.

“We are delighted with Alejandro. He is so talented, young and he ⁠showed us his wish to help our ​project. We are ‌really happy,” ‌Unai Emery said.

Villa’s third signing of the summer, to follow the arrivals of Johan Manzambi and João Gomes, comes via a familiar trade route. The £117m deal that took Morgan Rogers to Stamford Bridge earlier this week continued a run of transfers between the two clubs, incorporating Carney Chukwuemeka’s and Omari Kellyman’s sale to Chelsea in 2022 and 2024, Ian Maatsen heading in the reverse direction in 2024 and Axel Disasi’s brief 2025 loan to Villa.

Another former Chelsea charge, Jadon Sancho, spent last season on loan at Villa from United and, despite becoming a free agent, he was not signed. Youri Tielemans has also departed Villa for Manchester United this month after his £35m release clause was triggered as the Europa League champions rebuild as a Champions League club, though one under Uefa sanction.

Earlier this summer Villa received a partially suspended £19.4m fine by Uefa for a “significant breach” of squad-cost rule for 2025. Depending on the club significantly decreasing their squad-cost ratio in 2026, £12.9m is suspended, with the club restricted on the registration of new players on their squad list for the coming Champions League season.

Sports.title: Arsenal sign Greece forward Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge for £34m
Sports.content:
Arsenal have completed the £34m signing of Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge. The Greece international, 24, has signed a five-year contract with the Premier League champions and arrives as a replacement for Leandro Trossard following the Belgian’s switch to Besiktas.

Tzolis’s move to the Emirates Stadium – Arsenal’s third permanent transfer of the summer – arrives 48 hours after the north Londoners missed out on Morgan Rogers who signed a £117m British-record fee with Chelsea, describing his new employers as the “biggest club in London”.

Tzolis scored 43 times in 108 appearances for Club Brugge, and lined up in the Belgians’ 3-0 Champions League defeat by Mikel Arteta’s side in December. “I need some time to realise it, I think,” Tzolis said. “⁠It’s absolutely amazing to sign for such a big ​club, the champions of ‌England. I’m very ‌proud to be part of this team for ‌the next season.”

Arsenal’s sporting director Andrea Berta added: “We’re delighted to have completed the signing of Christos. [He] is an extremely versatile attacking player who naturally operates on the left but is comfortable across the front line. He’s an excellent finisher with both feet, thrives in tight spaces, and possesses incredible technical ability.

“Christos has produced outstanding numbers in terms of goals and assists over the last three seasons, and he’s a player who will raise the technical level of our squad, while bringing positive energy, enthusiasm and a strong mentality to our team. We’re confident Christos will make a significant contribution to our club, and we hope our supporters will enjoy watching him play in an Arsenal shirt. We look forward to sharing this exciting new chapter together.”

Tzolis played 14 Premier League games for Norwich during the 2021-22 campaign but his only two goals at the club came in the League Cup. Loan periods with Twente and Fortuna Düsseldorf followed before he made the move to Brugge in 2024.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The Greek follows Piero Hincapié – who turned his temporary deal with Arsenal into a full-time switch – and goalkeeper Illan Meslier, a free signing from Leeds, as the Gunners’ third signing. The announcement arrives as a welcome boost for Arteta after defender William Saliba was this week ruled out for an “extensive period” with the back problem the curtailed his World Cup. The France international is set to miss the start of Arsenal’s Premier League defence.

Sports.title: Manchester United consider Camavinga and Berge as midfield overhaul continues
Sports.content:
Manchester United have identified Real Madrid’s Eduardo Camavinga and Fulham’s Sander Berge as midfield signings to further strengthen Michael Carrick’s squad.

United have already signed two midfielders this window: Andrey Santos in a £48m deal from Chelsea and Youri Tielemans for £35m from Aston Villa. But with Casemiro having departed and Manuel Ugarte ruled out for what may be a prolonged period due to a knee ligament injury, the club is considering moving for another midfielder.

Camavinga is believed to favour staying at Real though the Spanish club may be open to selling the Frenchman in order to make space for Rodri. The 23-year-old Camavinga, who has three years left on his contract and was not part of France’s World Cup squad, has a €1bn release clause, but Real would listen to offers of between €50m-€60m (£42m-£51m) for the player, it is thought.

View image in fullscreen Sander Berge featured for Norway at the recent World Cup, including in the quarter-final against England. Photograph: Chris Carlson/AP

Berge, who is 28 and has previously been on United’s radar, would cost around £40m and, unlike Camavinga, has considerable playing experience in England. The Norwegian signed for Sheffield United in 2020, joined Burnley in 2023 and left for Fulham the following year. Berge played in Norway’s 2-1 World Cup quarter-final loss to England.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

United’s list for a possible new midfielder includes Bournemouth’s Alex Scott and Roma’s Manu Koné.

Sports.title: Norway considers filing Fifa ethics complaint over Trump role in World Cup red card saga
Sports.content:
Donald Trump’s role in clearing Folarin Balogun from a mandatory one-game ban at the World Cup is set to provoke a formal complaint to Fifa ethics investigators.

The Norway soccer federation said Thursday its board of directors will consider filing the complaint at its next meeting, likely on 6 August.

“We need our leader in Fifa to say that this was an error,” Norwegian federation president Lise Klaveness told the Times in an interview published Thursday.

After Trump called Fifa president Gianni Infantino, a one-game ban for Balogun’s red-card tackle against Bosnia and Herzegovina was deferred so he could play against Belgium with a quarterfinals place at stake.

Belgium beat the US 4-1 after a chaotic 36 hours at the World Cup. The Belgium players were seemingly fired up by one of the all-time controversies in tournament history.

Trump called the referee’s red card for Balogun after video review a “horrible” call and took credit for getting Fifa to review what should routinely have been a one-game ban.

“We all know that this verdict was influenced from external forces and did not have the proper process,” Klaveness told the Times of the Fifa ruling that was unprecedented in the past 60 years at World Cups. “When you bend a rule like this, you’re on a slippery slope that will put the whole game at risk,” said the former Women’s World Cup player for Norway, who is an elected member of European soccer body Uefa’s executive committee.

Klaveness is a lawyer and judge who has positioned the Norwegian federation as a conscience in world soccer since her election in 2022. “It is a worry for the game when you compromise fundamental rules of the game,” she said Thursday about not enforcing Balogun’s ban.

Norway previously joined a London-based NGO’s complaint to the Fifa ethics committee alleging Infantino breached a statutory duty of political neutrality, including by creating a peace prize to award to Trump at the World Cup draw in December.

The close personal and political ties between Trump and Infantino include the US president believing the soccer official could be a good pick as next secretary general of the United Nations, the New York Post reported this week.

The human rights NGO, FairSquare, also has filed an ethics complaint about the Balogun incident to the International Olympic Committee, where Infantino is an elected member, about breaching its rules on political neutrality.

Fifa and the IOC rarely acknowledge or provide updates on potential cases before their ethics bodies. The independence of Fifa’s process to handle complaints alleging unethical conduct has been questioned since the lead investigator and judge both were replaced in 2017, in the second year of Infantino’s presidency. Fifa has yet to publish documents explaining how its disciplinary judges reached verdicts about Balogun or other World Cup players.

Sports.title: Maldini confirms crisis-hit Italy have held talks with Guardiola and Ancelotti
Sports.content:
The Italian football federation (FIGC) has talked to Pep Guardiola, the former Manchester City coach, and Carlo Ancelotti, the Brazil manager, about taking over the crisis-hit national team.

It hopes to announce the new Italy coach within the week, with the Azzurri still reeling after failing for a third straight time to qualify for the World Cup.

Paolo Maldini, the former Italy and Milan defender, was named as the federation’s new technical director at the start of the month and was present at a meeting with the Serie A clubs on Thursday, along with the new FIGC president, Giovanni Malagò, and the special advisor Leonardo.

“Honestly, today we can’t give news about what’s happening. You’ve identified one of our targets,” Maldini said when asked about Guardiola in a news conference after the meeting. “We can’t hide that we also talked with Carlo Ancelotti before talking with Pep. Honestly, it seemed right to start with the best in the world, to see their general availability.”

Guardiola left City at the end of last season, bringing to a close a trophy-laden, 10-year spell in which he established the club as a force in Europe and changed the face of English football. The 55-year-old has won numerous major titles across his coaching career including at Barcelona and Bayern Munich.

Maldini and Leonardo spent three days in Barcelona recently to speak with Guardiola about taking the Italy job. “The best thing would be to announce the new coach this week, but even more to wait for the person we really want,” Maldini said. “So there’s urgency, but not so much inside us.”

Ancelotti signed a contract extension with Brazil in May through to the 2030 World Cup. But the five-time world champions had one of their worst ever performances on football’s biggest stage as they were eliminated in the last 16 thanks to a 2-1 loss against Norway.

The 67-year-old has won league titles in Italy, England, France, Spain and Germany. He is also the only coach to have won the Champions League five times.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Italy, four-time world champions, missed out on a third straight World Cup after a playoff loss to Bosnia and Herzegovina in March, prompting the resignations of the FIGC president, Gabriele Gravina, and the head coach, Gennaro Gattuso. Gattuso had taken over from the fired Luciano Spalletti the previous June with the team already flailing following a defeat against Norway in their opening qualifier.

The former Italy coaches Roberto Mancini – who led the Azzurri to victory in the European Championship in 2021 – and Antonio Conte are also among the favourites to take charge of the national team. Andrea Pirlo, who helped Italy to win the World Cup in 2006 as a player, is also reportedly in contention.

Sports.title: Arsenal set to sign history-making EFL star after missing out on Jeremy Monga
Sports.content:
Arsenal set to sign history-making EFL star after missing out on Jeremy Monga

Arsenal are reportedly set to complete the signing of 16-year-old sensation Axel Donczew from Cardiff City.

The Gunners have moved for another history-making teenager after missing out on Jeremy Monga, who joined Manchester City.

3 Arsenal are set to sign another young star after missing out on Monga to City Credit: Manchester City

Monga is the second youngest ever player in Premier League history and the youngest ever Championship goalscorer, and he signed for Man City from Leicester earlier this summer.

That deal was completed despite Arsenal having an agreement in place, with City swooping in to complete a hijack and sign the starlet.

Mikel Arteta missed out on his target in the end - but the club have now made an approach for a second youngster.

According to The Athletic, the Gunners are on the brink of signing Donczew, who is Cardiff's youngest ever player.

The midfielder made his Bluebirds debut in October 2025, appearing as a substitute in an EFL Trophy tie against Newport County.

His first appearance, at 16 years and 117 days old, saw him break the record set by ex-Arsenal star Aaron Ramsey, who made his Cardiff bow aged 16 years and 123 days old in 2007.

He then went on to feature in another game in the cup competition, playing 23 minutes against AFC Wimbledon in December.

Donczew also has caps for Wales on the international stage, playing for his country at under-15 level through to the under-19s.

Across his 11 national appearances, he has scored two goals.

The teenager is also eligible to play for Poland, so he has multiple options when it comes to future senior representation.

3 Arteta has done some business already this summer, with more big names linked Credit: Getty

Arsenal's signings so far this summer

Donczew looks set to be the next arrival for Arsenal in this transfer window, with the Gunners already welcoming two new faces.

Christos Tzolis' signing was confirmed on Thursday, as the ex-Norwich winger made a £34million move from Club Brugge.

That came after former Leeds goalkeeper Illan Meslier joined the club following the expiration of his contract at Elland Road.

In fact, the Gunners have made three signings already this summer, if you include the permanent arrival of Piero Hincapie.

Hincapie spent last season on loan at the Emirates, but signed a full-time contract at the club for £34.5m in June.

More incomings are expected though, as Arteta looks to bolster his squad for their Premier League title defence this term.

3 Guimaraes is one of Arsenal's targets as they look to secure multiple new signings Credit: Getty

Arsenal have been linked with John Stones, who is now a free agent after leaving Man City at the end of his contract.

And they are also continuing to pursue Newcastle's Bruno Guimaraes, having already seen an approach rejected.

The Gunners made an offer of £65m for Guimaraes, but they were knocked back, despite agreeing personal terms.

They are expected to return with an improved bid for the Brazilian, who is understood to want to leave St. James' Park.

That new offer for the Toon captain is set to be over £70m.

Sports.title: Arsenal urged to give Declan Rice extended break or risk early retirement
Sports.content:
Arsenal have been warned they'll pay the price long term if they don't give Declan Rice an extended summer break.

The 27-year-old endured a relentless campaign that saw him play an exhausting 69 games, totalling 4,925 minutes across all competitions for club and country.



3 Rice struggled to match his club form with Arsenal during the World Cup, with an ongoing hamstring injury and illness affecting his game Credit: Getty

Rice missed just two Premier League for the Gunners, and featured in every World Cup game for the Three Lions.

He became a champion of England, starring in Mikel Arteta's side with four goal contributions during their title-winning season.

Additionally, he helped propel England to their best ever finish at the World Cup since 1966, securing a third place finish with a 6-4 victory over France in the bronze medal match.



However, after featuring in nearly every fixture available, it's clear that congested scheduling is mounting physical demands on Rice.

He was managing a hamstring issue in North America, having already suffered from a dead calf and minor knee injuries earlier in the season.



Immediately after England's final game of the tournament, Rice said: "That's what you do [play through injury] when you get to come to a World Cup. It's an honour, you do anything you can to put on this shirt.

"You never know when it's going to come to an end, you never take it for granted.



"The body's been through a lot this season. I think you can see I'm mentally done, physically done. I need a break now."

And Peterborough United chairman Darragh MacAnthony insists Arsenal must not rush Rice back from his break.

MacAnthony told talkSPORT: "I'd be saying to him, you go away for like a month, go get a holiday with your family, and then we're going to do a month of light training, and you're not going to touch a football for a couple of months.

3 Arsenal are working hard on their title defence with new signings, including Christos Tzolis Credit: Getty



"Because that kid, he's not a kid, he's 27 now, he will be burnt out by 30. You know, the body, it's amazing what football can do to the body, and we've seen over the years.

"Do you remember Fabinho at Liverpool? He was phenomenal one season, and over one summer he aged ten years."

Saka concern

Rice is not the only Arsenal star facing physical strain after a relentless 12 months.

Arsenal have also confirmed William Saliba will be sidelined for an extended period with a back injury.



Meanwhile, Bukayo Saka arrived at the World Cup with a persistent Achilles issue.

Even England manager Thomas Tuchel felt the winger needed careful management, opting not to allow the 24-year-old to train every day.

3 Tuchel was being extremely careful with Saka, who only started three games at the tournament

MacAnthony added: "Sometimes it's the wear and tear on the engine, right? And you worry about that for say Rice, you worry about Saka with his hamstrings now, his Achilles that he's got those issues with.



"So they're going to have to handle it really, really well."

Sports.title: Premier League releases its own team of the tournament after controversial FIFA picks
Sports.content:
Premier League releases its own team of the tournament after controversial FIFA picks

The Premier League has unveiled its very own World Cup team of the tournament, albeit with one key caveat.

It came hot on the heels of FIFA revealing it's World Cup 'Dream XI', which was voted on by fans across the globe.



6 A number of Spanish Premier League stars shone on the world's biggest stage Credit: Getty

The 'Dream XI' produced some rather peculiar picks, with Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha selected ahead of Spain's Unai Simon, who won the Golden Glove having kept seven clean sheets.

Spanish centre-back Pau Cubarsi, who was named the Young Player of the Tournament, was also snubbed from the 'Dream XI'.

There was also no room for either Simon or Cubarsi in the Premier League's team of the tournament, but that wasn't down to their qualities.



Instead, it's because they don't play in the English top-flight, which was the primary criteria for inclusion.

Announcing the team, which was listed in a 4-3-3 formation, the Premier League confirmed it was chosen by fans from all over the world from a shortlist of 101 players.



So, which Premier League stars made the cut?

Which goalkeeper made the team?

We start between the sticks and it's England goalkeeper Jordan Pickford who got the nod.

Pickford, who plays for Everton, made 19 saves for the Three Lions across the tournament as they finished third.



The 32-year-old beat the likes of Argentina's Emiliano Martinez (Aston Villa), Dutch gloveman Bart Verbruggen (Brighton) and Brazil's Alisson (Liverpool) in the voting.

Which defenders made the team?

At the back, Spain's Pedro Porro (Tottenham) and Argentina centre-back Lisandro Martinez (Manchester United) retained their spots in the line-up from the 'Dream XI'.

6 Despite playing a part in Spurs coming 17th, Porro ensured Spain wouldn't have similar misery Credit: Getty

That meant one other centre-back position as well as left-back was up for grabs.



Partnering Martinez in central defence was his Argentina teammate Cristian Romero (Tottenham).

Romero was a virtual ever-present for the La Albiceleste, missing just one of their eight matches throughout the tournament.

Completing the back four was England's Djed Spence (Tottenham), who is a natural right-back, but slotted in comfortably at left-back.

With the additions of Romero and Spence, that means 75 per cent of defence featured in the Premier League's team of the tournament was made up of Tottenham stars.



However, the duo may not be in north London for much longer, with Romero holding talks with Inter Milan while Spurs are understood to be open to offers for Spence.

6 Spence won over fans thanks to his perfectly-timed tackles Credit: Getty

Which midfielders made the team?

Spain's Rodri (Manchester City) was the only midfielder from the 'Dream XI' to be included in the Premier League's team of the tournament.

That should not come as much of a surprise since he was awarded the Golden Ball, which is given to the best player at the World Cup.



Joining Rodri in the midfield was England's Elliot Anderson (Manchester City) and Argentina ace Enzo Fernandez (Chelsea).

Anderson started every match for the Three Lions prior to their third-place play-off and finished top of the charts among his teammates for tackles (21) and interceptions (8).

It was also a tournament to remember for Anderson off the field, as he completed a £116m switch from Nottingham Forest to Manchester City.

Fernandez's World Cup ended on a sour note when he was sent off against Spain in the final, although he failed to address his red card in his post-match statement shared on social media.



6 Fernandez picked up two yellow cards in the space of 11 minutes during the final Credit: Getty

The midfielder also may not be a Premier League player for much longer having pined for a move to Real Madrid in recent months.

Which forwards made the team?

There's no prizes for guessing who was voted to lead the line in the Premier League's team of the tournament.

Erling Haaland (Manchester City) was the people's choice having scored seven goals in five games for Norway.



On the right, Bukayo Saka (Arsenal) received the nod despite starting three games for England.

Saka ended the tournament with three goals to his name, all of which were scored against France in the third place play-off.

His treble saw him become just the fourth England player to score a hat-trick in the gloal tournament.

6 Only Kylian Mbappe [ten] and Lionel Messi [eight] scored more goals than Haaland's seven in North America



And incredibly, only Harry Kane [14], Gary Lineker [ten] and Jude Bellingham [eight] have scored than Saka's six World Cup goals for England.

Senegal's Ismaila Sarr (Crystal Palace) completes the Premier League's team of the tournament on the left wing.

Sarr netted four times in as many games, which helped him become Senegal's leading goalscorer at the World Cup.

Sports.title: EFL club left gutted as Chelsea snap up star in under-the-radar transfer
Sports.content:
Wigan Athletic have expressed their disappointment at seeing young star Harrison Bettoni depart for Chelsea.

The 18-year-old attacking midfielder has joined the Blues from the League One club on a four-year deal, with the two sides agreeing a 'significant' amount of compensation.



2 Bettoni burst onto the scene at Wigan last season Credit: Getty

Having signed for Wigan at under-13 level, Bettoni rose through the ranks to break into the first team.

He made his senior debut last season, scoring four goals in 26 appearances overall.

He notched up the only goal of the game as Wigan shocked Championship Preston North End in the FA Cup third round.



Wigan disappointed but proud

Announcing Bettoni's exit, Wigan managing director Sarah Guilfoyle said: "As a club, we made every possible effort to retain Harrison.

"We offered Harrison multiple strong and competitive long-term offers to remain at Wigan Athletic, reflecting both the high regard we have for his ability and the importance we saw him having in our future.



"Ultimately, every player reaches a point where they must make a decision they believe is right for their career. Harrison has chosen to pursue a new opportunity, and while we are disappointed not to see him continue his journey with us, we respect his decision.

"We've worked closely with Chelsea to agree a compensation package that reflects the time, care, and investment our academy has put into Harrison's development from a young age. Producing talented young players is something our academy takes immense pride in, and it's important that work is recognised.



"We thank Harrison for everything he has contributed during his time with us and wish him every success in the next chapter of his career."

Bettoni becomes Chelsea's fifth signing of the summer so far.

Earlier this week, the Blues completed a British-record £117m move to sign Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa.

Meanwhile, Alejandro Garnacho has moved the other way on loan but with an obligation to buy if certain conditions are met.

2 Rogers has just become the most expensive British player of all time, beating the record set earlier this summer when Manchester City paid £116m for Elliot Anderson Credit: Getty



The other new arrivals at Stamford Bridge are right-back Marco Palestra, striker Emmanuel Emegha and Geovany Quenda, who have come in from Atalanta, Strasbourg and Sporting Lisbon respectively.

The start of the Alonso era

Chelsea are preparing for the 2026/27 season with a new manager at the helm, Xabi Alonso.

They begin their Premier League campaign with a West London derby away to Fulham on August 24, before their home opener against Brighton on August 30.

Wigan, meanwhile, are building up to a third straight season in the third tier.



The Latics finished 15th last term, re-appointing Gary Caldwell as their boss in February.

They travel to newly promoted Cambridge United as the League One campaign kicks off on August 15.

Sports.title: Will Lionel Messi retire? Argentina captain tipped for new role with Real Madrid academy star
Sports.content:
Will Lionel Messi retire? Argentina captain tipped for new role with Real Madrid academy star

Lionel Messi has been tipped to retire from professional football before the 2030 World Cup.

The Argentina forward will turn 43 during the next finals in four years time.



4 Messi has been tipped to assume a new role with Argentina before the 2030 World Cup Credit: Getty

Fans had expected Messi to walk away from international football after winning the World Cup in 2022.

However, he remained part of the national team ahead of this summer's tournament, reaching the third final of his career.

Having scored eight goals and provided four assists, he was unable to guide Argentina to glory as they were beaten by Spain in the final.



The showpiece clash could now prove to be his final international appearance.

Meanwhile, Messi's current Inter Miami deal runs until the end of 2028, by which point he will be 41.



Although he could continue playing at club level until his contract expires, another World Cup appearance is less concrete.

Messi's international future

South American football journalist Tim Vickery remains unsure whether Messi will still be playing come the 2030 finals.



Speaking to Max Scott and Charlie Baker on talkSPORT, he was asked if the loss to Spain would be his last Argentina outing.

Vickery responded by admitting: "I don't know, because defeat for them is so painful that you'll need a little bit of time to assimilate.

"The next World Cup looks a long, long way off, especially after the evidence of the game.

4 Vickery believes Messi could nurture Paz over the next four years to become his successor for Argentina Credit: Alamy



"When you're playing against a team like Spain, it's really hard to carry someone who doesn't run.

"You can do it against some other teams, but against Spain, they're just too good without the ball. It's really, really tough.

"Before the game I was thinking, 'could he?' Could he still be around in four years? When Argentina's next game is in Buenos Aires in the World Cup, will he?

"Then after the game I'm thinking he's looking at the stands thinking 'no', but I wonder if he can play a role in the transition."



New role for Messi

Whilst Messi may not feature at the next World Cup, Vickery believes he could remain with the national team to nurture his successor.

He continued: "He's under contract for Inter Miami for another two-and-a-half years. There's a Copa America in 2028.

4 Nico Paz made just two appearances for Argentina at this summer's World Cup but could replace Messi on the pitch Credit: Alamy

"Nico Paz, who hardly got a look in this World Cup, partly because he can't really play with Messi because he wants the ball to feet just like Messi does.



"You can't have too many of them in your team, but Nico Paz I think is going to be the one for the future.

"I just think it's possible that Messi could stay in the squad as the kind of wise old owl, as a kind of Master Yoda.

"You could call him Messi Yoda, with Nico Paz as a kind of Luke Skywalker figure. I wonder if that will be the dynamic over the next couple of years."

Como's Nico Paz made just two appearances for Argentina during the World Cup, totalling 71 minutes of action.



The 21-year-old currently has one goal to his name in 11 senior caps since making his debut in October 2024.

4 The Como starlet has been tipped to become Messi's long-term heir for Argentina Credit: Getty

Of those, only five have seen him on the pitch at the same time as Messi.

However, the Real Madrid academy graduate is seen as the eight-time Ballon d'Or winner's long-term heir for Argentina.



Paz scored once in eight appearances for the Spanish giants before moving to Como two years ago.

He has since featured for the Serie A side 75 times, scoring 19 goals and adding 17 assists.

Argentina will host their first match at the 2030 World Cup on home soil as part of the tournament's centenary celebrations.

As a result, the Albiceleste have already automatically qualified for the finals alongside Spain, Morocco, Portugal, Paraguay and Uruguay.

Sports.title: Ballon d’Or should go to player who wasn’t even at the World Cup, not Lamine Yamal or Harry Kane
Sports.content:
Ballon d’Or should go to player who wasn’t even at the World Cup, not Lamine Yamal or Harry Kane

Neither Lamine Yamal nor Harry Kane should win this year's Ballon d'Or, believes talkSPORT's Gabby Agbonlahor.

Both players enjoyed fine 2025/26 seasons for their respective clubs, Barcelona and Bayern Munich respectively. Yamal starred in Spain's World Cup triumph while Kane scored six goals as he captained England to the semi-finals.

4 Kane found the net six times as England finished third at the 2026 World Cup Credit: Getty

But for Agbonlahor, there's another leading candidate – a player who wasn't even at the World Cup in Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

Kane to miss out on first Ballon d'Or?

Joining Shebahn Aherne on Thursday's talkSPORT Sports Breakfast, Agbonlahor initially earmarked Yamal for a first Ballon d'Or.

Responding to Aherne's suggestion that Kane was 'in with a very healthy shout of winning the Ballon d'Or' for the first time, the former Aston Villa striker said: "Listen, Harry Kane: fantastic season at Bayern Munich, done very well at the World Cup... six goals, two assists, 72 goals in total [for club and country]. But I don't think he's going to get it, Shebahn."

Kane scored a Bayern club-record 58 goals in 2025/26, but falling short at the World Cup could prove costly, feels Agbonlahor.

"I just think, you know, Champions League disappointment, World Cup disappointment... it's normally a player, if there's a World Cup in that year, that gets [the Ballon d'Or]," he went on.

"For instance, Rodri won it in 2024 after winning the Euros, and obviously success with Manchester City.

"I look at Lamine Yamal. Listen, won the Euros before; won the World Cup this year; won LaLiga; 45 appearances, 24 goals, 18 assists last season with Barcelona.

"I think he's my standout of all the players because he won domestically, he played a lot of football and he won the World Cup.

Agbonlahor also played down the chances of Kylian Mbappe, eight-time winner Lionel Messi Rodri before concluding: "I see Yamal picking it up."

But Agbonlahor then changed his mind to another potential first-time winner of the award given annually to the world's best player.

"Do you know the player that I would give it to?" he continued. "[Kvicha] Kvaratskhelia.

4 Kvaratskhelia is a back-to-back European champion with Paris Saint-Germain Credit: Getty

4 Yamal has completed international football at 19 years old having already won the World Cup and European Championship Credit: Getty

When Aherne noted how Kvaratskhelia didn't play in the World Cup, Agbonlahor replied: "Exactly, but that's the thing: just because he wasn't at the World Cup, he can't get it?

Kvaratskhelia 'the standout player'

"But if you think about the best player to watch with your two eyes has been Kvaratskhelia all season for PSG.

"He's been the standout player – more than Lamine Yamal; more than Harry Kane; more than everyone else."

Asked who he'd choose if he had a vote for the Ballon d'Or, Agbonlahor answered: "Kvaratskhelia. I'd pick him. I think he's the player that I've just enjoyed watching."

Former Napoli winger Kvaratskhelia was integral to Paris Saint-Germain's latest trophy-laden campaign, which culminated in the French giants becoming just the second side in the Champions League era to retain the trophy by beating Arsenal in the final.

The 25-year-old, affectionately known as 'Kvaradona', is the captain of the Georgia national team, who featured in their first major tournament at Euro 2024 but have yet to qualify for the World Cup.

The current Ballon d'Or holder is Kvaratskhelia's PSG teammate Ousmane Dembele.

4 Dembele was the first French player to claim the Ballon d'Or since Zinedine Zidane in 1998 Credit: Getty

The last time two different players from the same club received the award in successive years was when Cristiano Ronaldo and Luka Modric, then of Real Madrid, won it in 2017 and 2018 respectively.

The 2026 Ballon d'Or will be presented at a ceremony in London on October 26.

Sports.title: Delay on Man City’s 130 charges verdict branded ‘inexplicable’ by financial expert
Sports.content:
The wait for a verdict on Manchester City's alleged Financial Fair Play (FFP) breaches has been labelled 'inexplicable'.

A hearing into the club's 130 charges concluded in December 2024.

4 The wait for the verdict in City's FFP case has been labelled 'unacceptable' by Stefan Borson Credit: Getty

However, a decision has yet to be announced almost two years on.

Stefan Borson has now slammed the 'remarkable' delay for an outcome ahead of the new Premier League season.

City were first charged with 115 breaches of the Premier League's FFP rules in February 2023.

Those breaches are alleged to have taken place during a period spanning from 2009 to 2018.

A further 15 charges were later added to take the total amount to 130, with a hearing held between September and December 2024.

With the verdict yet to be announced, Borson provided an update on Thursday.

City charges update

The football finance expert and regular talkSPORT guest joined Alex Crook and Darragh MacAnthony live on air.

Following a text from a Manchester United fan relating to the charges, Borson was asked for the latest on a potential decision.

He explained: "The general feeling around the industry is that there’s been no decision yet, as remarkable as that is. 19 months on, 20 months on almost, still no decision.

"Totally unacceptable, of course, beyond all of the parties’ expectations about when they would receive a decision. Broadly inexplicable by any sport of norms in these sorts of matters.

4 Chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak and City have been awaiting a verdict since the hearing concluded in December Credit: Getty

"But these cases are taking a very long time. I mean, you do also have a situation with the Chelsea charges from the FA. That was a hearing that was held in November.

"It was a sanction-only hearing, a very simple hearing and we’re still waiting for that, and that’s been sort of eight or nine months.

"So I don’t really know what’s going on with these cases in terms of the timings and why they’re so elongated, but they’re completely out of the realms of normality. Most decisions are in way before this."

Chelsea are still awaiting the outcome of an FA hearing into 74 breaches of rules relating to football agents.

It comes after the club were fined £10.75million for the offences by the Premier League in March.

Borson on potential outcome

When asked what he expects the outcome for City to be, Borson added: "It's very hard to get off the fence. The reality is it's extremely hard to prove the allegations that have been made.

4 Borson has provided a fresh update on City's 130 charges for alleged FFP breaches Credit: talkSPORT

"I think just in the behaviour of Manchester City, since the hearing itself in particular.

"The spending and the level of confidence that they're portraying, the signature of numerous contracts, the fact that a manager was prepared to move from Chelsea, the fact that they've built a £400million stadium and facility at one end of the ground.

"Every signal that the club has given in terms of its spending and its putting its money where its mouth is, suggests that they feel that they've won.

"But of course, all of these cases are very difficult to predict because litigation is something that even the best cases can lose and you should never be too certain about the outcome of any of those cases."

As for if his prediction is that the club will be found innocent, he said: "It's more likely that City will prevail given the behaviours and given the face that what's alleged is inherently unlikely.

"But of course, if they've done it, as I've said many times, the punishment will be extremely severe and this won't be about transfer bans or things around the edges.

4 City have already completed a club-record £116million signing of Elliot Anderson Credit: Getty

"If everything is proved against City, the sanctions will be severe."

City latest

City are currently going through their preparations for the new Premier League season.

The upcoming campaign marks Enzo Maresca's first after replacing Pep Guardiola in the dugout this summer.

City have already broken their club-record transfer fee with the £116million signing of Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest.

Permanent deals for Mathys Detourbet, Jeremy Monga and Pierce Charles have also been completed.

Meanwhile, talkSPORT understands the club are increasingly hopeful of landing Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille.

A new era is set to start at Tottenham as Roberto De Zerbi begins his first full campaign in charge with a pre-season tour of Australia and New Zealand.

Spurs head Down Under without several key figures, as Pedro Porro, Marcos Senesi, Cristian Romero, and Djed Spence have been granted extended leave following their nations' campaigns at the World Cup.

3 De Zerbi has already spent over £200million overhauling his Spurs squad this summer Credit: Getty

However, there are multiple new signings who will be making their debuts for the team, including Jan Paul van Hecke, Andy Robertson, Mateus Fernandes, and Sandro Tonali.
