Sports.title: Charlie Woods snaps at fan in fiery on-course moment... a day after he was caught swearing on hot mic
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Charlie Woods, the 17-year-old son of golf legend Tiger Woods, had a fiery clash with a fan on Wednesday, moments after being caught in an X-rated hot mic moment.

The teenager endured a frustrating morning that saw his bid to win the 2026 U.S. Junior Championship at Saucon Valley Country Club come to an abrupt end.

After bogeying the first hole of a 14-for-2 playoff for the final pair of match-play berths, Charlie's dreams were crushed after carding a +5 over two days of action.

During that par-five first hole, after two competitors had secured birdies, the 17-year-old went for the green in two from 270 yards out - but fell 25 yards short.

As he attempted to hit his third shot, a fan took a photo during his backswing - with the shutter sound clearly heard as Charlie was going through the motions.

A video of the incident has since gone viral and captured the moment that the teenager turned around to the fan, asking: 'Really, dude?'

Charlie Woods, the 17-year-old son of golf legend Tiger Woods, had a fiery clash with a fan

Another person behind the camera could be heard saying: 'Right in his swing'.

Following the awkward moment, Woods was unable to convert his chip for birdie.

Tiger's son finished with a bogey - meaning that Eli Wessel of Indianapolis and Hudson Kutchma of Westfield, Indiana made it to the 64-person match-play bracket.

The unfortunate, viral moment came just one day after Woods dropped an X-rated hot mic moment, as he teed off on the par-three eleventh hole.

In another viral video, posted by Michael Schmittinger Jr., Charlie was seen screaming out: 'Oh, f*** you' following his tee shot.

In the end, this particular instance didn't have a major impact on the 17-year-old, who went on to make par on the hole.

The viral moments came just days after he failed to qualify for this year's US Amateur Championship - the leading annual tournament for amateur golfers in the United States.

He teed it up at Ohio State University's Scarlet Course last week in an attempt to secure his place in the tournament field.

It marks the latest blow for Charlie, who has struggled to string together a series of results

However, Charlie, who has committed to Florida State University when he finishes high school next year, struggled in the qualifying event.

He shot a five-over 76 to miss out on qualifying by six shots, according to Golf Digest. A total of 13 qualifiers and two alternates emerged from the Scarlet Course site.

It marks the latest blow for Charlie, who has struggled recently to string together a series of promising results in his young career.

Charlie has participated in seven ranked events this season, where his best finish was 19th place at the Junior Orange Bowl International back in January.

Aside from that event, Charlie is yet to secure another top-25 finish this season.

Sports.title: Elliot Anderson aims dig at Man United after sealing £116m move to Man City as he declares: 'I've joined the kings of Manchester'
Sports.content:
Manchester City have announced the £116million signing of England international Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest.

Anderson, 23, joins City on a five-year deal, signing a contract until the summer of 2031, and becomes the second most expensive British transfer.

His move to the Etihad, agreed on July 2, was expected to make him the most expensive British player of all time - topping the £115m Real Madrid paid for Jude Bellingham in June 2023.

However, the switch was put on hold until after the World Cup, where Anderson won a bronze medal with England.

During that time, Chelsea completed a £117m deal for fellow England international Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa, making Anderson the British record transfer that never was.

City's new arrival wasted no time winding up local rivals Manchester United, declaring his new club the 'Kings of Manchester'. In Anderson's lifetime, City have indeed won more trophies than United - claiming 26 compared to United's 24 since 2002 (including the Community Shield).

'It's one of the biggest derbies in the world and for as long as I've known Manchester, City have been the Kings of Manchester,' Anderson said. 'It'll be a great fixture, and I can't wait to be involved in something like that.'

Newcastle, who sold Anderson to Forest for £35m in 2024 for PSR purposes, do not have a sell-on clause in the deal - meaning Forest stand to make £81m profit on the midfielder.

Elliot Anderson puts pen to paper on five-year deal at Manchester City

Anderson will take some time to rest after a marathon seven-week World Cup before joining Manchester City training in three weeks

Anderson won bronze with England at the World Cup

The deal contains no add-ons, with £117m representing the full transfer fee.

Anderson won the Under-21 European Championship with England last June before leaping up to Thomas Tuchel's senior side for the first international break of last season.

He is now an established England international with 17 caps and featured in all of the Three Lions' games at this summer's World Cup.

Anderson turned out 50 times in all competitions for Forest last season, helping them secure Premier League safety and reach the last four of the Europa League.

Anderson said: 'City are one of the biggest clubs in the world and the squad they have is amazing - so strong in every position. As soon as I knew they wanted me, I was absolutely determined to make this move happen.

'As a footballer, you want to test yourself at the highest level. Being at City means I have that opportunity. From the outside looking in, City are a club that treats its players well and provides the perfect environment to excel. I'm over the moon. I can't wait to play for this club. I'm really looking forward to it.

'The success they have had and the way they have played the game in the last 10 to 15 years has been extraordinary. It's a privilege to be given the chance to be part of that.

'I think they're winners, they're relentless, and that's the sort of team I want to be a part of - champions and people who win trophies. Over the last 10, 12 years, they've dominated, so that's why I wanted to join. As soon as I arrive in Manchester after a break, I will be doing everything I can to establish myself in the City team.

'It's a club built to win trophies and compete at the very top of the game. That is exciting for any footballer. I am so happy to have been given this opportunity, and I am determined to repay the faith City have shown in me.'

Everywhere on the pitch 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/iNouzyZJJp — Manchester City (@ManCity) July 23, 2026

Manchester City director of football Hugo Viana labelled Anderson 'one of the outstanding young midfield talents in world football right now'

Anderson had the most touches (3,300), won the most duels (297) and won the most possession (306) across the Premier League last term.

City say Anderson has experience far beyond his age with 174 senior appearances in club football

Anderson added that Enzo Maresca's intense style of football suits his game and noted that there is plenty of room for improvement.

'I always believed that I could get to this point and this is where I want to be. Now that I'm here, I'll keep pushing and try to take this Club forward. I'm only twenty-three, so I've got plenty of time to get to my best levels, and I'm not there yet - there's more to come from me.

'I'm really looking forward to that (working with Enzo Maresca). I've watched his teams over the past couple of years and spoke to a few of the lads from Chelsea and they all rate him very highly.

'I'm really looking forward to getting to work with him. I like to be intense when I play and use lots of energy around the pitch and get the fans going. So, I think that'll be good.'

Manchester City's director of football Hugo Viana said: 'Elliot is one of the outstanding young midfield talents in world football right now. He offers energy, outstanding work rate and an exceptional range of passing.

'His improvement in recent years has been really impressive and underlines his desire to be the best player he can be. At just 23, there is plenty of opportunity for development over the coming years and we feel he can become a complete midfielder.

'Manchester City is the best place for him to develop his game and keep improving, we are glad that he sees things the same way as we do. I look forward to seeing Elliot working with us ahead of the new season. I'm sure every City fan is excited to see what he can do.'

Anderson is set for three weeks off before joining up with Maresca's side at the end of pre-season.

Sports.title: Leeds in advanced talks with Man City over £35m deal for England goalkeeper James Trafford - just a year after he joined for record £31m
Sports.content:
Leeds in advanced talks with Man City over £35m deal for England goalkeeper James Trafford - just a year after he joined for record £31m

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Leeds United are in advanced negotiations with Manchester City for goalkeeper James Trafford in a deal worth in excess of £35million.

Newcastle United, who have spoken to City in recent weeks about Trafford and tried previously to sign him, are now exploring other options.

The 23-year-old's representatives wish to insert a release clause in any new deal with the expectation that higher placed clubs will be in the market for the England goalkeeper's services further down the line.

Personal terms will not be an issue with Leeds' owners paying competitive salaries.

Trafford joined City last summer in a £27million move from Burnley, just two years after City sold him for £14m, and they expect a substantial profit plus sell-on.

Trafford was expecting to take the No 1 jersey when he signed for Pep Guardiola but was sidelined when City seized an opportunity to sign Gianluigi Donnarumma from Paris St Germain.

Leeds are in talks to sign Manchester City goalkeeper James Trafford, a year after he joined

Trafford ended up playing just four times under Guardiola in the league, but a further 13 cup games as they won the FA Cup and Carabao Cup.

City are now looking to add another goalkeeper as cover for Donnarumma as they negotiate the fee they want for Trafford.

They are continuing discussions with Lille also over a prospective £85million deal for Morocco international midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi.

The 18-year-old's arrival, alongside that of £116m signing Elliot Anderson, would be timely with Rodri due to miss the start of the season with back surgery.

The Spain captain has also yet to agree on a new contract and has one year remaining.

City announced Anderson's arrival from Nottingham Forest yesterday in a deal that made him the second-most expensive British player ever, behind Morgan Rogers, who joined Chelsea for £117m.

The 23-year-old Anderson signed a six year contract and said: 'City are one of the biggest clubs in the world and the squad they have is amazing - so strong in every position. As soon as I knew they wanted me, I was absolutely determined to make this move happen.

'As a footballer, you want to test yourself at the highest level. Being at City means I have that opportunity.

'From the outside looking in, City are a club that treats its players well and provides the perfect environment to excel. The success they have had and the way they have played the game in the last 10 to 15 years has been extraordinary. It's a privilege to be given the chance to be part of that.'

City also want to add a winger and a right-back.

Can Trafford relaunch his career?

​How did it go so wrong for Trafford at his boyhood club? It's only been a year since he re-joined City, but the goalkeeper already seems set to leave the club in search of more playing time.

​It could have been so different. Trafford came through the academy at City, and after impressing in a loan spell at Bolton Wanderers and then subsequently at Burnley in both the Premier League and Championship, he returned believing he was going to be the No1 at the club.

​But that's not how it panned out. Trafford only made three Premier League appearances for the Citizens before he was demoted to No2 after the arrival of Gianluigi Donnarumma from Paris Saint-Germain, and only four in total.

​'It wasn't what I expected coming into the season, and I tried to guard against the situation happening, but it's the reality,' Trafford said following a rare appearance against Salford City in the FA Cup last season.

​Now, if the move goes through, Trafford has the chance to relaunch his career at Leeds. The statistics show that before his disappointing spell back in Manchester, he was on the road to being a top goalkeeper. Hence, City bought him back.

​His performances on loan at both Bolton and Accrington Stanley, where he also spent a season on loan, earned the now England international a move to Burnley for £19m.

Trafford was initially brought back to City as No1 but only made three Premier League appearances before he was replaced by Gianluigi Donnarumma

Trafford showed his true potential when at Burnley in the Championship in the 2024-25 season

​After a bumpy start at the Clarets, in which he conceded 62 goals in 28 starts - and kept only two clean sheets - as they were relegated from the Premier League, Trafford showed his true potential between the sticks.

​As Burnley secured promotion from the Championship in the 2024-25 campaign, earning 100 points, Trafford broke John Ruddy and Paddy Kenny's clean sheet record with a remarkable 29 shutouts in 45 games. He only shipped a record-breaking 16 goals in those matches.

​In that season, Trafford remarkably managed to avoid conceding a single goal between December 22, 2024 and March 4, 2025. In that time, he managed 12 consecutive clean sheets, beating the previous record of nine.

​While Burnley ended up being pipped to the title by Leeds United that season, losing out on goal difference, Trafford was awarded the EFL Championship Player's Player of the season for his heroics in goal.

​Trafford's record-breaking season for the Clarets led to City triggering the buy-back clause they initially included in his sale, wrestling off competition from Newcastle.

While he may not have featured much in the top flight following Donnarumma's arrival, Trafford played every game on City's path to securing their ninth Carabao Cup.

​Trafford saved 88 per cent of the shots he faced during the competition, only conceding two goals and keeping four clean sheets, including one in the final against Arsenal.

​His 14 appearances in all competitions for City have shown he can still cut it at the top level, and he will be looking to relaunch his career in full if he completes the move to Yorkshire.

Sports.title: Inside Jeff Bezos' bid to buy into Liverpool: The role the Amazon billionaire could play, what 'super smart' £1.35bn investment means for transfer business, how it affects FSG - and what happens next
Sports.content:
As soon as the news emerged that Jeff Bezos was interested in forming part of a consortium to buy a stake in Liverpool FC, the jokes began.

Anfield was to become the Amazon Arena, a nod to the company where Bezos made his fortune. New signings would arrive on next-day delivery. Liverpool would not just be competing to be champions of Europe but the galaxy, referring to Bezos's part in the 21st-century space race.

Whatever your opinion on the fourth-richest man in the world, it is hard for Reds fans not to dream of the endless possibilities under a man worth £190billion according to Forbes.

But will Liverpool actually see any of the proposed £1.35bn investment? What role, if any, will Bezos play? And is it time for those supporters to get excited?

Daily Mail Sport has spoken to sources on both sides of the Atlantic to help tackle some of the big questions…

Jeff Bezos has discussed the possibility of joining a consortium which is pushing to buy a stake in Liverpool

Liverpool are in a period of transition with Andoni Iraola taking over as head coach in June

What is going on?

Liverpool's owners Fenway Sports Group are in talks to sell a stake in the club to a consortium backed by Amit Bhatia and funded in part by the family of steel tycoon Lakshmi Mittal.

Bezos is interested in being part of the consortium and other names are also keen to get involved.

Bhatia will be in charge of the bid. He stepped down as co-owner and director of Championship side Queens Park Rangers on Tuesday after nearly two decades at Loftus Road, where he has a stand named after him.

The 46-year-old is the son-in-law of Mittal, the 73rd richest man in the world with £23.4bn to his name per Forbes, and the consortium is keen to buy around £1.3bn in the club.

A spokesperson for Liverpool's owners FSG told Daily Mail Sport earlier this week: 'An investment consortium led, managed, and represented by Amit Bhatia has expressed interest in making a strategic minority investment in Liverpool Football Club.'

It is thought that FSG welcome the potential opportunity and this is another way the conglomerate, who also own the baseball behemoth Boston Red Sox, are looking to further position the club for success.

It would be a similar move, though on a larger scale, to when FSG sold 4 per cent to Dynasty Equity in September 2023. Principal chair John W Henry has always been eager for additional investment while still being keen to hold the majority stake.

FSG sources stress that no deal is signed just yet, with the parties in early discussions at this stage, though the fact the consortium has been put together is a significant development. And there are signals that everyone involved is keen for a deal to be done.

Businessman Amit Bhatia is part of the consortium in talks to buy a stake in the Reds

Would it be a wise move for FSG?

Football finance expert Kieran Maguire certainly thinks so.

He tells Daily Mail Sport: 'As far as the potential Liverpool investment is concerned, it looks like it's going to be up to 30 per cent or £1.3bn. That values the club at just over £4bn, which is broadly in line with expectations.

'From FSG's point of view, it's a super smart piece of business. Yes, they have sold part of the club before but this will ensure they still own a controlling stake of around 60 per cent.

'So in terms of the long-term strategy of the club and the individual transfer windows and recruitment issues, it is still FSG's decisions that are being made. If they are selling 30 per cent, that money goes to FSG not Liverpool, so there is no physical impact upon the club's coffers.

'If the club is looking to borrow money at a future date for whatever circumstances and you are owned by Mittal's son-in-law and Bezos, they will be in a position to lend money on an interest-free basis which can only help in terms of cash flow.

'Also, having a potential partner of the magnitude of Bezos does mean there is the opportunity for synergies. If Amazon Prime want to increase their global influence, then one way could be to do a partnership with Liverpool, whether in terms of content or sponsorship.

'Liverpool goes out to the world and Amazon goes out to the world as well. As well out of the world, maybe! He is flying people into space after all.'

Finance experts believe it would be 'a super smart piece of business' from FSG to sell a stake in the club

What is Bezos's involvement?

Bezos, who made his massive wealth by founding Amazon out of his Seattle garage in 1994 and has since launched ventures such as (the unfortunately-named, for Liverpool fans) space company Blue Origin and the Washington Post news group, is interested.

Sky News reported that Bezos was invited to join the syndicate led by Bhatia. His exit from QPR on Tuesday, the same day the news broke about his interest to invest in Liverpool, came at a telling time.

The intentions of the consortium are clear, though Bezos has historically been cautious when it comes to major sports deals. He was interested in buying the current Super Bowl winners Seattle Seahawks and fellow NFL team Washington Commanders but pulled out.

There has been an influx in similar deals in recent years, notably Ineos' investment in Manchester United and Todd Boehly with Clearlake at Chelsea.

While Boehly is still seen as the figurehead of that move, Behdad Eghbali and Clearlake run the show. Eghbali loves football and has been pleasantly surprised at the English sporting culture when attending games at Stamford Bridge.

Perhaps we will see Bezos in the posh seats at Anfield before too long, too.

It is believed that Bezos was invited to join the syndicate led by Bhatia

What happens next?

The news of FSG being open to selling a stake came as a surprise to many, including some personnel at the club.

It is not said to be an indication that Liverpool's Boston-based owners, who bought the club in 2010, are looking to sell up. If anything, it is part of their strategic plan to position the club to prosper.

Some fans point the finger at FSG for various shortcomings.

They are no saints, for sure – some of their ticketing policies and price hikes have irked many – but they have done far more good than bad during their time as custodians of the club, including regenerating Anfield and financially backing the club into a successful era on the pitch.

As for the consortium, sources believe they are serious.

The day-to-day running of the club would be unlikely to change if it goes through, but being backed by such mega-rich investors can never be a bad thing.

Sports.title: George Russell's World Championship hopes given major boost as Mercedes discover mystery glitch holding him back
Sports.content:
George Russell's World Championship hopes given major boost as Mercedes discover mystery glitch holding him back

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

George Russell’s rocky world championship hopes received a boost as Mercedes discovered the mystery glitch ahead of Sunday’s Hungarian Grand Prix.

The British racer crashed out on the first lap in Belgium last weekend after dramatically losing pace on the Kemmel Straight and tagging Lewis Hamilton’s Ferrari.

The malfunctioning software that led to his retirement was separate from intermittent failures that cost him up to six-tenths per lap in practice.

A despairing Russell likened the initial gremlins to driving with an arm tied behind his back, before ranting over his radio when his race was cut short the next day. ‘Un-f***ing-acceptable,’ he screamed.

Now the 28-year-old, speaking in Budapest, revealed that work back at the factory in Brackley has uncovered the problems. He said: ‘These new power units are exceptionally complex and there was something deeply embedded in the calibration of the code (in the electric component) that was almost impossible to see unless you knew exactly what to look for.

‘I am glad we found it.’

George Russell's World Championship hopes have received a big boost after Mercedes found a mystery glitch holding him back

Despite having slipped to third in the title standings, not only 50 points behind his team-mate Kimi Antonelli but five back from Hamilton, he insisted: ‘I definitely feel this is the most resilient I have been my whole life, and I take pride in my mentality out of the car.

‘My F2 season was a little bit like this. It felt like one thing after another. You bounce back and then you get knocked down again. Three days later I’m feeling good. I am glad there are some positive answers from the factory. Eyes are looking forward now.’

Russell stopped short of apologising for his heated radio outburst, but wanted to play the conciliatory team man.

‘We all hold ourselves to the highest of levels,’ he said. ‘My emotions were exceptionally high because of getting knocked out of the race. Ninety-nine per cent of words over the radio are pure frustration and hot-headedness.

‘I am the first person to look at myself in the mirror and try to improve. We work together. The whole team is standing by me and vice versa.’

Sports.title: West Ham transfer briefing: The four centre backs and three midfielders on shortlist in post-Sullivan overhaul, how Daniel Kretinsky convinced Jarrod Bowen to stay and the five stars heading for the exit
Sports.content:
Life back in the Championship has come with a much-needed boost for West Ham, whose talisman, captain and main goal threat Jarrod Bowen pledged his future to the club. It softens the blow of losing Mateus Fernandes to Tottenham for £85million, and the imminent departure of winger Crysencio Summerville to Al-Hilal in Saudi Arabia. But ahead of the club's first season in the second tier for 15 years and with turmoil off the pitch, the next six weeks will be crucial to ensuring West Ham bounce back to the Premier League at the first time of asking. Here, our expert JAMES SHARPE provides all the information you need to know on the Hammers' latest ins and outs. Jarrod Bowen handed West Ham a much-needed boost by signing a new contract Mateus Fernandes was the first of the big names to leave West Ham this summer, joining Tottenham for £85m What do West Ham need? For a few seasons now, there’s been talk of a much-needed West Ham overhaul. Too many players, signed by too many different people, for too many different managers and, crucially, for too much money, had left an ageing, unbalanced squad not fit for the Premier League. That overhaul never really came but now relegation to the Championship, and the financial constraints that come with it, have forced their hand, while a change in ownership could well see it through. Top stars, though not all of them, have gone and will continue to leave so they need to strengthen all over. So far, the only addition has been making Under 21s loanee Keiber Lamadrid's move permanent from Venezuelan side Deportivo la Guaira. West Ham could do with a new striker. Taty Castellanos did pretty well after arriving for £25m in January but his fellow winter window signing Pablo offered little. For all the dirty work off the ball and his £21.8m fee, he’s yet to score a single goal. Callum Wilson had flirted with extending his contract for another season after a solid debut campaign with several crucial goals that nearly kept the club up, but the Englishman has now joined Brentford on a one-year deal. Nicklas Fullkrug – remember him? – is back from his loan at AC Milan but he is on the list of players the club want to sell if anyone will have him. The £85m departure of all-round midfielder Fernandes leaves a massive hole for Nuno Espirito Santo to fill. Even though Konstantinos Mavropanos, voted Hammer of the Year, has been offered an updated contract similar to the one signed by Bowen, West Ham are still desperate for defensive additions, with further departures expected in that area. West Ham have only made one signing so far this summer - making Keiber Lamadrid's loan move from Venezuela permanent Hammer of the Year Konstantinos Mavropanos has been offered a new deal What’s the latest on Summerville? The Hammers have agreed to sell Summerville to Al Hilal for around £55m. It’s quite the throwback to the good old days of transfer deals, where a fee is agreed first between the buying and selling club. Nowadays, clubs usually agree terms with the prospective player (even though tapping up in an official capacity is still banned) with the fee the last piece of the jigsaw to be thrashed out. This was very much the other way around and, for a while, looked like it could prove a sticking point. Summerville was understood to prefer a move to a European side, despite the heftier wages the Saudis can offer. Summerville was on Manchester United’s radar and the Red Devils held exploratory talks with West Ham. Roma were also seriously interested and while their first offer of £39m was much lower than Al Hilal’s, they have spent the last few days trying to thrash out a more lucrative proposal. However, it is understood Summerville – who scored five goals in 31 Premier League games last season – has now agreed to the Saudi move, meaning the Hammers will bank the best part of £140m for the departure of just two players. Crysencio Summerville is set to join Saudi side Al Hilal for £55m Which other players could leave? Jean-Clair Todibo is keen to depart, and Nuno wants him gone too. The centre back refused to play in West Ham’s final-day relegation decider against Leeds after being substituted just 26 minutes into the penultimate game of the season against Newcastle. A few clubs are interested. Marseille have been keeping tabs as have Juventus but neither have yet tabled bids. They would prefer loans, West Ham wouldn’t but might have no choice. AC Milan had the option to buy Fullkrug this summer after his loan expired but, unsurprisingly, opted against it. Fiorentina have shown loose interest but nothing more. West Ham have accepted that they are unlikely to get back the £27m they paid Borussia Dortmund for him two summers ago. Midfielder Edson Alvarez and goalkeeper Alphonse Areola are also on the ‘for sale’ list, the latter especially now that Mads Hermansen has nailed down his place as Nuno’s No 1 despite the shaky start to his Hammers career. Aaron Wan-Bissaka is also a player West Ham are willing to sell for the right price. They want £25m for him and there’s mild interest from Lazio, while he is on Arsenal’s long-list of targets. There have been rumours that David Moyes is keen to bring him to Everton but sources told Daily Mail Sport that interest is wide of the mark. Jean-Clair Todibo is keen to depart, and head coach Nuno Espirito Santo wants him gone too West Ham want £25m for right back Aaron Wan-Bissaka (left), who is on Arsenal's long-list What convinced Bowen to stay? There was widespread feeling before the summer that relegation would spell the end for the club captain’s time at West Ham. England boss Thomas Tuchel hinted that being embroiled in a relegation scrap for a poor team had hindered Bowen’s chances of selection for his World Cup squad ahead of others, despite scoring and assisting more goals than all the other England wingers in the Premier League last season. ‘Does Jarrod suffer a bit from the situation at his club? It is difficult for him,’ said Tuchel. ‘Does Noni (Madueke) and Bukayo (Saka) profit from the situation of their club (Arsenal)?’ Even father-in-law Danny Dyer said he’d begrudgingly accept Bowen leaving for Real Madrid or Manchester City. No one has to worry about that anymore. Bowen has agreed to stay to try to get West Ham back into the Premier League. The club have inserted a release clause into Bowen’s deal, which kicks in if West Ham fail to secure an instant return to the top flight. He will also receive a fair whack as a bonus if they do. Bowen flew to Prague for talks with Daniel Kretinsky, the impending majority shareholder following the departure of David Sullivan, and his lieutenant Jiri Svarc. The Hammers skipper was impressed by the ambition and clarity of the man soon to be at the helm. Kretinsky knew that the biggest marker he could put down for how the club will be run under his watch was to convince Bowen to stay, not only to give West Ham the best shot at promotion but also to send a message to the rest of the club, squad and prospective signings that they mean business. That Bowen (right) played for a relegated team hurt his chances of making England's World Cup squad as he slipped down the pecking order behind the likes of Bukayo Saka (centre) Owner Daniel Kretinsky managed to convince Bowen to stay over talks in Prague

Your browser does not support iframes.

How is life after Sullivan impacting transfers? At the start of June, Sullivan resigned from his position as co-chair after 16 years at the club in the wake of ‘serious historic allegations’ about his conduct, ones he describes as ‘entirely false’. For all the heads of recruitment or technical directors that have come and gone over the years, it was always Sullivan who had final say on transfers. Insiders believe the club is already working more efficiently, in the knowledge that too many mistakes have been made in the past. Everyone, at last, is pulling in the same direction. Interim CEO Karim Virani is running the ship and new head of recruitment Nils Koppen, who joined from Copenhagen at the start of July, is getting his feet under the table with his data-led approach to identifying targets. The feeling is that everything is more aligned. Nuno is unlikely now to come to work to find out, despite all the planning, that the owner has suddenly spent £30m on an injury-prone striker just because he wants to, although his super agent Jorge Mendes is still believed to be trying to exert his influence. There’s less than a month to go until the Championship opener against promotion rivals Burnley, so already some supporters are starting to get twitchy. The sense from within the club, however, is that they are finally implementing a process they can trust, one in which they don’t have to panic buy. New head of recruitment Nils Koppen (pictured) has reunited with interim CEO Karim Virani, who he worked with previously at Rangers How much money do they have to spend? With almost £140m in the bank from just two sales, one might think West Ham are all set to splash the cash. It’s not quite that straightforward just yet. West Ham lost £104.2m in their most recent accounts and the club need to make sure they comply with new Squad Cost Rules (SCR) for this season that limit spending on transfers, wages and agent fees to 85 per cent of revenue. SCR, at least, will ignore the huge losses they made. Club sources suggested how much of their transfer incomings can be splashed on future signings will become clearer once the ownership issues, the passing of shares and discussions over outstanding debts, have been resolved. The priority first is making sure the club is viable and in line with SCR. Kretinsky is expected to inject a substantial amount once he takes de facto control, with SCR allowing owner injections of up to £33m over three years. That’s not to say that West Ham aren’t pressing ahead with targets, even if sources suggested that incoming deals may happen later in the window. As such, Koppen has also informed the club’s youngsters that it will be a week or two until they find out whether they will be a part of the first team or shipped out on loan. Who are they after? Axel Disasi, who made a superb impact on loan from Chelsea last season, is their key target but does not want to commit to Championship football at this stage of the window and would prefer to find himself a new club in the Premier League or overseas. Chelsea are believed to want £25m for the 28-year-old Frenchman. Southampton centre back Taylor Harwood-Bellis is on West Ham's shortlist for centre backs The Hammers are also keen on Celtic's Arne Engels, a former target of Nottingham Forest They have enquired about Midtjylland and Ecuador midfielder Denil Castillo (right) Cardiff’s Dylan Lawlor and Leicester’s Ben Nelson are also options on their defender shortlist, as well as Southampton centre back Taylor Harwood-Bellis. The departure of Fernandes has left them keen to bolster the midfield and West Ham are understood to have enquired about Portugal Under-21 international Gustavo Sa at Famalicao and Denil Castillo at Midtjylland, who was an unused substitute in all of Ecuador’s games at the World Cup. The Hammers are also keen on Arne Engels at Celtic, whom Nottingham Forest tried to sign for £25m in January. The Belgian is said to want to test himself at a higher level and there’s a feeling among sources in Scotland that the summer is the ideal time to cash in on one of their main assets. Insiders say any deal could hinge on whether Celtic get a deal over the line for Paderborn midfielder Mika Baur.

Sports.title: Argentina assistant coach explains reason behind Dani Olmo 'punch' in ugly post-World Cup final scenes - as he insists 'it was more of a push'
Sports.content:
Argentina assistant coach explains reason behind Dani Olmo 'punch' in ugly post-World Cup final scenes - as he insists 'it was more of a push'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Argentina assistant coach Roberto Ayala has attempted to downplay his post-match clashes with Spain's players after the World Cup final.

Lionel Scaloni's side were so close to retaining their title on Sunday after lifting the trophy in 2022, but were beaten 1-0 by Spain following a tense and scrappy affair.

They were aggressive throughout the match, as they had been during their semi-final victory over England, yet things escalated at the end of the game.

Having already had Enzo Fernandez sent off for a wild late challenge on Pau Cubarsi towards the end of normal time, Paredes grabbed Eric Garcia by the throat and pushed Gavi to the ground by putting his hand in the Spaniard's face.

Nahuel Molina also thumped Rodri in the torso as he was running by to celebrate Spain's triumph, while Thiago Almada was involved, too.

Paredes even appeared to throw punches during the altercations and Ayala, who is Scaloni's assistant, held Garcia around the throat before he was caught on camera striking Dani Olmo.

Argentina coach Roberto Ayala has tried to downplay his clashes with Spain's players

Ayala clashed with Eric Garcia before he appeared to strike Dani Olmo after Sunday's final

Then, as the Spanish squad lifted the trophy, Argentina's players faced away from their opponents in what was viewed by many as a poor show of sportsmanship.

FIFA have since launched an investigation into their behaviour, which could have serious consequences for those involved.

However, Ayala has attempted to defend what happened, insisting his clash was 'more of a push than anything else'.

Addressing the incident for the first time, he told Esports Migdia on Valencia Capital Radio: 'Obviously I’m sorry. Because of my position, I can’t allow a feeling, or what I might receive from the other party, to change my mood and my actions.

'I’m sorry, but for me, these are things that stay there and that’s it. For me, things need to be put behind us and left there.

'It was more of a push than anything else, it wasn’t a punch like they’re saying, and that’s it. It was a reaction to something he said, but that’s it. If I see him, I’ll obviously apologise to him in person.'

Ayala then tried to add further context to the general ugly scenes on the pitch at the MetLife Stadium as he added: 'It’s a shame, and you have to accept the facts and the things you’ve done on the field.

'When the game ends, what I see is a fight in the middle of the pitch, and we rush to go after our players, and it ends up like that because that’s not who we are.

'I take responsibility for what I did. My intention was to go and separate them, that was my intention, but sometimes things happen and emotions run high, but that’s no excuse.

'And given my position, my behaviour has to be different, regardless of what I receive.'

Ayala (right), a former Argentine international, serves as assistant to boss Lionel Scaloni

Announcing their probe into what had gone on in the aftermath of Sunday's game, FIFA said: 'Following an assessment of the relevant match reports for the FIFA World Cup final between Spain and Argentina, and in line with article 36 of the FIFA disciplinary code (FDC), the FIFA disciplinary committee has appointed a disciplinary and ethics prosecutor to investigate potential breaches of the FDC with regard to the post-match incidents.

'Further details will be communicated by the FIFA disciplinary committee once the prosecutor’s report has been completed.'

Despite the nasty scenes, Spain midfielder Gavi, who was pushed to the ground by Paredes amid the chaos, surprisingly defended his Argentine counterparts.

During Spain's celebrations back home, Gavi was asked for his take on what had gone on and said: 'No, to tell you the truth, I don't think he (Leandro Paredes) should be suspended.

'I understand it's not a good image for children, but I think there's also that side to football, which is a bit more physical, more aggressive.

'The most logical thing would have been to send him off during the match, and that's it. In the end, I think it's all football, and it has to be that way.'

Sports.title: Lionel Messi's Inter Miami return with comical own goal in highly-anticipated first MLS game after the World Cup
Sports.content:
Defending MLS Cup champions Inter Miami returned to play after the World Cup and it appears that there is still some rust 'The Herons' need to knock off.

While runner-up Lionel Messi was not present as he rested following Argentina's defeat, friend Luis Suarez and Inter Miami re-started their season against the Chicago Fire, who recently acquired Barcelona striker Robert Lewandowski.

But just moments into the match, Miami keeper Rocco Rios Novo committed a horrific blunder to put his team behind the 8-ball.

Playing the ball out of the back, Novo was in position to receive a pass from his defender, Ian Fray in the 18th minute.

But rather than send the ball up the pitch, Novo whiffed on the kick entirely and watched as it rolled under his foot and into the back of his own net.

The crowd at the Nu Stadium were stunned into silence as Novo was made to do a walk of shame to get the ball from the back of his net.

Inter Miami keeper Rocco Rios Novo made a stunning error in his first game back from break

Novo horribly misplayed a backpass from a defender and watched as it rolled into his own net

Despite this, Novo and Inter Miami pulled out a 3-2 victory over the Chicago Fire

Just how everyone predicted! pic.twitter.com/tzmsY9ERnm — Chicago Fire FC (@ChicagoFire) July 23, 2026

Lewandowski, who was playing in his first match since joining the Fire in the summer, was standing right by Novo and waited to jump on any mistakes. Instead, Novo did the work for him.

However, as horrible as the mistake was, Novo and Inter Miami still pulled out a 3-2 victory over Chicago despite being without Messi and Argentina teammate Rodrigo De Paul.

Suarez bagged a brace with goals in the 27th and 51st minutes before Chicago's Puso Dithejane evened the game in the 67th.

Miami pulled out the winner when 20-year-old midfielder Preston Plambeck buried a shot in the back of the net just three minutes before the 90.

Inter Miami sit second in the MLS standings in both the Supporters Shield and the Eastern Conference, now five points behind leaders Nashville SC.

Sports.title: BHA freezes activity of leading syndicate after members complain they’ve not been paid
Sports.content:
BHA freezes activity of leading syndicate after members complain they’ve not been paid

No entries or declarations will be allowed for Deva Racing whose flagship horse Imperial Emperor has won nearly £1.5 million in prize-money

View 4 Images Imperial Emperor is a star for Deva Racing run by Ryan Tongue (inset)

The BHA has put a stop to entries and declarations for horses owned by a popular racing syndicate after members complained they had not been paid.

The Deva Racing Syndicate has a dozen horses in training in stables in Britain, the US and Dubai, managed by Ryan Tongue, who as a teenager served tea to 20-champion jockey Sir AP McCoy when he worked in the Worcester weighing room.

Tongue, 30, has worked in a number of roles in racing, briefly as a jockey and then as a racing manager when he was involved in the purchase of dual Grand National winner I Am Maximus for the late owner Michael Grech.

‌



Seven years ago he took over Deva Racing, whose flagship horse Imperial Emperor brought the syndicate to national attention through his exploits in Dubai.

Trawlerman vs Scandinavia Goodwood Cup rematch set after Gold Cup thriller READ MORE :

The gelding, who was bought from Godolphin for £63,000 and put into training with local champion trainer Bhupat Seemar, has been transformed into a dirt performer.

He has won five of his eight starts for Seemar and earned a start in the last two runnings of the Dubai World Cup, one of the world’s richest races.

View 4 Images Deva Racing members on the podium in Dubai (Image: Dubai Racing Club)

After two victories, including at Group 1 level during the latest carnival and a fourth place in the World Cup, his winnings have risen to nearly £1.5 million.

However attempts by syndicate members to secure their share of the prize-money from his latest campaign have been unsuccessful and as a result the problems have been brought to the attention of the BHA.

‌



One of the members, Tom Walton from Leeds, who works for a Manchester law firm, told Mirror Racing: “We have uncovered the overselling of shares and ultimately Ryan has kept prize-money.

View 4 Images Imperial Emperor has won nearly £1.5 million (Image: Dubai Racing Club)

“I got paid roughly £7,000 last year but I do know of one syndicate member who got nothing. We’ve not received any prize-money from this season when the horse won £760,000.

‌



“The last response I had from Ryan was on June 19 which said he wouldn’t be speaking to me, only to another member Mark. Ryan then blocked me and Mark is getting no response too.

“The BHA gave him a deadline and he told them he would endeavour to pay within 60 days but he was currently experiencing ill-health.”

In April, Walton discovered that Imperial Emperor had been entered in an online auction in Dubai without his knowledge. The gelding was withdrawn from the sale and the 20 original owning members subsequently completed a deal to buy the horse.

‌



View 4 Images Bhupat Seemar, the trainer of Imperial Emperor (Image: YouTube)

Walton said: “I wouldn’t want this experience to put anyone off getting involved in racing. Ryan and Deva are certainly outliers. The shining light is we’ve still got the horse and we can run him next season.

“I’ve kind of written the money off but what I want is to make sure that Ryan and Deva don’t have any involvement in racing again.

“I am presently a part owner in a syndicate run by My Future Champion. They’re a great outfit and I don’t want this experience to stain the whole syndicate world when there’s one like them around.”

A spokesperson for the BHA said “We can confirm that the BHA has put a stop on entries and declarations being made for Deva Racing Syndicate horses trained in Britain. We encourage any concerned syndicate members to contact the BHA on intel@britishhorseracing.com. We will be making no further comment regarding this matter at this time.”

Ryan Tongue has been approached for comment.

Sports.title: Newsboy’s horseracing tips for Friday’s six meetings, including Ascot Nap
Sports.content:
Newsboy’s horseracing tips for Friday’s six meetings, including Ascot Nap

Newsboy fancies his Nap, Paradise Walk, to win at Ascot and also hopes Imperial Cult can score at Sandown and complete his Daily Double

View 2 Images Ascot hosts a six-race Flat meeting on Friday when Newsboy’s nap, Paradise Walk, is fancied to win the finale (5.12) (Image: John Walton/PA Wire)

PARADISE WALK looks ripe for a hat-trick in the Sodexo Live! Fillies' Handicap (5.12) at Ascot on Friday afternoon. The Ralph Beckett-trained daughter of Starman qualified for a British Horseracing Authority handicap mark of 78 on the back of second placings at Chelmsford City and Southwell and Wolverhampton. Fitted with blinkers, Paradise Walk didn’t shine on her debut in the sphere when ninth to Cinque Verde on the first day of Newmarket’s Guineas Festival at the beginning of May. But Paradise Walk took a big step forward to gain a first career success from three rivals in a six-furlong handicap at Windsor next time, beating Space Party by three-quarters of a length. And my selection followed up back at five when accounting for Secret Mistral at Nottingham last time out. The assessor’s latest recalculation means that Hector Crouch’s partner must compete from a rating of 80 after a 4lb rise. But there is more to come and a third straight win is on the cards.

‌

At Sandown, IMPERIAL CULT and Jack Callan are expected to prove a potent combination in the Close Brothers Asset Finance Apprentice Handicap (5.15). After all-weather successes at Lingfield and Kempton Park, George Baker’s seven-year-old stumbled leaving the stalls in search of the hat-trick at Epsom but still rattled home to be beaten less than a length in fourth behind Super Hit. Granted better luck at the start, Imperial Cult can resume normal service.

Sports.title: Top jockey Rossa Ryan banned for 28 days after defeat on horse that ‘would have won’
Sports.content:
Top jockey Rossa Ryan banned for 28 days after defeat on horse that ‘would have won’

The rider’s chances of landing a first Flat jockeys’ championship are effectively over after he eased up too soon on a horse and was beaten by a nose at Sandown on Thursday

View 2 Images Thunder Home (far side) is caught on the line by Zero Error (Image: https://x.com/RacingTV)

Top jockey Rossa Ryan was banned for 28 days on Thursday after he was defeated on a horse that ‘would have finished first’.

‌



The 26-year-old is pursuing a first success in the Flat jockeys’ championship and was in third place behind, 11 winners behind Billy Loughnane and ten off Oisin Murphy at the start of the day. He looked set to claim one win back at Sandown in a maiden race for two-year-olds on the James Horton-trained Thunder Home.

‌



The 14-1 chance made the running and was ridden clear of his rivals with a furlong to run. He opened up a three length break over the rest but Zero Error, under Jamie Spencer, began to rattle home and, as Ryan was easing down in expectation of victory, that rival snatched success by a nose.

‌



Trawlerman vs Scandinavia Goodwood Cup rematch set after Gold Cup thriller READ MORE :

National Racehorse Week coming to Liverpool and Portsmouth with 76 yards open to public READ MORE :

Ryan was summoned to a stewards inquiry to explain his actions on the son of Night Of Thunder who was having his third start.

The stewards report said: “Rossa Ryan, the rider of THUNDER HOME (IRE), had appeared stop riding on the run to the line before recommencing his ride in the final strides to finish second, beaten by a nose.

‌



View 2 Images Rossa Ryan: banned for 28 days (Image: Getty Images)

“After being interviewed and shown recordings of the incident, Ryan was suspended for 28 days for failing to take all reasonable and permissible measures to obtain the best possible placing on a horse that would have finished first.”

Ryan, who is first jockey to Ralph Beckett for whom he has won the Prix de l’Arc de Triomphe and a Breeders’ Cup, will be sidelined from August 6 to September 2 inclusive.

He will miss several big races including the York Ebor Festival.

Sports.title: Jurgen Klopp favourite has told Andoni Iraola all about Liverpool target Maghnes Akliouche
Sports.content:
Jurgen Klopp favourite has told Andoni Iraola all about Liverpool target Maghnes Akliouche

Liverpool made an approach for Monaco's Maghnes Akliouche earlier in the transfer window

View 2 Images Liverpool have made an approach for Monaco star Maghnes Akliouche (Image: Francesco Scaccianoce - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images)

Former Liverpool star Takumi Minamino has already offered a glimpse into what the club might expect from Maghnes Akliouche. The duo have been teammates at Monaco since 2022.

‌



The Liverpool ECHO reported that the Reds made an initial approach for Akliouche as the club continue to hunt for wingers this summer. Liverpool contacted Monaco earlier in the transfer window to gauge Akliouche's availability, with wide options becoming a focus following Mohamed Salah's farewell.

‌



The 24-year-old netted seven goals and laid on 11 assists for the Ligue 1 outfit last season. The forward has reportedly been the subject of three rejected bids from Paris Saint-Germain.

‌



Whether the France international will sign for Liverpool and link up with summer recruit Victor Munoz in refreshing the club's attacking width remains uncertain. However, former Liverpool player Minamino has previously lauded Akliouche's character and his ability with the ball.

"When I arrived at the club, I noticed him straight away, he was the best young player in the team," Minamino told Monaco's club website in December 2024. "He has huge potential and he showed it last year against several teams.

‌



Jurgen Klopp set to appoint TWO ex-Liverpool coaches in Germany backroom team READ MORE :

OPINION Five standout World Cup stars Liverpool could sign next to answer Andoni Iraola plea by Ben Crawford

"He is always humble, he is a good player but also a good person above all. I am sure he will have a good future so I am happy to be able to play with him."

Minamino was often a backup option throughout his Liverpool career, but played alongside several prolific forwards during his time at the club. Shortly after Minamino completed his move to Monaco in 2022, Jurgen Klopp paid tribute to what the Japan international, who made 55 Liverpool appearances and claimed the 2020 Premier League title, had contributed to the side.

‌



"We miss him honestly. He is a fantastic player and he was a fantastic part of our squad," Klopp said. "We should not forget, as an offensive player coming to Liverpool in a time when the settled front three were Mane, Firmino, Salah; the new signing was Diogo Jota -- it's not like you have to be a bad player to not be in the first lineup.

"No, you have to be a world-class player to be around [the starting XI] and to be the next coming on, so Taki [Minamino] did that incredibly well for us."

View 2 Images Takumi Minamino and Akliouche have been Monaco teammates since 2022 (Image: Valery HACHE / AFP via Getty Images)

‌



New boss Andoni Iraola will be eager to forge an equally devastating attack during his tenure as Liverpool manager. However, the Spanish coach has been candid about the need to bolster his wide options following the earlier acquisition of Munoz from Osasuna.

"No, I think it is difficult to say a number when the market is open," Iraola said. "You have to be always open to new options to improve the squad. There are obvious situations where we need to sign players.

"A winger for example, we definitely need to sign a winger, but there are other situations where we will have to analyse what the market gives you, what is the cost, how we also see the players we have."

Sports.title: Trawlerman vs Scandinavia Goodwood Cup rematch set after Gold Cup thriller
Sports.content:
Trawlerman vs Scandinavia Goodwood Cup rematch set after Gold Cup thriller

Trawlerman and Scandinavia are set to renew their rivalry in the Al Shaqab Goodwood Cup after their epic Royal Ascot Gold Cup battle

View 3 Images Trawlerman won The Gold Cup at Royal Ascot in 2025

The Trawlerman camp are eagerly anticipating another thrilling contest when their veteran stayer goes head-to-head with Scandinavia for the second time in the Al Shaqab Goodwood Cup.

‌



Aidan O'Brien's Justify colt snatched the crown from the eight-year-old after two-and-a-half miles of gripping Gold Cup drama at Royal Ascot, where just a head divided the pair at the line. The stage is now set for a rematch, with Scandinavia arriving as the reigning champion and the division's most exciting emerging force.

‌



Yet this is also a race in which John and Thady Gosden have carved out considerable success over the years, courtesy of four-time winner Stradivarius, and they remain confident their current long-distance standard-bearer will give everything once more.

‌



National Racehorse Week coming to Liverpool and Portsmouth with 76 yards open to public READ MORE :

Frankie Dettori responds to cheeky suggestion he could make another dramatic comeback READ MORE :

Thady Gosden said: "What is fantastic in the staying division is you have horses that people know and have been around for a long time. To have an older horse like Trawlerman, who has done it all before and is trying to maintain his level, and then a younger horse in Scandinavia coming to take him on is brilliant.

"At the end of two and a half miles at Ascot there were only inches between them, which is I guess what it is all about. Hopefully they will deliver a race everyone wants to see again.

"Trawlerman ran a huge race against Scandinavia at Ascot and we'll have to see how we get on against him this time. But he's in great form and I'm sure he will put up a great fight.

‌



"The Goodwood Cup is a fantastic race to win. It's one of the main staying races in the middle of the summer and it would be fantastic to see him run a big one in it."

View 3 Images Just a head separated Scandinavia (right) and Trawlerman at the end of the Gold Cup (Image: Mike Egerton/PA Wire)

Not only was Trawlerman making his seasonal debut in the Gold Cup, but it also marked the first occasion he had been spotted on a racecourse wearing the goggles he now dons during the preliminaries.

‌



They will be back on display when he heads to the Sussex Downs, with the Gosdens brimming with admiration for the staying power of a horse that has worked his way steadily up through the ranks during his time at Clarehaven to become one of the Newmarket yard's most beloved names.

View 3 Images Trawlerman wearing ski goggles in the parade ring (Image: John Walton/PA Wire)

Gosden continued: "The goggles are an unusual thing that I guess you don't see very often, or ever really, he wears them every day (to help with an eye condition) and it seems to work.

Article continues below

"It's great to have a horse with his mentality. He has had his issues and is an older horse now, but he is mentally so resilient.

"He must have been up Warren Hill thousands of times by now, but he's up here every day loving it and enjoying it like it's his first time. He had a long layoff before the Gold Cup and a hard race, but was back out here two days later bucking and squealing wanting to do a bit more.

"It's a real privilege to have him and he's rare. You don't need to do anything different to keep him interested and he's always up for it, always enjoying it. I'm sure one day he will move on to do something else, but when that day comes I'm sure he'll miss us and this as much as we will miss him."

Sports.title: Argentina were rotten, violent losers but Liverpool star must now use his misplaced anger
Sports.content:
Argentina were rotten, violent losers but Liverpool star must now use his misplaced anger

Argentina midfielder Alexis Mac Allister claimed other countries have been rejoicing in his country's loss to Spain in the final but Andoni Iraola will be more interested in seeing how it affects his club form

View 2 Images Alexis Mac Allister will return to Liverpool after Argentina's World Cup shenanigans (Image: 2026 Liverpool FC)

Whatever your take on the behaviour of Argentina’s players during and after the World Cup final, you have to admire their siege mentality.

‌



They are getting flak from many angles but are simply doubling down on how proud they are and how the criticism will only make them stronger. There will be no apologies now, or ever. Patriotism is tough to measure but there is clearly no shortage of it amongst Argentinian footballers.

‌



And as a rule, their messages to supporters and their nation tend to be a little more emotional than those put out by English players. Lisandro Martinez even channelled some popular modern philosophy into his reflections on the proceedings.

‌



“Remember that the fall of the great is the joy of the mediocre,” posted Martinez. His Liverpool counterpart, Alexis Mac Allister warmed to the theme, writing: “Thank you to those from other countries who send us messages mocking or rejoicing in our pain. Without meaning to, you help us feel more and more proud to be Argentinian every day.”

Andoni Iraola clarifies future of two Liverpool stars linked with exits READ MORE :

Rodri to Real Madrid transfer truth as Man City contract stipulation revealed READ MORE :

It does not sound as though Mac Allister is up for saying sorry for the conduct of some of his team-mates any time soon. And when he refers to ‘other countries’, you can be sure England is at the top of his list.

It will be intriguing to see what sort of receptions the Premier League’s Argentinian players will get when the new club season starts in the middle of next month. There is unlikely to be open hostility but there will most definitely be reminders of how they behaved in New Jersey on the game’s biggest stage.

‌



When Mac Allister says people were ‘mocking or rejoicing in our pain’, he was mistaken. People were not ‘mocking or rejoicing’, they were simply pointing out that Argentina, on this occasion, proved to be rotten, violent losers.

View 2 Images Alexis Mac Allister was one of Argentina's most influential players in their run to the World Cup final (Image: Juan Luis Diaz/Quality Sport Images/Getty Images)

The same will be pointed out to Mac Allister and Martinez when they take to the field for Liverpool and Manchester United in the Premier League. And Andoni Iraola, in particular, will be hoping the antipathy towards Argentina’s national side proves to be a spur for Mac Allister after what was pretty much a season-long trough in form.

‌



In 37 Premier League appearances for Liverpool last season, Mac Allister contributed two goals and four assists. In 35 appearances in the 2024/25 campaign, he contributed five goals and five assists.

He was tireless in the World Cup - only Rodri covered more distance in the tournament - but often looked off the pace as Liverpool laboured to their fifth-placed finish. After reports linking Mac Allister with a move to Real Madrid, Iraola was compelled to stress that he wanted to keep the 27-year-old.

The new Liverpool manager said: “I think Alexis has been one of the best players at the club for the last few years, and he has had a very good World Cup, so it is normal that other clubs want our best players. But I want to keep my good players.”

‌



Fair enough. But there is surely no doubt he wants to keep the Mac Allister of 24/25 rather than the Mac Allister of 25/26.

Perhaps his anger at the ‘mocking and rejoicing’ will inspire him to get back to his best. Liverpool fans and Iraola will certainly hope so.

Sports.title: Furious Argentina fans launch petition to replay 'corrupt' Spain World Cup final
Sports.content:
Furious Argentina fans launch petition to replay 'corrupt' Spain World Cup final

Argentina were denied back-to-back World Cup titles when Spain beat them 1-0 in the final in New Jersey and their furious supporters are not taking the loss well

View 2 Images Spain lifted the World Cup on Sunday (Image: Getty Images)

Thousands of angry Argentina fans are demanding that the World Cup final be replayed due to a "corrupt" referee.

‌



Argentina were beaten 1-0 by Spain in extra time of the showpiece finale in New Jersey on Sunday. Ferran Torres' goal settled it for the dominant Spanish side, who bombarded the Argentina goal throughout the match.

‌



Defending champions Argentina failed to muster a single shot on target over the 120 minutes and were down to 10 men following Enzo Fernandez's red card in the 93rd minute. Goalkeeper Emi Martinez was extremely busy before finally being beaten by Torres' effort in the 106th minute.

‌



Argentina did not take the defeat well, with ugly scenes following the full-time whistle. Leandro Paredes was spotted kicking and punching as he shoved Eric Garcia to the ground and grappled with Gavi, while Nauel Molina appeared to have instigated the altercation by throwing a punch at Rodri.

Norway to make formal Donald Trump complaint over 'serious' breach of World Cup rules READ MORE :

Mirror readers crown World Cup's best pundit as Wayne Rooney beats Roy Keane READ MORE :

Some fans of the team are similarly bitter, judging by the more than 82,000 signatures on a petition calling for the final to be replayed. The Change.org petition's author Gisela Sanchez argues that FIFA should scrub the result due to the performance of Slovenian referee Slavko Vincic.

“The recent final between Argentina and Spain was tarnished by the controversial and corrupt performance of the referee who, according to video evidence, was bought to influence the match’s outcome," Sanchez writes.

‌



“It is a monumental disappointment for the players, coaches, and, above all, for the fans who crave to see a game decided by talent and dedication on the pitch, and not by rigged refereeing decisions.

“If we allow corruption to go unnoticed on this global stage, we are setting a bad example for future generations of athletes and fans.

View 2 Images Slavko Vincic was busy in the World Cup final (Image: Buda Mendes, Getty Images)

‌



“Therefore, we ask Fifa to review these incidents with seriousness and transparency, and to consider replaying the final – this time without the influence of a corrupt referee.”

Change.org is flooded with petitions of a very different nature - ones which call for FIFA to ban Argentina from future tournaments. One calling for the team to be banned from ALL future World Cups racked up over 29 million signatures before closing.

Vincic blew his whistle on 46 occasions for fouls, 25 of which were committed by Argentina players. Fernandez was sent off after picking up two yellow cards in the second half - one for dissent having not been awarded a free-kick and one for a reckless challenge on Pau Cubarsi.

‌



The match was played in a stop-start nature due to Argentina's spoiling tactics, but Spain eventually found a way through in extra time. FIFA are investigating the behaviour of Argentina's players in the aftermath of the match, which was widely slammed.

"It's a disgrace," Gary Neville said on ITV. “I love the competitiveness of the Argentines, fighting and scrapping for their lives, Messi has propped them up, but it’s been a disgrace the last few games."

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
