World.title: Presidential nominee Indrek Laul: I aim to unite parties, worldviews
World.content:
Presidential candidate nominee Indrek Laul says he wants to unite parties and different worldviews, following his nomination Thursday.

A total of 30 public figures including from the spheres of culture, business and academia issued a letter endorsing Laul, 58, as a candidate for September's presidential elections. He is the CEO of Estonia Pianos, a manufacturer of high-end grand pianos.

You have been proposed as a presidential candidate. Have you personally agreed to it?

Yes.

Why did you opt to accept?

My life experience has been in business, especially in Estonian exports, as well as in culture and education. It has also included representing Estonia abroad, together with my experience in charitable work in Estonia.

I would also mention the American Chamber of Commerce, where I have served as president for the past nine years. I have sat on the supervisory boards of several institutions. The experience gained from all of this has led me to think that now is the time to give back.

Was becoming a presidential candidate something you wanted yourself, or did the proposal come from someone else?

These thoughts have been there before. In 2021, President Toomas Hendrik Ilves encouraged me so much that I drew up ideas about what could be done in Kadriorg, and those ideas were also sent to Riigikogu members.

This time I have been in contact with several politicians, and as you will have seen, the broad public support that has emerged has given me the confidence to say yes to this candidacy.

Who are the politicians you have been in contact with?

I have been in contact with several politicians from different parties, and that has given me the impression that it is worth putting forward my candidacy.

Could you name any of those politicians or any of the parties?

I would rather not go into names at this stage. But I would like to say that I was invited to an official meeting at 2 p.m. today with the Isamaa Riigikogu group.

Would you say that your worldview aligns with that of Isamaa?

My worldview is so diverse that I am not a candidate for any one party. The reverse, I would seek to bring together different worldviews and different parties. I could even say different communities and ethnic groups, and find the common ground, the shared purpose that would unite us all, encourage cooperation, and direct us to do what Estonia needs.

How would you assess your support level among politicians at the moment? What do you think it might be?

The first meeting is with the first party today. I very much hope that the other parties will also invite me, and then we can see what level of support there will be.

Have you already started calculating how many votes you would need and how much support you currently have?

I have been thinking about it and have also met with several members of the Riigikogu to discuss the possibilities. And as to how everything develops, only time will tell.

Could you elaborate a little on those thoughts?

They are guiding principles. When we talk about what Estonia needs, what could unite us, what the challenges of our era are, I concluded that it could be the welfare of the people. The concept of the people's welfare is a historical one. It goes back to Ancient Rome, where the philosopher Cicero set as a goal for the republic that the welfare of the people should be the supreme law.

It was the first two words of that phrase, salus populi, meaning "the welfare of the people," that particularly engrossed me. Welfare itself encompasses three things: the well-being of the people, security, and the sustainability of the nation. Those are the three themes that can be brought together under the concept of welfare, with the goal of national unity and bringing people together. I believe that is a very worthy objective, and history has shown it to be a very fitting one.

Indrek Laul with one of the Estonia-made grand pianos, on the "Klassikatähed 2025" TV show. Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

At this point, it is appropriate to ask what your vision is of the role of the President of Estonia. What sort of president would you strive to be?

One of the president's primary responsibilities is to uphold the Constitution and defend the values that stem from it. We know these from the preamble to the Constitution: freedom, justice, the rule of law, internal and external peace, and, as it is very clearly written, ensuring the preservation of the Estonian nation, language, and culture through the ages.

But as I mentioned earlier, every era has its own challenges. I believe we need a president with a clear vision, international experience, broad expertise, and whose heartfelt desire and mission is to give back.

What are the challenges facing Estonia today that you would want to focus on as president?

First, the well-being of the people requires a strong and growing economy. Exports are what make nations wealthier. In this respect, the president can provide support, contribute from personal experience, and open doors for Estonian exporters, scientists, and innovators. Some of this is already reflected in the TAIE (Research, Development, Innovation, and Entrepreneurship) 2035 program.

Estonia is most rich in talent and gifted people. I believe that what I have managed to achieve with pianos — raising our pianos from a little-known country into the world's top tier — goes to show what is possible.

I would like to highlight the people and talents we have, so that we can all feel great pride and joy in the prosperity that an export-driven economy can provide. This also includes cultural exports and educational exports. We are a small country, and if we want to grow, we must look outward. Second, security. Security also means a sense of safety. The president has a clear role here. I have met with retired major generals. They have sent me written recommendations about the president's role, and more continue to come in. They are excellent recommendations, and I want to follow them. They provide valuable guidance on how the president can contribute to our security.

At the same time, Estonia will naturally continue strengthening its defense capabilities. We need very strong relations with our NATO allies, especially with the U.S., with whom I have decades of experience in maintaining relations, and we will continue supporting Ukraine.

Third, the sustainability of the nation means that everyone should have a good life here. Young people should want to stay in Estonia, start families, and see opportunities for self-fulfillment here. Then children will follow.

The president has a very important role in bringing people together so that we do not emphasize our differences but instead find common goals and take great pride in Estonia.

You have mentioned both domestic and foreign policy issues. Which of the two are closer to your heart both at the moment, and perhaps as a future president?

I would say that both are highly important. The three issues I spoke about — the well-being of the people, national security, and sustainability — are interconnected. If we want a stronger economy, we must focus on exports and develop high-value-added products so that we have a strong export economy because, once again, that is what brings money into Estonia. That, in turn, strengthens our domestic policy and internal security. It gives us the resources to finance the challenges our era has set before us. So both are important, and the president must be able to deal with them.

If we look at President Alar Karis's public approval rating in Estonia, it is quite high. What would you do differently as president, than Alar Karis did?

I would like to sincerely commend President Karis for the work he has done, and I hope that the next president will be able to continue from there with dignity.

Looking back to 2016 and 2021, your name also came up as a potential presidential candidate. Why was your candidacy not formally put forward then?

At the time, I understood that there were discussions taking place. I took it as kind support and recognition. I also shared ideas about what could be done in Kadriorg, but it was not nearly as purposeful a process as it is this time.

So is it now certain that you genuinely want to be president?

Those people who have come forward to support me are highly respected individuals. I am deeply grateful for their support, and I also feel the responsibility it brings. When people come forward and give you that kind of backing, and when that circle is much broader, then I believe the "yes" that I have given stands.

So you do want to become president?

The choice belongs to the members of the Riigikogu, and that is wholly democratic. It shows that democracy in Estonia works when there are choices.

But would you prefer your candidacy to gain enough of a backing at the Riigikogu, or would you also be prepared to go to the electoral college?

That decision is to be made by the members of parliament as to how the process proceeds. I hope to be invited to meet with the parties so that I can present my ideas.

Let me return briefly to a question I asked at the beginning of the interview. Which party are you most looking forward to meeting? Which party do you currently find most appealing?

Isamaa was the first to invite me at its own initiative, and I very much hope that the other parties will also extend invitations. I do not see any other option here. The Constitution requires us to find a consensus candidate.

The requirement of 68 votes out of 101 also reflects the spirit and substance of the Constitution — that a consensus candidate should be found. I will strive to be that consensus candidate, one who brings together different parties and different worldviews.

Throughout this interview, you have not mentioned any party other than Isamaa, and then only because you are meeting with them. Could your comments be taken to mean that your views align most closely with Isamaa's?

No, they cannot.

Let's talk a little about what happens next. Do you have a campaign team?

I have had supporters, and I am grateful to many people who have contributed.

But do you have a separate team that will actually run your campaign?

There is no large team. Instead, there are volunteers who have helped of their own free will, both with ideas and with practical work.

Are these volunteers your friends or acquaintances?

Yes, they are both.

World.title: OTP Bank makes boldest dreams in Russia come true
World.content:
The company acquiring Luminor, one of Estonia's largest banks, promises to grant private clients in Russia loans of three million rubles in three minutes, writes Argo Ideon. A wide range of services is available for Russian enterprises.

When I read on Monday morning that Luminor, a local bank operating in the Baltic states, is to be acquired by OTP, a company with a Hungarian background that operates not only in Central Europe but also in Russia, my first feeling was relief and satisfaction. Relief that I closed my Luminor account several years ago.

I just used it too rarely, and now I am fortunately spared moral dilemmas about how much my modest customer relationship with the bank might help Putin kill people in Ukraine.

In an ERR news story on Tuesday, the bank's communications manager Bence Gaspar commented that OTP is a very small bank in Russia (link in Estonian) — with a market share of 0.3–0.4 percent. "Our business there focuses on consumer loans for clients with lower creditworthiness, which is not such a sensitive activity. These are not business clients, and whatever we do, our first and most important goal is to comply with sanctions."

Kilvar Kessler, former long‑time head of the Financial Supervision Authority, says the bank's Russian presence should not be overstated, as there are other European banks still operating in Russia.

The easiest way to get an overview of OTP Bank's activities in Russia is probably to open the bank's Russian website at www.otpbank.ru. There, one does not get the impression that this is a microbusiness, as one might have been led to believe from the OTP spokesperson's comment.

On the front page, one learns that the bank has operated in Russia for 30 years, is one of the 50 largest banks in Russia, and has a presence in 800 Russian localities. OTP Bank issues consumer credit at 57,000 points in Russia and has two million active clients. "We help achieve goals" — one of OTP Bank's slogans for Russian clients.

"For those who are open to new things. We help clients unlock their potential and turn the boldest dreams into reality," people in Moscow, St. Petersburg, Tver and likely elsewhere can read.

According to the bank's comment, credits are not issued to business clients in Russia, but the information on the website advertises numerous other services for Russian small businesses and corporate clients.

Opening the small‑business section on the Hungarian‑Russian bank's website, one involuntarily gets the impression that Mr. Gaspar's modesty in presenting his employer would deserve a medal.

Because here it states specifically that OTP is one of the 30 largest banks in Russia (not 50) and has 2.4 million clients — almost twice the population of Estonia. Services offered by OTP include: current accounts, foreign trade, deposits, goods on installment, a recommendations program, and payroll projects. If you are a small company operating in a country at war for the fifth year, the idea of becoming a client of a nice foreign-owned bank might indeed arise.

For Russian corporate clients, OTP offers favorable conditions for currency transfers, letters of credit, and management of company cash flows.

If you are simply a private client of OTP Bank Russia, you have access to a debit card with 3,000 rubles cashback every month, a credit card (120 interest‑free days), and a cash loan ("up to 3 million rubles in three minutes").

"Here it states specifically that OTP is one of the 30 largest banks in Russia and has 2.4 million clients — almost twice the population of Estonia."

At this point, a small question arises: how many people connected to Russia's armed forces, war industry or political repressive apparatus might have a convenient OTP Russia bank card or loan in their pocket? The website does not answer this, but it could be one of the questions asked by the European Central Bank as the regulatory authority whose task is to approve OTP's purchase of Luminor in Estonia.

Of course, it would be rather strange if a bank already operating smoothly in several EU member states suddenly did not receive permission to acquire a local bank in the Baltic states. Hard to imagine such a thing happening.

The publication The Banker wrote in May about the reasons why several European banks have not yet left Russia, as the U.S. Citibank did only this February, selling its branch to the Russian investment bank Renaissance Capital. One must find a suitable buyer for the Russian bank who is not under Western sanctions, and the transaction must receive approval from the Russian central bank and, in reality, also Vladimir Putin personally.

"French bank Société Générale sold its Russian subsidiary Rosbank at the start of the war in 2022, but other major lenders — UniCredit, Raiffeisen, ING — are still trapped in the country," notes The Banker.

Meaning, even if you want to leave, you are kept in Russia, if the parent bank is simply not ready to write off its billions in assets.

OTP Bank is not discussed separately in that story, but some stats are provided. The largest European bank subsidiary operating in Russia by assets is Austria's AO Raiffeisenbank with USD 24.1 billion. Next is Hungary's OTP Bank with USD 9.79 billion, followed by Italy's Unicredit Bank Russia with USD 8.4 billion (source: The Banker database, Q1 2026).

Of course, OTP is not Sberbank. But is not some marginal player in Russia running a small bakery under an archway. OTP Bank actively participates in the increasingly militarized Russian society. For example, OTP was present at this year's St. Petersburg International Economic Forum — the flagship event of the Russian economy and an international showcase, reportedly attended by 20,000 guests and featuring Putin himself. On the website one also finds a news story about the presentation by OTP Bank's head of the artificial intelligence lab, Alexey Mezentsev, at the GTM26 conference in St. Petersburg in July.

If you work in Russia, you will also help Moscow authorities develop the country's wartime economy and artificial intelligence — how could it be otherwise.

In any case, I remain pleased that I closed my Luminor account in time.

World.title: Baltics to strengthen joint energy reserves, share emergency equipment
World.content:
The Baltic states have agreed to share and jointly procure critical reserve equipment for the electricity system to strengthen the three countries' energy security.

A joint agreement signed in Riga, Latvia, on Wednesday will allow the sharing of existing critical reserve equipment and create a cooperation framework that also includes the possibility of developing a joint regional reserve in the future.

The unified approach increases the resilience of the electricity system, improves the efficiency of resource use and reduces the impact of disruptions on consumers, a press release said.

"The Baltic states have shown that energy security can best be strengthened through cooperation. A joint crisis reserve mechanism will help ensure that, in the event of serious failures or damage, the necessary reserve equipment is available in the region and can be quickly deployed. This will make our electricity system more resilient and, if necessary, support its rapid restoration," said Minister of Energy and Environment Andres Sutt (Reform).

The declaration signed by the ministers will also allow for closer cooperation between Estonia's transmission system operator Elering and the transmission system operators of Latvia and Lithuania.

As the next step, the transmission system operators will develop a mechanism for sharing existing reserve equipment and jointly assess opportunities for creating a regional reserve to be procured together in the future.

"The changed security situation and growing threats to energy infrastructure have increased the need for solutions that enable the electricity system to be restored more quickly in the event of major disruptions," the press release said.

World.title: Iraq, Iran ink four key bilateral agreements
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq and Iran inked four agreements on Thursday focusing on transportation, rail connection, and municipal support, as well as government administration and human resource training.

The agreements were signed during meetings in Tehran between Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, with an emphasis on improving regional networks and collaborative work across borders, according to the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

Representatives from the transportation ministries of both countries signed a bilateral agreement designed to establish a structure for the international road transit of goods.

To improve rail network connectivity, the two sides signed an agreement to extend a railway connecting the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, to the Iranian city of Kermanshah. This railway will traverse the border city of Khosravi in Iran and Iraq’s Khanaqin.

Additionally, Tehran and Baghdad became sister cities after signing municipal twinning agreements and cooperative public administration training efforts.

The two countries also inked an agreement on administrative training, education, and human resource development.

The geopolitical achievement takes place as Iraq promotes an expansive economic strategy. Al-Zaidi’s visit to Tehran comes after a notable trip to the United States, where Iraq inked 48 business agreements worth over $60 billion with US corporations.

Through these diplomatic moves, Baghdad apparently aims to establish itself as a regional gateway.

World.title: Iraqi PM meets Iranian president in Tehran
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi met on Thursday with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian in Tehran, marking his first official visit to Iran since taking office.

Al-Zaidi’s reception in the Iranian capital was followed by a bilateral meeting with Pezeshkian and a joint session attended by a high-level Iraqi delegation, according to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The Iraqi prime minister proposed a diplomatic initiative focused on stabilizing the region in light of recent escalations in military operations between the United States and Iran.

Al-Zaidi said in a statement on X that he will address matters of shared interest, bilateral cooperation, regional concerns, and measures to consolidate regional security and stability.

According to al-Zaidi, Iraq and Iran have a deep connection rooted in their shared history, culture, geographic closeness, and mutual interests. This relationship highlights the importance of dialogue and collaboration in achieving sustainable development for both countries and fostering stability in the region.

The discussions reportedly centered on economic agreements, especially concerning essential shared resources like gas supplies and the declining water flows in the Tigris and Euphrates rivers.

The Iraqi delegation underscored that Iraq will stay unbiased and neutral in any foreign tensions between Tehran and Washington.

This visit takes place after al-Zaidi met with US President Donald Trump in Washington, where they inked several trade and economic deals worth billions of dollars.

Following his visit to Tehran, al-Zaidi is expected to continue his regional tour, stopping in Turkey and Saudi Arabia to discuss bilateral cooperation.

World.title: Iraq’s public debt stands at 47% of its GDP
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi prime minister’s financial advisor Mazhar Saleh told Rudaw News on Wednesday that Iraq’s total public debt is approximately 47 percent of the country’s gross domestic product (GDP).

Although Baghdad can easily handle its debt burden, the country’s dependency on revenues generated from oil exports leaves its economy exposed to various external factors.

The major issues in the Iraqi economy, according to Saleh, are its reliance on oil income, the poor performance of other productive sectors, and the growing administrative costs.

To guarantee that the Iraqi economy can survive foreign shocks, the Iraqi government is working to diversify income sources, notably in the industrial, agricultural, and service sectors, as well as reforming the tax, customs, and banking systems, according to Saleh.

In late June, the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) revealed that the country’s domestic debt rose to 95.7 trillion Iraqi dinars ($73 billion) by the end of April 2026 compared to 90.51 trillion dinars ($69.1 billion) recorded at the end of 2025, representing an increase of 5.16 trillion dinars ($3.9 billion).

In 2024, the domestic debt in Iraq stood at 83.05 trillion Iraqi dinars (approximately $63.4 billion).

According to the statistics, domestic debt increased during the first four months of 2026, while external debt dropped in comparison to prior years.

Iraq’s external debt stood at $54.101 billion in 2025, compared to $54.601 billion in 2024 and $56.207 billion in 2023, marking a total drop of $2.106 billion over two years, according to the CBI.

Senior officials in the Iraqi financial sector and representatives from Oliver Wyman, a renowned firm specializing in financial audits, emphasized the significance of developing medium-term plans customized to the nature of the debt, Iraq’s credit rating, and key global indicators.

The officials also called for drawing up budgets based on realistic evaluations of the country’s available finances and execution capabilities.

World.title: Iraqi security seizes 40 gold bars, large sums of cash in corruption case
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Supreme Judicial Council revealed on Wednesday that investigations into the case of Adnan al-Jumaili, a deputy oil minister accused of corruption, have resulted in the seizure of 13 billion Iraqi dinars (nearly $10 million), $400,000, and 40 gold bars hidden in different locations in the northern province of Salah al-Din.

The step is part of the Iraqi government’s ongoing nationwide anti-corruption campaign launched last month.

The Iraqi judiciary said in a statement that each of the gold bars weighs one kilogram. It added that security forces also seized five kilograms of gold jewelry, according to the state-run news agency (INA).

The seizures resulted from ongoing investigations into the suspect, according to the statement.

Al-Jumaili’s case is one of the most prominent corruption cases that emerged in the past few months, as the government’s campaign targets people suspected of theft and wasting public funds.

Iraqi authorities had already announced al-Jumaili’s arrest on allegations of financial and administrative corruption before the judiciary opened a broad investigation into the issue, including a review of his accounts, assets, and finances.

The Supreme Judicial Council did not provide any information on the locations where the money and gold were discovered and mentioned that search and recovery efforts are ongoing.

The Iraqi cabinet affirmed that recovering public funds is one of the priorities of its agenda, while the Federal Commission of Integrity and the judiciary are working to pursue those accused both inside and outside Iraq.

World.title: Air defenses intercept 4 drones in northern Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The international coalition’s air defense systems intercepted on Wednesday evening four drones over Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

The systems were activated when flying objects approached the US consulate and its associated logistics base, according to Al-Arabiya News.

Four explosions were reportedly heard in the skies over Erbil following the activation of the international coalition’s air defense systems.

A security source confirmed that air defenses successfully intercepted and destroyed the drones before reaching their targets, adding that the attack caused no casualties or material damage.

On Tuesday, Iraqi security sources said that air defenses intercepted three explosive-laden drones near the US consulate in Erbil with two drones targeting a camp of the Kurdistan Freedom Party (PAK), an Iranian Kurdish opposition group.

The state-run news agency (INA) reported that Erbil International Airport temporarily suspended flights but later announced their resumption.

Iraqi air defenses shot down an explosive-laden drone on Monday near Harir Air Base in Iraq, which houses US and international coalition forces. There were no reports of casualties or damages.

No group has claimed responsibility for the attacks. Neither Iraqi officials nor the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) has issued a statement identifying the attackers or the types of drones involved.

The recent escalation in Iraqi Kurdistan, which largely included drone assaults over Erbil, comes amid rising tensions between the United States and Iran, the most serious since a cease-fire deal was reached in mid-June.

World.title: US dollar rises against Iraqi dinar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar compared to the Iraqi dinar rose on Wednesday in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, and the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq, Erbil.

The US dollar exchange rate slightly rose in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,504 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,502.5 Iraqi dinars on Wednesday’s morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,510 Iraqi dinars and 1,500 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate also rose, fluctuating between 1,508.5 and 1,507.5 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation indicated a difference of over 10 percent in the exchange rates.

World.title: PM Al Zaidi proposes joint fund in call with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi held high-level telephone discussions with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Wednesday, July 22, 2026, focusing on expanding economic cooperation, trade, and industrial investment between the two nations.

According to an official statement released by the Prime Minister’s Media Office, the talks covered bilateral ties across multiple sectors, with particular emphasis on economic partnerships, trade volume expansion, direct investment, and joint migration management frameworks.

Key Discussion Pillars

Joint Iraqi-German Fund: Prime Minister Al-Zaidi proposed establishing a dedicated joint fund to finance industrial development projects in Iraq with German technical and capital backing.

Economic Reforms & Anti-Corruption: Al-Zaidi reiterated Baghdad’s commitment to eradicating administrative corruption and creating an open, transparent environment for foreign capital to diversify Iraq’s national economy.

Official Invitation to Berlin: Chancellor Merz extended a formal invitation to Prime Minister Al-Zaidi to visit Germany for an official state visit to deepen economic and political coordination.

Support for Fiscal Reform: Germany reaffirmed its support for the Iraqi government’s ongoing economic and financial reforms, expressing strong readiness from German corporations to expand investment footprints across Iraq.

The discussions highlight Baghdad’s broader diplomatic strategy of leveraging European economic integration to modernize domestic industrial infrastructure and broaden trade partnerships beyond energy exports.

World.title: Lebanon PM says Beirut working for ‘complete Israeli withdrawal’
World.content:
Zawtar al-Gharbiyah – Lebanon is working towards a “complete Israeli withdrawal” from areas it occupies, Prime Minister Nawaf Salam said on Wednesday on a visit to a village where Lebanon’s army recently deployed.

“We will continue mobilising our political and diplomatic efforts to secure a complete Israeli withdrawal from the south,” he said in Zawtar al-Gharbiya.

Israeli forces were previously present on the outskirts of the village following the war with Iran-backed Hezbollah.

Salam visited the town a day after Lebanese President Joseph Aoun met with his US counterpart Donald Trump at the White House, where he “stressed the urgent need for a full Israeli withdrawal from Lebanese territory”.

Under a US-sponsored agreement signed last month, Lebanon’s army is meant to disarm Hezbollah and the Israeli military is to withdraw from “pilot zones” where Lebanese forces will subsequently deploy.

Hezbollah has repeatedly rejected the agreement and refuses to lay down its weapons.

The military said on Tuesday that Israeli forces “opened fire” near troops deploying at Zawtar al-Gharbiya.

The Israeli military said it had only fired “warning shots into the air” after Lebanese soldiers entered an area that was “not part of the pilot area”.

Hezbollah drew Lebanon into the Middle East war by attacking Israel in support of Tehran on March 2, prompting major Israeli airstrikes and a ground invasion.

After planting a Lebanese flag in Zawtar al-Gharbiya on Wednesday, Salam said “in parallel with the army’s deployment, we will continue opening roads, removing rubble, and securing essential services, enabling our people to return safely and with dignity to their homes and villages”.

– ‘Heads held high’ –

The war caused widespread destruction, mainly in the south, though violence has declined since the signing of a framework agreement between the United States and Iran last month and the Lebanon-Israel deal.

According to the United Nations, more than 700,000 people have returned to their homes over the past few weeks.

In Zawtar al-Gharbiya, dozens of residents waited at the village’s entrance for permission to go check on their homes.

“We will enter the town with our heads held high, thanks to the presence of the Lebanese army,” Abbas Yaghi, 73, told AFP.

The military had told residents on Tuesday to avoid entering the village “until the security situation stabilises”.

The army is conducting a sweep of the town, which is geographically contiguous with its Israeli-occupied neighbour, Zawtar al-Shariqya.

Israeli troops still launch intermittent strikes in surrounding towns, the latest on Nabatieh al-Fawqa.

“We will follow the army if it gives us permission to enter,” Mostapha Ammar, a 60-year-old resident of Zawtar al-Sharqiya said, hoping that Israel would withdraw from other areas.

Wafaa Ismail, 64, also from Zawtar al-Sharqiya, was not granted permission to enter the neighbouring village as Salam visited.

She expressed frustration at seeing the prime minister enter on his own, escorted by the army, saying: “He should have brought the people in with him so he could claim victory.”

World.title: ‘Antisocial elements taking advantage’: Sonam Wangchuk urges protesters to remain peaceful, says 'only peace is my way'
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Climate activist

on Thursday appealed to supporters to maintain peace during the ongoing protests over the alleged NEET paper leak, saying some "antisocial elements" were trying to provoke violence and urging demonstrators to respond only with non-violence.

In a post on X marking the 26th day of his hunger strike, Wangchuk said he was distressed to learn that attempts were being made to derail the peaceful nature of the protests outside Delhi's Jantar Mantar.

"DAY 26. PEACE & ONLY PEACE IS MY WAYâ¦ While at Jantar Mantar the protests remain peaceful Iâm pained to learn that elsewhere some antisocial elements are taking advantage of the peaceful protests to provoke violence," Wangchuk wrote.

"No matter what the other side does our response must only be flowers. Please keep this tradition at all costs," he added.

Continues fast from hospital

Wangchuk's latest appeal came a day after he was shifted from Delhi's Safdarjung Hospital to Medanta Hospital in Gurugram, where he continues his indefinite hunger strike.

According to a statement issued by Medanta Hospital, Wangchuk remains "stable and alert", with his vital signs within accepted parameters.





The hospital said he is being treated by a multidisciplinary team of doctors and that all medical care is being provided with his informed consent.

Earlier on Wednesday, Wangchuk had said he had lost 11 kilograms during his 25-day fast but remained determined to continue unless the government assured that no legal action, including FIRs, would be taken against protesting students.

"I request the government not to use force against children.

I demand an assurance for no accusations or FIRs through which they can be threatened with police or jails," he had said.

The activist had also praised students who participated in the Cockroach Janata Party's 'Chalo Sansad' march on July 20, saying they remained peaceful despite police action.

"Even upon being instigated and some elements being brought in for stone pelting, you remained patient. My heart melted.

Because they were attacked brutally, I decided to continue fasting," Wangchuk had said.

He added that several ministers and opposition leaders, along with a letter signed by 65 MPs, had urged him to end his hunger strike, but reiterated that he would do so only after receiving assurances that protesters would not face legal action.

CJP calls for nationwide protests

Meanwhile, the Cockroach Janata Party has called for coordinated peaceful protests across the country on Friday, urging student unions and other organisations to join demonstrations demanding Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation over the alleged paper leak.

The protest call comes as the Centre continues to seek a discussion with the Opposition on the issue without preconditions, while CJP leaders have maintained that the education minister's resignation remains "non-negotiable".

World.title: Centre monitoring 2,485 Himalayan glacial lakes; 56 classified as 'very high risk'
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Centre on Thursday said it is monitoring 2,485 glacial lakes spread across the Himalayan river basins using remote sensing techniques. It also informed Parliament that 56 glacial lakes have been classified as 'very high risk' following a scientific assessment conducted in 2025 due to their potential to trigger Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs).

In a written reply in the Lok Sabha, jal shakti state minister Raj Bhushan Choudhary said the Central Water Commission (CWC) monitors glacial lakes larger than 10 hectares across four states and two Union Territories from June to October every year using remote sensing.

The minister said the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), in collaboration with national scientific agencies, carried out a scientific assessment of 189 high-risk glacial lakes across the Indian Himalayan Region in 2025.

"Based on the assessment, 56 glacial lakes were classified as very high risk considering their potential to trigger Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs) and the exposure of downstream habitations and infrastructure," Choudhary said.

He said the government has started establishing Glacial Lake Outburst Flood (GLOF) Early Warning Systems (EWS) at selected high-risk glacial lakes based on hazard assessments and continuous monitoring.





However, the minister clarified that no end-to-end GLOF Early Warning System has been commissioned so far under the National GLOF Risk Mitigation Programme (NGRMP).

Choudhary said the NDMA is implementing the NGRMP, which was approved in 2024 for Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh at a cost of Rs 150 crore.

"The programme envisages Hazard and Risk Assessment, Monitoring and Early Warning Systems, site-specific structural and non-structural mitigation of measures, and community awareness and capacity building," he said.

The minister added that Rs 52.50 crore has been allocated under the Monitoring and Early Warning System component of the programme.

He also said the NDMA, along with the Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation (SDC) and the Sikkim State Disaster Management Authority (SSDMA), carried out multi-agency expeditions to the high-risk South Lhonak and Shako Cho glacial lakes in Sikkim during 2023 and 2024. The expeditions were aimed at supporting scientific studies and developing monitoring systems, early warning mechanisms and mitigation measures.

(with inputs from PTI)

World.title: India slams Pakistan's 'state-sponsored' misinformation at Asean, says Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India on Thursday categorically rejected

's comments at the Asean Regional Forum in Manila, calling them "baseless and unwarranted".

New Delhi slammed Islamabad of using the multilateral platform to peddle "state-sponsored disinformation" and divert attention from its record of sponsoring cross-border terrorism.

"It is no surprise that a multilateral forum has once again been cynically exploited by Pakistan to amplify falsehoods, peddle state-sponsored disinformation, and divert attention from its own well-documented record of sponsoring cross-border terrorism," MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said.

"The Union Territories of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh have been, are and will always remain integral and inalienable parts of India.

Pakistan has no locus standi to comment on the same," MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said in response to media queries.

Jaiswal also said India's position on the

remained consistent, stating that the treaty stands in abeyance in response to Pakistan's continued sponsorship of cross-border terrorism, including the Pahalgam attack. "IWT will continue to be held in abeyance until Pakistan credibly and irrevocably abjures its support for cross-border terrorism," he said.





Jaiswal also condemned Pakistan's practice of propagating "officially sponsored disinformation, often dressed in religious terminology such as the use of terms like 'Fitna al-Hindustan'."

"This is a futile attempt by the Pakistani establishment to deflect attention from its own internal crises and its well-proven role as a safe haven for global terrorist networks," he said.

He added that Pakistan would serve itself better by "dismantling the infrastructure of terrorism on its soil and putting its own house in order" instead of pointing fingers at its neighbours.

External affairs minister S Jaishankar attended the foreign minister-level meetings under the Asean framework, including the Asean-India, East Asia Summit and Asean Regional Forum meetings in Manila over the last two days.

Pakistanâs deputy prime minister and foreign minister Mohammad Ishaq Dar led Pakistan's delegation at the forum. He raised the Jammu and Kashmir dispute, calling for its resolution in accordance with

resolutions, and expressed concern over India's decision to hold the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance.

World.title: Watch: Gujarat rains trigger waist-deep flooding, vehicles go under
World.content:
Gujarat rains wreck havoc

Floodwaters submerge vehicles, roads in Vapi

Relief operations underway, CM reviews situation

Red alert continues, rescue teams on standby

NEW DELHI: Around 1,200 people have been rescued and hundreds more relocated as heavy rains battered south Gujarat, with Umbergaon taluka in Valsad district receiving over 1,100 mm of rainfall in just 16 hours, officials said on Thursday.One rain-related death was reported in Tapi district. The Indian Air Force and Coast Guard have been put on alert for rescue efforts, while NDRF and SDRF teams are deployed across the affected areas.Valsad district was the worst hit, with many talukas receiving over 600 mm of rain during the same period. A red alert for heavy to extremely heavy rainfall was in effect for Valsad, Navsari, Surat and Tapi districts.Large parts of Vapi in Valsad district were inundated, with floodwaters submerging parked vehicles and disrupting normal life. Videos from the area showed waist-deep water in residential colonies and commercial areas, with people wading through the deluge.The Kaveri river in Navsari rose sharply, stranding 200 people across 11 villages. They were rescued and relocated to safety. In Surat, 1,500 residents were moved from low-lying areas and waterlogged localities.Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel visited the State Emergency Operation Centre and reviewed the situation, speaking to district collectors and instructing them to move people from vulnerable areas to safer places.He also spoke to Union Home Minister Amit Shah, who assured all necessary assistance.Over 300 roads were temporarily closed, more than 200 state-run bus trips were affected, and power outages were reported in many areas.The IMD has issued a red alert for Valsad, Navsari, Dangs, Surat and Tapi for Thursday and Friday. NDRF and SDRF teams are deployed across the affected districts, with additional teams on standby in Amreli, Junagadh and Bhavnagar.Several trains to Mumbai were cancelled or short-terminated due to rising water levels along rail routes in south Gujarat.The state has received around 36 per cent of its annual average rainfall so far, with south Gujarat recording over 62 per cent of its seasonal average.

World.title: ‘Must be handled with empathy’: BJP veteran Murli Manohar Joshi breaks ranks, backs NEET protesters
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Veteran

leader and former Union minister Murli Manohar Joshi on Thursday extended support to students protesting over the alleged NEET paper leak, saying their concerns about the examination system are "genuine" and should be addressed with empathy rather than force.

In a rare intervention from a senior BJP figure, Joshi also criticised the police action against protesting students in Delhi earlier this week, describing it as "merciless" and warning that such use of force could alienate large sections of society from the government's vision of a Viksit Bharat.

"It is painful to see young students from different parts of the country assembled for days on the streets of New Delhi.

Their anxieties and concerns regarding the examination system are genuine and must be handled with empathy and a desire to find a lasting solution," Joshi said in a post on X.

"It is very painful to see that even young girls were brutally mishandled," he added.

Calling for a more humane approach, Joshi said, "I fervently hope that this is not treated merely as a law-and-order issue to be tackled through the use of force."





He further warned that such action "shall alienate large sections of Indian society from the national goal of Viksit Bharat."

BJP, opposition continue war of words

Joshi's remarks came amid an intensifying political confrontation over the alleged NEET paper leak and the ongoing Monsoon Session of Parliament.

The BJP accused the

of avoiding a discussion on the issue in Parliament despite the government expressing readiness for a debate. BJP president Nitin Nabin said the opposition was "running away" from a discussion because its "double standards" would be exposed.

"The NDA government is fully prepared to hold discussions at every level on the future of students and youngsters," Nabin said, while challenging the opposition to participate in a debate on NEET and other issues concerning students.

Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman also asserted that the Centre had already taken action against those accused in the alleged paper leak and remained committed to ensuring justice for students.

She accused the Congress of pursuing "disruptive politics" instead of participating in a parliamentary discussion.

Commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal appealed to the opposition not to politicise the issue, saying the government would take the "strictest possible action" against those found guilty in paper leak cases.

Earlier in the day, Prime Minister Modi issued his first public response to the ongoing agitation, announcing that the government would set up fast-track courts to ensure swift punishment for those involved in paper leak cases.

"Nothing is more important than the welfare and future of our youth! We have decided to set up fast-track courts to ensure swift and stringent punishment for those involved in paper leaks. Have directed the concerned authorities and officials to take all necessary steps. Those who try to harm the future of our youth will not be spared," PM Modi wrote on X.

Opposition backs students, Parliament remains deadlocked

Meanwhile, opposition parties have continued to press for the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan and have linked the issue to the alleged assault on student protesters.

Leader of opposition

said INDIA bloc leaders were heading to Gandhi Smriti to express solidarity with students affected by the alleged paper leak and those injured during police action.

"India's students are not alone. The entire Opposition stands with them and their demands," Gandhi wrote on X.

The Opposition has made Pradhan's resignation and a discussion under Rule 267 in the Rajya Sabha key demands before agreeing to a debate, while the government has maintained that it is willing to discuss the issue without preconditions.

The deadlock has repeatedly disrupted proceedings in both Houses of Parliament.

World.title: Tanul Thakur On The Corporate Cruelty Driving The H-1B Visa Economy
World.content:
Tanul Thakurâs 'Wild Wild East' Uncovers the Human Cost of the American Dream

How did this book come about?
