Excerpts:I was an H1B worker in the US from 2011 to 2013. And during my time there as an electrical engineer, I got more than a whiff that there was some scam going on in the H1B visa programme... And this idea really stayed with me, this idea of primarily Indians exploiting Indians in the US. Cut to a few years later, I returned to India to pursue my passion of being a full-time writer and a journalist. And this idea then really thundered back to me in all its different manifestations... I think subconsciously I wanted to write a book that would explore morality, enslavement, identity of modern day Indian elites... The actual story though snowballed into a much bigger and much more significant something...This started off as a very literary project... I wanted to write a "non-fiction novel"... Then these questions started to ping my conscience: why do we not know about this scam? Who benefits from it, apart from the obvious corporate American entities? And then I figured out that this is not just about a few individuals or a few firms.It's essentially like an entire society colluding to both perpetrate and also hide the scam. .. You have these immigration forums, anonymous people with fake monikers talking about how they scam the system. You have visa mills and a bunch of parties coming together to perpetrate something really, really horrific. So the book changed during the process. I changed during the process.Sometimes it felt like a science fiction story... I was constantly taken aback, not just by the brazenness of the scam, but also about how this was hiding in plain sight... On the one hand, you are seeing all these crazy things that are happening, and on the other, there's absolute silence about it in the outer world... There were many heartbreaking things that I found... I was very surprised by the kinds of entities that I used to consider heroes. Say the American media, academia, some politicians â most of them turned out to be villains... Just understanding how it is humanly possible for human beings, in this case three protagonists, to absorb so much of pain, to absorb so much of anguish... on a day to day basis and yet have the courage to solder on. These are the things that really stayed with me.Think of it as a chain of blocks. So essentially you have a client, which is to say like a Fortune 500 firm or a corporate America entity which wants â I mean back in 2010 or something â let's say wanted a Java specialist. So it would ask a big outsourcing giant, which is called a prime vendor, do you have a Java specialist for this kind of a contractual position? If they do, they supply that. If they don't, that's when the desi consultancy model comes in, it would ask a smaller outsourcing or a staffing company. And that's how the chain gets built. You have a client, you have a prime vendor, then you have one or two companies in between. Then you have an H1B employer who is sponsoring the visa for an H1B worker. Now, a decade ago, if a client was paying around $120 per hour for a Java specialist or for an IT specialist with six years of experience, different parties would take a cut and the H1B worker would get somewhere around $25 an hour.And amidst that, there is insane amounts of wage theft. You have your purchase orders being edited, you have no idea how much your employer is getting... There is this thing called benching, wherein you're supposed to pay the H1B worker when he or she doesn't have a project. But that never happens. In fact, you don't just not get paid when you're benched. You have to pay your employers taxes during that period. There is this immense amount of psychological cruelty that's meted by Indian owners of body shops or desi consultancies to Indian H1B workers. This dehumanization exists at varying levels. There's this literal and metaphorical transformation of identity. You are often handed a resume which has seven or eight years of fake experience. Then you get a job through a proxy interview. Even at the client side, if you don't know anything, you have this process of like on job support where you can outsource your job to some other techie in India. So very rampant exploitation almost becomes the language of this industry.First of all, they were themselves so frustrated... Nobody thought their stories were stories. Nobody thought of them as people. So the very fact that I told them that I'm interested in this, that I completely understand your pain, anguish, maybe it had kind of helped that I had done some bit of my own research... I think it was just my persistence. And I think in that persistence, they had seen some bit of my wonder, my innocence, my intellectual curiosity, but also my rage, my very incipient rage. .. They all got eased into the process because I think they had understood that he's not a regular journalist, which is to say that he genuinely cares for us as people... I think being genuinely open, innocent and curious about their lives as people and applying largely the same matrices, but icing it with a copious amount of rage about the systemic abuse itself, I think kind of endeared them to talk to me.What occurred to me around 2020 is that this is a book about the tyranny of capitalism. It's about the tyranny or the dictates of American neoliberalism. And I am essentially just using H1B as a metaphor or as a lens to explore that... One can very easily and glibly dismiss a lot of American workers as racist or bigoted or xenophobic. Some of them could be, sure. But many of them are actually not just these things. They are simply very saddened about their economic and psychological and personal devastation. But that's also one of the biggest corporate cruelties, right? Or it's one of the biggest corporate tricks... A lot of Americans are just blaming Indians, which is insane to me because given the way this H1B system has been abused... they should not be each other's adversaries. They should understand that they are both being pitted against each other... This is something that I want a lot of people to understand, that this is essentially not about immigrants versus citizens, it's about immigrants and citizens versus exploitative corporations and the exploitative American capitalist structure itself.

World.title: Evening news wrap:  Parliament deadlock over NEET continues, Gulf invests to find new oil routes & more
World.content:
Government reaches out to opposition for NEET debate without preconditions; opposition insists on Pradhan's resignation.

Gulf nations spend billions on new oil pipelines to bypass Strait of Hormuz as Iran blockade continues.

CJP and government locked in standoff over venue for talks as protest demanding Pradhan's resignation continues.

India's first hydrogen-powered train clocks 900 km in five days of commercial operations on Jind-Sonipat route.

Iran claims its strikes destroyed Patriot systems and THAAD radar at US bases in Jordan and Kuwait; US yet to confirm.

Here are the top 5 stories of the day

Government reaches out to opposition for NEET debate, urges talks without preconditions

The government has reached out to opposition parties to break the Parliament deadlock over the NEET paper leak, offering a discussion without preconditions but opposing the demand for education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation.

Union home minister Amit Shah met Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla after repeated adjournments, while opposition leaders including Rahul Gandhi and Akhilesh Yadav also held talks with the Speaker.

Gulf nations spend billions on finding new oil routes to bypass Strait of Hormuz

Gulf nations are accelerating pipeline projects worth billions of dollars to create alternative export routes bypassing the Strait of Hormuz, with at least seven major projects under construction, planned or under discussion.

Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline and UAE's Fujairah terminal are operating near full capacity, while Abu Dhabi is speeding up a $3 billion pipeline to increase Fujairah's capacity by 1.2 million barrels a day.

Iraq is reviving plans for pipelines through Turkey and Jordan, but analysts warn alternative routes remain vulnerable to Houthi attacks.

CJP protest continues as government, activists locked in standoff over venue for talks

The Cockroach Janata Party and the government remained locked in a standoff over the venue for talks, with the CJP insisting on Jantar Mantar while the government proposed an alternative location.





The protest demanding the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET paper leak has entered its second month. Police action against protesters and the detention of CJP leaders have further escalated tensions.

Iran claims strikes destroyed Patriot systems, THAAD radar at US bases

Iran's IRGC claimed it destroyed Patriot air defence systems, a THAAD missile defence radar and an MQ-9 Reaper drone depot in retaliatory strikes on US bases in Jordan and Kuwait, though the claims could not be independently verified and the US military has not confirmed any damage.

India's first hydrogen-powered train clocks 900 km in five days

India's first hydrogen fuel cell-powered passenger train has covered around 900 kilometres during the first five days of commercial operations on the Jind-Sonipat route in Haryana, with passenger fares ranging between Rs 10 and Rs 25.

World.title: Trump says Saudi nuclear deal hinges on kingdom joining Abraham Accords with Israel
World.content:
US President Donald Trump on Thursday said the proposed US-Saudi civil nuclear agreement would only be approved if Saudi Arabia normalises diplomatic relations with Israel by joining the Abraham Accords, adding that the deal would not permit uranium enrichment or any military nuclear programme.

Trump's remarks come a day after the United States and Saudi Arabia signed a civil nuclear cooperation framework, known as a 123 Agreement, that will now require approval from the US Congress.

In a post on social media, Trump said, "The Civil Nuclear Deal (There will be no enrichment of material!) being made between the United States Department of Energy and Saudi Arabia, which pertains only to non-military use such as the ones that Iran and UAE (and others) already have, will be approved, but is totally subject to Saudi Arabia joining the very respected and successful Abraham Accords.

The United States is not opposed to Civil (Non-Enriched) Nuclear Facilities.

"

Trump's statement marks a shift from the framework announced on Wednesday, under which the two countries agreed to cooperate on Saudi Arabia's civilian nuclear programme. The agreement, signed by US Energy Secretary Chris Wright and Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman, lays the groundwork for nuclear cooperation while requiring congressional review before it can take effect.





The Trump administration has said the agreement adheres to the highest standards of nuclear safety and non-proliferation. Secretary of State Marco Rubio also defended the deal, saying the United States would not enter into any arrangement that increased the risk of nuclear weapons proliferation.

Poll Vote & Share your view Should Saudi Arabia be required to normalize relations with Israel before receiving nuclear cooperation from the US? Yes, it's a necessary step. No, they should be treated independently. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

The agreement has nevertheless drawn scrutiny from some US lawmakers, who have raised concerns that allowing Saudi Arabia to pursue uranium enrichment for civilian purposes could eventually create pathways for nuclear weapons development.

Trump's latest remarks also appear to narrow the scope of the proposed agreement by insisting there would be "no enrichment of material" and linking final approval to Saudi Arabia's recognition of Israel through the Abraham Accords, the US-brokered normalisation agreements signed by Israel with several Arab states during Trump's first term.

The announcement comes as the United States and Israel continue military operations against Iran, with Washington maintaining that Tehran's uranium enrichment programme could enable it to develop nuclear weapons, a charge Iran denies, insisting its nuclear activities are solely for peaceful purposes.

World.title: At least 1,200 rescued as torrential rain pounds south Gujarat; PM Modi, Amit Shah review situation
World.content:
Around 1,200 people have been rescued and hundreds more shifted to safer locations as torrential rain continued to batter south Gujarat, prompting Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel to review the flood situation, even as the Centre assured full support for rescue and relief operations.

One rain-related death was reported from Tapi district, while the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), State Disaster Response Force (SDRF), the Indian Air Force (IAF) and the Coast Guard were placed on alert as authorities intensified rescue and relief efforts.

Prime Minister Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah spoke with Mr. Patel on Thursday (July 23, 2026). to review the situation arising out of the heavy rainfall in Gujarat and promised full support from the Central Government for rescue, relief and safety measures.

Downpour affects essential services

According to SEOC data, Valsad was the worst-hit district, with Umbergaon taluka recording more than 1,100 mm of rainfall in just 16 hours, between 6 a.m. on Wednesday and 10 a.m. on Thursday. Several other talukas in the district received more than 600 mm of rainfall during the same period.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a red alert for Valsad, Navsari, Dang, Surat and Tapi districts for Thursday and Friday, warning of heavy to extremely heavy rainfall.

The heavy rainfall disrupted transport and essential services across south Gujarat. More than 300 roads were temporarily closed, over 200 Gujarat State Road Transport Corporation bus services were affected, and power outages were reported from several locations.

In Surat, fire department personnel used boats to rescue residents trapped in flooded localities, shifting at least 40 people from the Pandesara area to safety. Heavy rainfall was also reported from Umarpada, Ambika, Palsana and Mahuva talukas. Surat Collector Tejas Parmar said Umarpada, Bardoli, Mahuva and Kamrej had recorded particularly heavy rainfall.

Rain also lashed Ahmedabad city on Thursday (July 23, 2026), flooding several residential societies and forcing the closure of multiple underpasses, disrupting traffic.

Rail services were affected as several Mumbai-bound trains were cancelled or short-terminated because of rising water levels along railway tracks in south Gujarat. Western Railway set up help desks for passengers.

In Narmada district, heavy rains cut off several villages in Dediapada and Sagbara talukas after road connectivity was disrupted.

The IMD has also issued a red alert for Panchmahal, Dahod and Mahisagar districts in central Gujarat, while 11 districts are under an orange alert and 10 districts under a yellow alert.

According to SEOC data, south Gujarat has already received more than 62% of its average seasonal rainfall, while the State has received about 36% of its annual average rainfall so far this monsoon season.

Relief work in full swing

Earlier in the day, Mr. Patel visited the State Emergency Operation Centre (SEOC) in Gandhinagar to assess the situation and also spoke to Mr. Shah, who assured the State government of all necessary assistance for rescue and relief operations.

Relief Commissioner Gaurang Makwana said NDRF and SDRF teams have been deployed across the affected districts, with additional personnel being mobilised as rainfall intensity increased.

“The Air Force and Coast Guard are also on alert and people will be airlifted if necessary once weather conditions improve,” Mr. Makwana told reporters.

He said around 1,200 people have been rescued so far. In Surat, nearly 1,500 residents have been shifted to safer locations, while in Navsari, around 200 people stranded in 11 villages due to the swelling Kaveri river have been rescued and relocated.

Senior officials, including district Collectors and mamlatdars, have been stationed in the affected areas to oversee relief operations.

Surat currently has two NDRF and five SDRF teams deployed, while Valsad has two NDRF and four SDRF teams. Additional NDRF teams are being mobilised for Navsari, while SDRF and NDRF teams have also been kept on standby in Amreli, Junagadh and Bhavnagar.

According to an official release, Mr. Patel also spoke to Minister Naresh Patel and the Valsad Collector to review rescue and relief measures and assured that additional NDRF teams would be deployed if required. He directed the Collectors of Surat and Navsari to evacuate residents from low-lying and waterlogged areas.

World.title: Jantar Mantar protest LIVE: 17 Delhi metro stations to remain shut on July 24 as CJP calls for nationwide protests
World.content:
Union Minister Jitendra Singh on Thursday (July 23, 2026) said that the Centre is ready for talks with the Cockroach Janta Party amid the latter’s protest in Delhi’s Jantar Mantar over paper leaks and the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. However, CJP has declined the invitation and said that the talks need to happen at Jantar Mantar or at another neutral venue.

Also read: The cockroach dilemma facing India’s political parties

Earlier today, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, in a social media post, said that his government will set up fast-track courts for action against those involved in paper leaks. “Nothing is more important than the welfare and future of our youth! We have decided to set up fast-track courts to ensure swift and stringent punishment for those involved in paper leaks. Have directed the concerned authorities and officials to take all necessary steps in this regard. This continues our series of steps for safeguarding the interests of students. Those who try to harm the future of our youth will not be spared,” Mr. Modi said.

Also Read: 16 metro stations, including Rajiv Chowk, Patel Chowk, Delhi Gate and Central Secretariat, closed, says DMRC

The CJP reacted to the announcement and said that while fast-track courts will address what happens after the paper leak, why there are paper leaks is a larger issue that the government must address.

Medanta Hospital on Thursday said activist Sonam Wangchuk, who is admitted to the hospital, is being treated by a multi-disciplinary team of doctors. In a health bulletin update, the hospital said Mr. Wangchuk’s condition remains unchanged and he continues to remain stable and alert, with his vital signs within accepted parameters.

World.title: Women’s reservation should be implemented without delimitation: Justice Hariparanthaman
World.content:
The freeze on delimitation of parliamentary constituencies should continue, and women’s reservation should be implemented immediately after being delinked from delimitation and the Census, former Madras High Court judge D. Hariparanthaman (retd.) said on Thursday (July 23, 2026).

Releasing the book, The Delimitation Debate: The Union and its Units, published by The Hindu Group at its headquarters in Chennai, the former judge cautioned that an increase in the number of Lok Sabha seats would hamper meaningful deliberations in the House.

“The problem of raising the numbers is that deliberations cannot take place,” he said. Besides, if the increase is based on population, southern States will stand to lose adequate representation in the Lok Sabha. This would amount to penalising the southern States for having implemented the national population policy well. “Taking into consideration other democracies, 543 itself is a good number,” he said.

Justice Hariparanthaman also batted for equitable representation of all States in the Rajya Sabha, much like the U.S. Senate model.

K. Ashok Vardhan Shetty, retired IAS officer and member of the High Level Committee on Centre-State Relations constituted by the Tamil Nadu government, said Article 329(a) places the Delimitation Commission’s proposals inside a constitutional “black box”, insulating it from executive, parliamentary, and judicial scrutiny.

The Commission comprises a retired Supreme Court judge as chairperson, the Chief Election Commissioner or a nominee, and the State Election Commissioner of the State concerned. “This is dangerous and has to be corrected. In Japan and Germany, the Delimitation Commission advises but the legislatures pass the delimitation legislations,” he said.

Mr. Shetty suggested the introduction of the “dialogue model” implemented in Canada where the delimitation commission’s proposals are deliberated by a parliamentary sub-committee and the remarks are sent back to the commission for clarification. To improve representation in both Houses, the Rajya Sabha, or the House of States, may be recast on the lines of the U.S. Senate while for the Lok Sabha, a digressive proportionality system, as in practice in Brazil, may be implemented to reduce the gap between the more populous States and the smaller ones. Delimitation should be frozen until all States fell within a narrow band of the National Total Fertility Rate, he said.

N. Ram, Director, The Hindu Group Publishing Pvt. Ltd., suggested that the ideas discussed in the book may be further distilled to make them accessible for all, which then may be translated to other languages.

Also present were Nirmala Lakshman, Publisher, The Hindu Group, and Suresh Nambath, Editor, The Hindu.

R. Srinivasan, head, Magazines and Special Publications, THG Publishing, said the title was the Group’s 219th publication since the formation of a Special Publications vertical in 2017.

The book is a collection of 17 essays — preceded by an introduction — on delimitation, federalism, representation, and Census, and highlights how the lack of access to key data makes delimitation studies difficult in India. Among the authors are Ashok Lavasa, former Election Commissioner; S.Y. Quraishi, former Chief Election Commissioner; G.N. Devy, linguist, cultural activist, and literary critic; Zoya Hasan, Professor Emerita, Jawaharlal Nehru University; and Radha Kumar, former Director-General, Delhi Policy Group.

World.title: Delhi Police’s preventive detention power under NSA extended till October 18
World.content:
The Lieutenant Governor has extended the Delhi Police's power of preventive detention under the stringent National Security Act (NSA) till October 18, according to an official notification.

In a statement, the Delhi Police said this was a "routine extension" of the power and it had been "interpreted out of context" in certain media reports that were claiming that the power had been granted to quell the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led protest.

Jantar Mantar protest LIVE

The CJP began its protest at Jantar Mantar on June 20 against the NEET paper leak and to demand the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the issue.

On Monday, tens of thousands tried to march to Parliament as part of the CJP-led "Chalo Sansad" protest. The march witnessed violence, with scores of protesters and police personnel injured.

According to the notification issued on July 15 by the Delhi government's Home Department, the city police commissioner has been granted the power of detention under Sub Section (2) of Section 3 of the NSA. The power will be valid up to October 18, it said.

The NSA empowers the Centre and States to detain individuals to prevent them from acting in a manner "prejudicial to the defence of India". The detention period under the NSA ranges from three to 12 months, though it can be revoked earlier. It can be revoked by the local administration and has to be ratified by a board headed by a former High Court judge.

Because it is preventive detention and not arrest, there is no legal obligation to present the detainee before a court of law.

In its statement, the Delhi Police said, "... it is clarified that the said order is a routine extension/renewal of powers under the NSA, which is issued every three months."

It further said the present renewal was granted on July 7 for the period from July 19 to October 18, well before the commencement of the CJP protests.

"It is further clarified that no specific request was made in the present context. The renewal is a routine administrative exercise and has been interpreted out of context by certain media reports," the statement said.

A Delhi government officer said the power of detention under the NSA was extended routinely after every quarter. This power had been delegated since the 1980s, he said.

World.title: Man arrested for attempted theft at Canara Bank branch
World.content:
The Bantwal Rural police, on Wednesday, arrested a 33-year-old man in connection with an attempted theft at Canara Bank’s branch in Farangipet on June 13.

The police said the accused, identified as Mohammed Shakir, of Maripalla in Bantwal, broke part of the building’s roof to enter the bank in the early hours of June 13. Bank employees noticed the attempted theft when the branch was opened. The police said nothing had been stolen from the branch.

The police said an inquiry was under way to find out whether any other persons were involved in the incident. Shakir was booked under Sections 331(3) (house trespass), 331(4), 305(a) (theft in a dwelling house) and 62 (attempting to commit offences punishable with life imprisonment or other imprisonment) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

World.title: Literary critic M. Leelavathy chosen for Prof. M.K. Sanoo award
World.content:
Literary critic M. Leelavathy has been chosen for the award instituted by the Prof. M.K. Sanoo Samskarika Kendram.

The award carries ₹1 lakh, a citation, and a sculpture crafted by Unni Kanayi. Author Vinil Paul was chosen for the young achievers’ award instituted by the organisation, said a release.

The awards will be handed over on August 2, 2026, here by Opposition leader Pinarayi Vijayan. There will also be a discussion in which senior journalist R. Rajagopal will participate.

World.title: Kerala University Syndicate scraps ₹2-crore sculpture park project
World.content:
The Kerala University Syndicate on Thursday (July 23, 2026) revoked its earlier decision to establish a ₹2-crore sculpture park at the Karyavattom campus.

The sculpture park, proposed in the university’s 2025-26 budget by the previous Left-dominant Syndicate, was expected to feature statues of eminent personalities including Karl Marx, Charles Darwin, Socrates, and Rabindranath Tagore. The park was planned on both sides of the main entrance to the campus.

The Syndicate, chaired by Vice-Chancellor in-charge Mohanan Kunnummal, decided to utilise the earmarked funds for creating a garden on the campus and enhancing student amenities.

The Syndicate also resolved to submit project proposals to secure financial assistance under the Union government’s Khelo India scheme for upgrading sports infrastructure on the university campus.

Moreover, the meeting constituted a Syndicate sub-committee to prepare a comprehensive policy framework for autonomous colleges affiliated with Kerala University. The committee will hold consultations with the managements of autonomous colleges and examine the relevant University Grants Commission (UGC) regulations, government guidelines and university statutes before submitting its report.

Regarding the land encroachment case involving the AKG Centre, the Syndicate decided to file a counter affidavit before the Kerala High Court and to complete the survey and demarcation of the university’s land within a stipulated time-frame.

World.title: Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman invited to BRICS summit in Delhi
World.content:
Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has been invited to participate in the BRICS summit that will be held here on September 12 and 13, according to Shama Obaid, Bangladeshi Minister of State for Foreign Affairs.

Mr. Rahman has received an invitation from the Indian government to be a guest at the BRICS summit, Ms. Obaid told journalists in Dhaka on Thursday (July 23, 2026).

This is the first BRICS summit to be held after Mr. Rahman came to power in February, following a landslide victory for his Bangladesh Nationalist Party in the general election held after nearly 15 months of an interim government in Dhaka. Mr. Rahman’s first two foreign trips after taking charge were to Malaysia and China last month, when he met Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim and Chinese President Xi Jinping.

Also Read | Bangladesh says it foiled multiple attempts by India to force people into the country

Several important discussions are pending between India and Bangladesh, due to the lack of any high-level contacts between the two countries since the fall of the Sheikh Hasina government in August 2024. One of these issues awaiting resolution is the Ganga water treaty of 1996, which needs to be renewed as its validity ends on December 31, 2026. The two sides need to meet and finalise the draft of the renewal before that date.

World.title: ‘Husband and I are proud…’: Why actor Pallavi Purohit says motherhood should never be forced
World.content:
Choosing to be child-free is becoming an increasingly visible life choice, yet it continues to invite strong opinions and social scrutiny, particularly for women. Television actor Pallavi Purohit, who has portrayed mothers in several popular shows, recently spoke about why she has chosen a different path in her personal life.

DISCLAIMER: This article is based on information from the public domain and/or the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine.

Calling it a “thoughtful and conscious decision,” the actor said that motherhood is among the most precious phases for a woman, only if a woman is ready for it — mentally, physically, and emotionally. Further stressing that one must not have children following societal pressure, the actor spoke about adoption, too.

Reflecting on the reactions she has received, she added that her family supports her choices without judgements. “My husband and I are both proud of our decision. After all, it’s our life, and we have every right to decide what we want from it,” she continued. Her comments, made during an interview with The Times of India, raise broader questions about societal expectations, emotional wellbeing and the many ways people experience nurturing and fulfilment. We asked an expert.

Choosing parenthood with intention

Dr Sakshi Mandhyan, psychologist and founder of Mandhyan Care, tells indianexpress.com, “I do not think there is a perfect moment to become a parent. What matters much more is whether the decision comes from personal readiness or from pressure or expectation. Parenthood is not only about wanting a child. It is about being emotionally available, adapting to changing priorities, and accepting that another person’s needs will become part of your everyday life.”

Dr Mandhyan has met people who were certain they wanted children and others who were equally certain they did not. “Neither choice is psychologically healthier than the other. What usually creates distress is living someone else’s decision instead of your own. I encourage people to ask themselves, before becoming a parent, whether they genuinely desire the role or whether they are trying to meet social expectations.”

Children also thrive when they are welcomed into an emotionally welcoming environment. “The more voluntary the decision, the greater the possibility of raising them with commitment and emotional availability instead of obligation or resentment,” shares Dr Mandhyan.



Protecting your well-being from social pressure

Dr Mandhyan finds that people become emotionally exhausted not because they answer the question once, but because they feel expected to defend the same decision repeatedly. After a while, the conversation becomes no longer about curiosity and starts feeling like an assessment of whether their life choices are acceptable.

She adds that one important psychological skill is recognising that not every question deserves a detailed explanation. A calm and respectful response is often enough. Healthy boundaries do not have to sound harsh. They simply communicate that a thoughtful decision has been made and does not require ongoing discussion.

“I also believe people become emotionally freer when they stop measuring the value of their decisions through the approval of others. There will always be different opinions around marriage and parenthood. The goal is not to convince everyone. Rather, it is to remain at peace with a decision that has been made after honest reflection and is consistent with one’s own values and life circumstances,” notes Dr Mandhyan.

Respond calmly and respectfully instead of feeling pressured to defend your choice.

Set healthy boundaries by communicating that your decision has been made thoughtfully.

Avoid measuring the value of your life choices through other people’s approval.

Focus on staying at peace with a decision that reflects your own values and life circumstances.

World.title: Indian-American doctor Amish Shah wins Arizona Democratic primary, to face Trump-backed rival
World.content:
Indian-American doctor Amish Shah won the Democratic primary in a hotly contested congressional district in Arizona, United States, defeating the establishment-backed candidate.

Shah, an emergency medicine doctor, is a moderate Democrat who shot to fame with his unique style of campaigning, wherein he reached out to 28,000 homes. Shah will face Republican candidate and former NFL kicker Jay Feely, who has been backed by US President Donald Trump, for the November midterm election to the US Congress.

I have always prided myself on being a hardworking, grassroots candidate. Our victory in this primary was a grassroots victory where Arizona voters made their voices heard. Now, it’s my job to earn the support of every voter in this district—including Democrats who voted for… pic.twitter.com/iczMEyEhyt — Amish Shah, MD (@DrAmishShah) July 23, 2026

From NFL teammates to election rivals

Notably, before becoming political opponents, Shah and Feely were part of the same NFL team, where the Indian-origin doctor was the physician providing emergency care while Feely was the kicker, AP reported.

Today is Arizona’s primary election. If you haven’t voted yet, it’s time to make your voice heard. Let’s flip this district once and for all with a Democratic candidate guided by integrity, ready to put Arizona families first. Vote Dr. Amish Shah to be the Representative in… pic.twitter.com/DRLng46uZ3 — Amish Shah, MD (@DrAmishShah) July 21, 2026

Defeats establishment-backed rival

In the Democratic primary, Shah, who is a three-term member of the Arizona House of Representatives, defeated Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee backed Marlene Galán-Woods, a former Republican who switched during Trump’s first tenure.



Democratic candidate for Arizona’s 1st Congressional Dr. Amish Shah poses in Phoenix. (AP Photo) Democratic candidate for Arizona’s 1st Congressional Dr. Amish Shah poses in Phoenix. (AP Photo)

Woods became the third Democratic primary candidate to have lost a contested House primary this year, after Jasmeet Bains in California and Joe Baldacci in Maine.

Gujarati roots and medical career

Amish Shah was born to Gujarati parents who immigrated to the United States in 1960s, and earned his medical degree from the Northwestern University at Northwestern University Medical School as part of the Honours Program in Medical Education, PTI reported.

For his Master’s in Public Health at the University of California, Berkeley, Shah obtained a full merit scholarship which was followed by residency training in Emergency Medicine at New York City’s Level-1 trauma centre.



‘A grassroots victory,’ says Shah

After winning the Democratic nomination, Shah said, “Our victory in this primary was a grassroots victory where Arizona voters made their voices heard. Now, it’s my job to earn the support of every voter in this district – including Democrats who voted for another candidate, Independents frustrated with our political system, and Republicans disappointed with the state of the country,” PTI reported.

World.title: India hit by doping woes at CWG; judoka removed, weightlifting team sanctioned
World.content:
India is expected to win at least half-a-dozen medals in weightlifting, and the squad size reduction is likely to affect the tally. (PTI Photo)

Even before the Glasgow Commonwealth Games were declared open on Thursday, the Indian contingent suffered a setback after two of its medal prospects – one each in weightlifting and judo – were withdrawn following anti-doping rule violations.

Arun Kumar, a Judoka participating in the 78 kg category, was removed from the judo squad after he was provisionally suspended by the National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA). Although judo team is yet to leave for Glasgow, India can’t name a replacement due to the competition rules.

Hours after Kumar’s suspension, it was revealed that another Indian athlete, weightlifter Dilbagh Singh, would return from Glasgow – although for no fault of his own. Indian weightlifting has reported five positive cases during the period of June 1, 2025, to July 22, 2026. Consequently, India’s athlete quota was slashed from 16 to 11.

World.title: To ease Delhi traffic congestion, PWD to construct Karawal Nagar, Brittania Chowk elevated flyovers
World.content:
The plan to construct a flyover comes in the wake of residents, as well as the traffic police, flagging the issue of congestion in the stretch. (Representative image)

In a relief for commuters who are forced to spend hours in traffic densely congested roads in the Capital, the Public Works Department (PWD) has proposed to construct two elevated flyovers — one from Britannia Chowk to Outer Ring Road via ShakurBasti Railway Station, and another over the Karawal Nagar drain from Ankur Enclave to Gokulpuri Metro station — officials said on Thursday. The flyovers are also expected to ensure smooth connectivity between the West, North West, North-East, and Central parts of Delhi, they added.

According to a senior PWD official, both proposed elevated corridors will be 5-km-long.

“Britannia Chowk is one of the busiest junctions which connects West and North West Delhi and also provides connectivity to North Delhi and Central Delhi. The stretch is located in a densely populated area with mixed residential areas, restaurants, shops and office complexes on the road. It also sees good pedestrian movement owing to the presence of malls, metro stations and shops etc nearby. One can get stuck on a stretch for at least 30-35 minutes and the traffic gets worse during peak hours,” the official said.

World.title: ‘Immense respect’: Shubman Gill speaks up on CJP protest
World.content:
India’s ODI and Test captain Shubman Gill has broken his silence on the protests led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) over the NEET paper leaks. Gill is the latest among a string of sportspersons to have spoken on the protests, stating that he has “immense respect” for “every young person who believes in making their voice heard peacefully”.

“As a young Indian, I believe our generation deserves every opportunity to learn, dream and shape the future we all aspire to. I have immense respect for every young person who believes in making their voice heard peacefully,” said Gill in a statement that he put out in his Instagram stories. “Education has the power to shape our nation’s future. I hope we move forward with compassion, mutual respect and keeping the best interests of every student at heart.”

Gill put the statement up on his Instagram stories. (Shubman Gill Instagram screenshot) Gill put the statement up on his Instagram stories. (Shubman Gill Instagram screenshot)

Gill’s statement comes closely on the heels of India batting great Sachin Tendulkar breaking his silence on the protest. Today, when students feel disappointed that their hard work hasn’t been rewarded, it is understandable. Collectively, we should all work together towards ensuring they don’t feel this way again. Young India is full of dreams and energy. They are the fuel to our success,” said Tendulkar on X.

Top sportspersons Abhinav Bindra, Yuvraj Singh, Nikhat Zareen, had also spoken up on the issue, stressing on the need for “dialogue” and to “work together”. Bindra, India’s first individual Olympic gold medallist, did not directly mention the protests, but made his stance clear. Double Olympic medallist Manu Bhaker had also spoken up through a social media post for the youngsters hitting the streets. Boxer Zareen had asked the government to listen to the protestors while World Cup-winning cricketer cricketer Yuvraj also urged for dialogue.

Earlier, double Olympic medallist Manu Bhaker had also spoken up through a social media post for the youngsters hitting the streets.

Here’s what Bhaker wrote: “At this point, it’s about the lives of the future of our nation. It’s about us. I am a student, and at one point, we all were students. Every child deserves access to education, safety, and a fair chance at life. These are not privileges—they are fundamental rights.

“The students and children who lost their lives were meant to be the future of our country. Their dreams, their potential, and their futures should have been protected. This is not about promoting or opposing any political party. It is about speaking up for what truly matters—education, the environment, safety, and accountability. These issues affect every one of us, regardless of our beliefs.



“I take immense pride in representing my country. That is why it is deeply heartbreaking to see the students suffer like this. We owe them more. We owe every child a future where they can learn, grow, and dream without fear.”

World.title: Suniel Shetty says he first met son-in-law KL Rahul as a fan, regrets not buying IPL team
World.content:
Not too many people know that Suniel Shetty wanted to be a cricketer before he became an actor. An avid sports buff, little did he know that decades later, he’d get a cricketer as a son-in-law. KL Rahul married his daughter and actor Athiya Shetty in 2023. They’re now parents to a daughter, Evaarah Vipula, born last year.

Suniel Shetty on his first meeting with KL Rahul

Suniel Shetty recently recalled that he first met his then-future son-in-law KL Rahul as a fan. “It was a fanboy moment. I met him as a fan much, much before they met each other. To this day, that’s how I look at him — somebody who’s very well-spoken, soft, humble, and leaves a huge impact on the youth whenever and wherever he plays,” said the actor.

World.title: He stepped out to save his car. He returned to find his family buried beneath their ‘Taj Mahal’
World.content:
Since Sunday, Mohammad Latief has been wading through the rubble of the ‘Taj Mahal’ – the name locals gave his five-storeyed palatial house on the foothills of the Pir Panjal in Jammu’s Poonch district. All that remains of the painstakingly built house is its steel frame. Yet it is not this that Latief mourns — it’s the loss of his family: his wife, daughter, three sons and a toddler grandson.

The 59-year-old’s family were buried under a landslide that hit his house in the early hours of July 19, triggered by the relentless downpour that has assailed the Union Territory since July 19. The death toll in the landslides and floods in the region currently stands at 28, 22 of them from Poonch alone.

Eight people were buried under the landslide that hit Latief’s house, six of them his family: his wife Noor Safia, 45, daughter Khalda Kousar, 25, sons Sajad Ahmed, 16, Haq Nawaz, 10, and Shah Nawaz, 10, and grandson Sufian, 1. The other two victims were relatives — Bano Bi, 60, and her grandson Mohammad Akram, 7.



Only the bodies of Noor Safia, Bano Bi and Akram have been found, and the search continues for the rest.

“My family and the house are gone. Allah, who gave them to me, took them back and I accept his will,” he says.

Latief, who worked in Saudi Arabia and was home on six months’ leave, woke up to the deep rumbling of thunder at 3 am on July 19 and headed outside to move his vehicle, parked near a local stream down the hill, to a safer location.

As he was outside, his wife called to ask him to hurry back because it was raining heavily. That was the last time he heard her voice.

“When he returned, large boulders and mud marked the place where his home stood,” his nephew Zahoor Ahmad, a social activist, says.



Latief, who began working in Saudi Arabia in 1998, built the house over seven years, making sure he got the best of everything, right down to the bathroom fittings. “Even taps fitted in the bathrooms and kitchen were bought from abroad,” says his nephew Zahoor.

Jammu and Kashmir has been seeing relentless rain and landslides since Sunday, prompting the government to suspend traffic on highways. Deputy Chief Minister Surinder Choudhary and National Conference MP Mian Altaf had a close call on July 22 when a landslide nearly hit the vehicle they were travelling in to visit Rajouri and Poonch districts to oversee rescue operations.

The rain has also prompted the government to suspend the ongoing Amarnath Yatra pilgrimage.



Back in Poonch, Latief is desperate to find the remains of his family. His house is gone, and all that remains of his family are now his daughter Farida Kousar, married and living in Murrah, and his son Sarfaraz, an 18-year-old studying in Jammu.

“Now let me make an effort to find out if there are any survivors under the debris,” he says.

World.title: From Ladakh to Coorg: 5 of India’s best off-roading destinations
World.content:
India’s diverse terrain makes it a paradise for off-road enthusiasts. Whether you’re navigating mountain passes above 17,000 feet, crossing icy streams, or driving through deserts and dense forests, these routes test both your driving skills and endurance. Here’s a look at five of the country’s most exhilarating off-roading destinations.



Ladakh

No list of off-road adventures is complete without Ladakh. Home to some of the world’s highest motorable roads, the region offers everything from gravel tracks and water crossings to steep mountain passes.

Highlights:

* Khardung La and Chang La passes.

* Nubra Valley’s sand dunes

* Pangong Tso and Tso Moriri routes

* Dramatic landscapes above 5,000 metres

World.title: Trump says US-Saudi nuclear deal subject to Riyadh joining Abraham Accords
World.content:
US President Donald Trump on Thursday said a landmark deal with Saudi Arabia that would establish a civilian nuclear programme in the Gulf country is contingent on Riyadh joining the Abraham Accords and normalising ties with Israel.

In a post on Truth Social, Trump said the deal only pertained to the civilian use of nuclear facilities “such as the ones that Iran and [the] UAE (and others) already have”.

He added that the deal “will be approved, but is totally subject to Saudi Arabia joining the very respected and successful Abraham Accords”.

The Abraham Accords are a set of agreements brokered under Trump in 2020 and govern the normalisation of diplomatic relations between Israel and countries that have historically been hostile to it. They, however, remain unpopular among the public in many parts of the region, not least because they do not tackle the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

The move comes as the United States under President Donald Trump fights a war with Iran that began in large part over concerns with Tehran’s nuclear programme — an issue that remains a key point of contention during now-stalled peace talks.

Two agreements — one on “peaceful nuclear cooperation” and another on “bilateral safeguards” — were signed by US Energy Secretary Chris Wright and his Saudi counterpart Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman, the US Energy Department said.

The text of the deals was not immediately made public.

“Together, these two agreements lay the legal foundation for a decades-long, multi-billion-dollar partnership that advances several priority economic and strategic objectives, including nuclear non-proliferation,” the department said in a statement.

A provision in the deal would potentially see US companies build a uranium enrichment facility in Saudi Arabia, the Wall Street Journal reported. The Energy Department statement made no mention of such a provision and did not offer comment when asked about it by AFP.

The deal will be submitted to Congress for review, but the Republican-controlled legislature is unlikely to block its implementation.

US lawmakers from both parties and Israeli officials have previously voiced opposition to such a project over fears Saudi Arabia could eventually convert it to develop nuclear weapons.

Saudi Arabia, like Tehran, has long been adamant about its right to pursue a civilian nuclear programme.

Washington has sought in recent years to include any deal concerning a nuclear agreement in a wider strategic effort that would see Saudi Arabia normalise ties with Israel, along with the signing of a US-Saudi defence pact.

Pakistan and Saudi Arabia signed a mutual defence pact in September 2025.

Proliferation concerns

The US signed a nuclear agreement with the kingdom’s neighbour, the United Arab Emirates (UAE), in 2009, although the country does not enrich its own uranium.

A drone struck a generator in May near the UAE’s Barakah nuclear plant, the Arab world’s only such facility, causing a fire.

Policymakers have long feared that if Iran produced a nuclear weapon, the move would set off an arms race across the Gulf.

US Energy Secretary Wright dismissed concerns about proliferation, insisting the deal was in Washington’s economic and strategic interest.

“Rest assured, these agreements uphold the highest standards of nuclear safety and non-proliferation, while relying on the world’s best nuclear technology and scientists, designed right here in the United States,” he said in a statement.

The US-Saudi deal was signed under Section 123 of the US Atomic Energy Act.

The US has agreements governing nuclear cooperation with more than 50 countries, although the extent varies.

Experts said such a deal had been in the works for a considerable period, but some raised concerns about the potential for enrichment on Saudi soil.

“It would be a mistake to allow Saudi Arabia the capability for enrichment,” said Matthew Kroenig of the Atlantic Council in comments made before the deal was formally announced.

“Washington is right to strengthen its relationship with Riyadh, but it should not do so at the expense of its effective nuclear weapons non-proliferation standards.”

Jennifer T. Gordon, director of the Atlantic Council’s Nuclear Energy Policy Initiative, lauded the agreement as a “win for the US over Russia and China”.

“Saudi Arabia has made it clear that it will purchase nuclear energy technologies and begin a civil nuclear program; the only question has been whether the kingdom would choose to work with the US and its allies, or whether it would turn to Russia or China,” she said.

World.title: Heavy monsoon rains lash Lahore, disrupt routine life
World.content:
LAHORE: Heavy monsoon rains caused widespread water accumulation across Lahore on Thursday, disrupting routine life, slowing traffic and creating difficulties for commuters as rainwater remained stagnant on major roads, intersections and underpasses in several parts of the provincial capital.

Despite claims by the district administration and the Water and Sanitation Agency (Wasa) Lahore that drainage operations were being carried out on an emergency basis, residents faced difficulties due to three to four feet of standing water on streets, roads and submerged underpasses, along with slow traffic movement.

The city received 343 millimetres of rain over the past 48 hours, according to the Provincial Disaster Management Authority (PDMA), which warned of possible urban flooding during the second spell of monsoon rains.

Rainwater accumulated at more than 130 locations across Lahore, affecting traffic movement in several areas. Low-lying localities, major roads and underpasses remained among the worst-affected points.

In DHA Phases 1 to 5, water accumulation disrupted traffic at multiple locations. Around two feet of water accumulated from Defence Mor to A Block Checkpost, slowing the movement of vehicles.

The Ghazi Underpass and Masjid Chowk Underpass were closed due to heavy water accumulation, while traffic was diverted to alternate routes.

Traffic movement was also affected from Lalak Jan Chowk to LUMS Road, Watain Chowk to LUMS, Main Boulevard DHA and on the route from Masjid Chowk to Ghazi Chowk.

Vehicles were diverted through Z Block and other alternate routes due to the closure of underpasses.

Other areas reporting water accumulation included Harbanspura, Mall Road, Cooper Road, Lakshmi Chowk and Chouburji Chowk, where Wasa teams carried out drainage operations.

The rain also exposed recurring urban drainage challenges as water entered houses in low-lying areas of the city, while commuters complained about difficulties travelling through flooded roads and underpasses.

Many citizens complained that the authorities had not taken any measures to drain water from their houses, leaving them to remove it from their homes and streets on their own.

Citizens also faced delays as vehicles became stranded in rainwater on roads, forcing motorists to move slowly through standing water, while some avoided major roads due to the risk of breakdowns.

Several deep sinkholes, measuring around 10 square feet, appeared on three to four roads across the city, including Canal Road, Johar Town Main Boulevard and Bhekay Wala Mor, causing parts of the roads to collapse. Lahore traffic police cordoned off the affected areas and diverted traffic after Wasa teams reached the sites.

Another sinkhole reappeared on Khayaban-i-Firdousi, where barriers were placed as a precautionary measure and traffic was diverted to alternate routes.

The PDMA said that so far 21 people had died and 154 others had been injured in rain-related incidents across Punjab during the ongoing monsoon season.

Fifteen deaths occurred due to building collapses, two due to lightning strikes, three due to electrocution and one person drowned. At least 38 houses also sustained partial damage.

PDMA Director General Umar Abbas Mela directed district administrations to remain on high alert and warned of urban and flash flooding risks.

He advised citizens to avoid weak structures, low-lying areas and contact with electricity poles and wires during rainfall.

Meanwhile, Wasa Lahore said it had placed its teams on high alert and launched emergency drainage operations.

Wasa Managing Director Ghufran Ahmed visited several affected areas, including Mall Road, Cooper Road, Lakshmi Chowk and Chouburji Chowk, to monitor rainwater removal operations.

He said all disposal stations were operating at full capacity, while additional machinery and staff had been deployed at water accumulation points. More than 21 monsoon emergency relief camps had also been made operational.

He said Wasa’s 24/7 monsoon control room was monitoring the situation through more than 200 live cameras, including those installed at underpasses across the city.

Lahore Deputy Commissioner retired Capt Ali Ijaz also visited Harbanspura and other areas to review drainage operations.

He claimed that most major roads and waterlogged points had been cleared in record time, while the remaining low-lying areas would be drained soon.

The administration and Wasa urged citizens to avoid unnecessary travel during heavy rainfall, stay away from electricity infrastructure, avoid driving through flooded areas and report water accumulation to Wasa through its helpline, 1334.

However, residents criticised the recurring problem of water accumulation in Lahore, saying that despite repeated monsoon preparations, poor drainage capacity, blocked sewer lines and delays in rainwater removal continued to create difficulties for citizens every year.

Meanwhile, Chief Traffic Officer (CTO) Syed Abdul Raheem Sherazi directed officials to cordon off the sinkholes on different roads across the city and take measures to provide alternate routes to citizens for smooth travel.

He also deployed traffic officials outside the underpasses to divert traffic. “Rain duty with commitment, professionalism and public safety is their top priority,” he said.

World.title: Pakistan 'disappointed' with EU report on GSP+ compliance issues, says it understates reforms
World.content:
Pakistan on Thursday expressed “disappointment” with the European Union’s (EU) recent report that pointed out issues in Pakistan’s compliance with its commitments under the Generalised Scheme of Preferences Plus (GSP+).

The report was issued last week as part of the European Commission’s global assessment of the GSP during the 2023-2025 period. It said Pakistan had “regressed in a number of areas while positive change was limited”.

Responding to a query during a weekly press briefing on Thursday, Foreign Office (FO) spokesperson Tahir Andrabi appreciated the report’s “acknowledgement of Pakistan’s legislative progress” and its continued compliance with 27 international conventions under the GSP+.

“Nevertheless, I would be remiss if I do not express disappointment with the assessment, with the report’s overall narrative which does not present sufficiently balanced pictures of Pakistan’s performance,” Andrabi added.

He said the EU report “understates the breadth of reforms undertaken since Pakistan joined GSP+ in 2014” and “places disproportionate emphasis on the lower-than-desired progress in a few areas”.

At the same time, the FO spokesman affirmed that GSP+ remained “central to Pakistan’s economic relationship with the EU, supporting exports, employment, women’s economic participation, poverty reduction and broader economic development”.

He observed that GSP+ was a “mutually beneficial arrangement in that aspect”.

“We will remain constructively engaged with the European Commission and other EU institutions and remain committed to the effective implementation of international conventions underpinning the GSP framework,” Andrabi affirmed.

He highlighted that beyond GSP+, Pakistan’s EU cooperation extended to development, migration, counterterrorism, regional stability, climate resilience, connectivity and many other areas.

FO ‘completely rejects’ Amnesty report on Kabul strikes

The FO spokesperson also “completely” rejected an Amnesty International report released on July 21 that claimed that Pakistan targeted a rehab facility in Kabul on March 16, which purportedly resulted in a large number of civilian casualties.

Responding to a question, Andrabi said, “We completely reject the allegations made by Amnesty International.”

He termed it “unfortunate that such serious allegations have been presented without any credible evidence”.

The FO spokesperson asserted: “Any military strikes by Pakistan were undertaken in exercise of its right to self-defence under principles of necessity and as a measure of last resort and directed only and exclusively against terrorists and their logistical support bases in Afghanistan.”

He maintained that Pakistan’s “response was proportionate to the level of threat while strictly adhering to the principle of distinction, precaution and proportionality”.

“The scale and scope of this action reflected restraint, particularly in light of the severity and frequency of terrorist attacks faced by Pakistan. Pakistan rejects any insinuation in this regard otherwise.”

Both the government and the military had asserted that Pakistani forces had targeted an ammunition and drone storage site in the airstrikes conducted on the night of March 16.

Andrabi called on Amnesty and the international community to “direct rigorous scrutiny towards the Taliban regime’s continued patronage of terrorist groups” and to “address the root causes that this Amnesty International report has conspicuously failed to address”.

He further urged the international community to hold the Afghan Taliban regime accountable for its failure to uphold its obligations under the relevant United Nations Security Council resolutions and its commitments under the Doha agreement to “prevent Afghan soil from being used as a launch pad for terrorism”.

Andrabi declared that Pakistan reserved the right to “take all necessary measures in order to safeguard its sovereignty [and] territorial integrity, and safety and security of its people”.

“No responsible state can remain passive when its civilians and security forces are repeatedly targeted,” he emphasised.

The FO official said the Taliban regime continued to “maintain a permissive environment for a range of terrorist organisations, including the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) and other affiliates”.

He added: “The freedom to undertake terrorist activities allowed to these listed organisations, their access to bases and sanctuaries on Afghan soil, as well as ability to recruit, finance and execute cross-border attacks, constitutes a serious threat to regional peace and security.”

Noting that such attacks had killed and injured “thousands of innocent Pakistani citizens”, Andrabi asserted they were “planned, financed, supported and carried out from Afghan soil all under the watch and patronage and active facilitation by the Taliban regime”.

In the past few years, Islamabad has repeatedly urged the Taliban administration in Kabul to dismantle terrorist sanctuaries on Afghan soil that are used for attacks in Pakistan. Officials say those appeals have gone unheeded.

Dar to attend SCO meeting in Kyrgyzstan

Separately, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar will arrive in Kyrgyzstan today on a two-day visit to take part in the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation’s (SCO) meeting of the Council of Foreign Ministers (CFM).

The SCO is a 10-nation Eurasian security and political grouping whose members include Pakistan, China, India, Russia and Iran. The CFM is the third-highest forum in the SCO format.

In his press briefing, Andrabi said Dar will lead the Pakistani delegation at the CFM.

He added that during the visit, DPM Dar was also expected to call on Kyrgyzstan President Sadyr Zhaparov and hold multiple bilateral meetings on the sidelines of the SCO moot.

Later, the FO also issued a curtain-raiser on the visit, noting that the CFM focuses on the issues of international relations, as well as the foreign and security policies of the SCO.

World.title: Israeli far-right minister leads hundreds to Al-Aqsa Mosque on Jewish mourning day
World.content:
Israeli far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir led hundreds of Israeli Jews into Jerusalem’s Al-Aqsa mosque compound on Thursday, breaching the site’s decades-old status quo as he marked a Jewish day of mourning.

The visit coincided with Tisha B’Av, the Jewish fasting day commemorating the destruction of the First and Second Temples, which is being observed from Wednesday night through Thursday this year.

AFP footage showed Ben Gvir and hundreds of fellow worshippers at the Al-Aqsa compound, including Jewish settlers who lined up from the early morning hours to enter the site, where many performed prayers.

“Look at what’s happening here: Jews are praying and feel that they are the rightful owners here,” Ben Gvir said in a video filmed at the compound and posted on his Telegram channel.

“Everywhere, people understand that the State of Israel is the sovereign authority. There is still more to do, and with God’s help, we will continue to move forward.”

Located in Israeli-annexed East Jerusalem, the compound is revered as Islam’s third holiest site and, simultaneously, as Judaism’s most sacred location, where the two ancient temples once stood.

Access is governed by a decades-old “status quo” arrangement between Israel and Jordan, whose religious foundation administers the site. Under that arrangement, Jews may visit but are not permitted to pray there, while Muslim worship is meant to continue uninterrupted.

In recent years, however, Ben Gvir and other Jewish visitors have repeatedly tested and breached those limits, including through open prayer at the compound, drawing condemnation from Jordan, the Ramallah-based Palestinian Authority and Muslim religious bodies.

Jewish visitors enter the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound in Jerusalem’s Old City on July 23, 2026. — Reuters

Jordan denounced Ben Gvir’s latest visit to the compound.

“Jordan firmly rejects and strongly condemns the continued incursions by Israeli officials, Knesset members and extremist settlers into Al-Aqsa mosque, as well as the role of Israeli police in facilitating these actions,” foreign ministry spokesperson Fouad Al-Majali said in a statement on Thursday.

He described the actions as “unacceptable attempts to impose new realities at Al-Aqsa Mosque/Al-Haram Al-Sharif through efforts to alter its existing arrangements”.

Turkiye also slammed Ben Gvir’s visit.

“We remind the international community that it is a shared responsibility to prevent the Netanyahu government’s provocative actions and attempts to create faits accomplis, which violate the historical and legal status of holy sites in Jerusalem, particularly Al-Aqsa Mosque, which belongs exclusively to Muslims,” the Turkish foreign ministry said.

The Israeli government has publicly maintained that its policy on the status quo remains unchanged, even as incidents like Thursday’s continue to inflame the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

Since taking office, Ben Gvir has stormed the site more than a dozen times, and has previously used Tisha B’av gatherings to call for tougher action against Palestinians in Gaza and the Israeli-occupied West Bank.

Beyond marking the temples’ destruction, the day of fasting is traditionally tied to a string of calamities said to have befallen the Jewish people on or near the same date throughout history.

World.title: Karachi police claim suspect in six-year-old girl's abduction, murder killed in shootout
World.content:
KARACHI: The police on Thursday killed the alleged abductor and murderer of a six-year-old girl in a shootout after the suspect allegedly opened fire on law enforcers during a raid in Karachi’s Keamari area.

According to a statement issued by the Keamari police spokesperson, a first information report (No. 265/2026) under Sections 364-A and 302 of the Pakistan Penal Code was registered at Jackson Police Station regarding the abduction and murder of a six-year-old girl.

The spokesperson stated that police obtained CCTV footage from various locations along with other available evidence, which was thoroughly examined during the investigation.

“Based on the CCTV footage and information gathered during the investigation, police received credible information regarding the whereabouts of a suspect,” the spokesperson said.

Acting on this information, he said, a police party reached the Mubarak Mosque area, within the jurisdiction of Jackson Police Station. “However, upon seeing the police party, the suspect opened fire on the officers, prompting the police to retaliate,” he claimed.

“During the exchange of gunfire, the individual sustained gunshot injuries and later died,” the spokesperson further claimed.

Immediately after the incident, he added that the crime scene was secured and all relevant evidence was taken into custody in accordance with legal procedures.

“A separate case regarding the police encounter is being registered at Jackson Police Station, while legal and forensic proceedings related to the incident are also underway.”

The police spokesperson added that an investigation into the abduction and murder of the young girl was “continuing comprehensively in light of CCTV footage, medico-legal findings, forensic evidence, technical analysis and other available evidence”.

Meanwhile, the body of the six-year-old girl was recovered from bushes in the Manora area, police said.

According to Police Surgeon Dr Sumaiyya Syed, “The victim was subjected to sexual violence.”

“There are multiple marks of violence all over the body,” she added. “All samples have been collected. The cause of death has been reserved pending the reports.”

Earlier this month, police arrested a 20-year-old man for the kidnapping, rape and murder of a six-year-old boy before allegedly dumping the victim’s body, wrapped in a gunny bag, onto an empty plot from the third floor.

World.title: Torrential rains disrupt travel across GB as floods wash away roads, bridges
World.content:
Torrential rains in Gilgit-Baltistan caused widespread travel disruptions in the mountainous region as flash floods and landslides washed away roads and bridges, leaving thousands, including tourists, stranded.

The Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) forecast rain and warned of glacial lake outburst floods (GLOFs) in GB until July 26.

Floods blocked the Karakoram Highway (KKH), Babusar Road, Baltistan Road, Naltar Highway, Ghizer-Shandur Road, Astore Valley Road and other routes connecting various remote areas, leaving thousands, including tourists, stranded at multiple locations.

The GB Disaster Management Authority (GBDMA) said the KKH was blocked at multiple sections from Dassu to Hunza and Nagar districts.

Picture taken on July 23, 2026 shows a tractor stranded after landslides and floods were caused by torrential rainfall in Gilgit-Baltistan. —Photo via author

Continuous flooding at multiple locations caused difficulties for relief and rehabilitation activities. Many areas remained disconnected from surrounding regions as bridges and connecting roads were washed away.

In Skardu, severe flooding in the Tormak Nallah area of Rondu subdivision washed away at least three important communication bridges, including the Malan Bridge.

Floods also severely damaged roads, communication bridges, farmlands, crops and infrastructure in various areas of Kharmang, Ghanche and Shigar districts.

Suspension bridges and power houses were also damaged by floods in Haramosh.

Picture taken on July 23, 2026 shows aftereffects of landslides and floods caused by torrential rainfall in Gilgit-Baltistan. —Photo via author

Electricity and water supply systems were disrupted, suspending communication services in Astore, Tangir, Thore and other areas of Diamer.

Furthermore, drinking water schemes, irrigation channels and protective embankments were destroyed, while several villages were cut off from one another.

Dozens of families in Losala village of Astore, Thore Valley, Tangir in Diamer and other areas were rendered homeless as a result of floods and landslides.

Picture taken on July 23, 2026 shows a van stuck after landslides and floods were caused by torrential rainfall in Gilgit-Baltistan. —Photo via author

Across Ghizer district, temporary road blockages, localised flooding and partial damage to two houses were reported. As a precautionary measure, vulnerable communities were evacuated to designated safe locations.

Rising water levels in the Hunza-Nagar River have placed eight households in Gilgit’s Jutal area at risk.

Picture taken on July 23, 2026 shows aftereffects of landslides and floods caused by torrential rainfall in Gilgit-Baltistan. —Photo via author

In Ghizer, river erosion has damaged agricultural land and non-fruit trees in Yasin Valley, Sheliabad, Amit and other areas, while the Ghizer-Shandur and Ghizer-Gilgit roads remain blocked.

Authorities have advised passengers and tourists to avoid unnecessary travel in the region.

Authorities’ response

A statement issued by the GBDMA said rising water levels in rivers and streams had damaged homes, roads, bridges, crops and agricultural land.

The GBDMA, district administration, Rescue 1122 and other agencies are jointly engaged in relief activities, according to the statement.

As of Thursday, affected families were being shifted to safer locations, while the process of providing tents, rations, medicines and clean drinking water was underway.

The GBDMA said relief items, including tents, food, medicines and other essential supplies, had been provided to affected people.

Picture taken on July 23, 2026 shows aftereffects of landslides and floods caused by torrential rainfall in Gilgit-Baltistan. —Photo via author

GB Chief Minister Amjad Hussain directed authorities to expedite relief and rehabilitation work in the affected areas.

CM Hussain instructed all concerned departments and the district administration to remain on alert round the clock to ensure the safety of lives and property.

He directed the food and health departments to ensure an uninterrupted supply of rations, clean drinking water, tents, medicines and other essential items in the affected areas.

Orders were issued to immediately mobilise heavy machinery for emergency repairs of infrastructure, bridges and main and secondary roads damaged by flash floods, and for the restoration of traffic.

The GBDMA and district administration were directed to remain proactive in dealing with the emergency situation by maintaining close coordination with the NDMA.

The CM said that the regional government would not leave the people alone in this difficult time.

“Rehabilitation of the victims and all possible assistance will be ensured by utilising all available resources,” he added.

He directed all concerned commissioners and deputy commissioners to conduct field inspections themselves and submit daily monitoring reports on relief activities to the CM’s Secretariat.

Earlier, CM Hussain visited the NDMA headquarters in Islamabad and met NDMA Chairman Lieutenant General Inam Haider Malik and other senior officials to discuss the current situation.

According to a statement, the NDMA chairman briefed CM Hussain on the authority’s ongoing initiatives aimed at reducing disaster risks, strengthening preparedness and improving emergency response across Pakistan, particularly in GB.

The NDMA chairman said that modern scientific and technological systems were being used to issue timely early warnings in disaster-prone areas, while relief and rehabilitation activities were being carried out in coordination with relevant institutions following natural disasters.

He further informed the chief minister that glaciers in GB were being continuously monitored using advanced scientific methods, with each glacier assigned a unique identification code to ensure effective monitoring of its movement, size and potential risks.

CM Hussain said glaciers in GB were Pakistan’s largest natural source of freshwater and stressed that their protection, effective monitoring and sustainable management should remain national priorities.

He praised the NDMA’s automation, scientific monitoring and technology-based systems, expressing confidence that these measures would further strengthen disaster preparedness, particularly in GB.

He said the Government of GB would further strengthen its institutional cooperation with the NDMA to develop a coordinated and effective strategy for disaster risk management.

The chief minister emphasised that the impacts of climate change had become a reality and that GB was one of the most affected regions, with increasing risks of GLOFs, flash floods and landslides.

He stressed that climate-related challenges should be prioritised at all national forums and called for coordinated efforts by federal and provincial institutions, along with all relevant stakeholders, to protect communities, infrastructure and natural resources.

World.title: Kashmir, IWT among key global challenges threatening 'peaceful coexistence', Dar tells Asean moot
World.content:
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Thursday drew attention to key challenges threatening peaceful coexistence and stability across the world, listing the Kashmir dispute and India’s threats to Pakistan’s water share among them.

He made the remarks at the 33rd ministerial meeting of the Asean Regional Forum (ARF) held in Manila, the Philippines.

Foreign ministers and delegates from 27 member states of ARF gathered for the summit, which comes amid a flare-up in the war between the United States and Iran. The conflict is a key concern for the 11-nation Asean, which has a combined gross domestic product of about $3.8 trillion heavily reliant on Middle East oil.

Addressing the meeting, DPM Dar highlighted eight key challenges that he said “continue to threaten peaceful coexistence, stability and our livelihoods across the region and the world”.

“Any delay in addressing these challenges will only undermine our collective efforts to achieve peace, stability and prosperity across our regions and beyond,” he said.

Noting the “continued failure” to resolve longstanding disputes in South Asia, he particularly called attention to the Jammu and Kashmir dispute as “the heart of regional instability”.

He said that Pakistan continued to advocate for a “just and peaceful” settlement, in line with the United Nations Charter and resolutions as well as the aspirations of the Kashmiri people.

The deputy premier also expressed concern once again over India’s decision to unilaterally place the Indus Water Treaty (IWT) in abeyance after hostilities flared up between the two nations last year.

“We simply cannot afford to let this serious provocative development remain unaddressed,” Dar said, urging the entire international community to support a peaceful resolution to the issue.

The issue of water has remained a bitter point of contention between the two nuclear-armed nations since May 2025. Earlier this month, the top brass of Pakistan’s army vowed to undertake “all measures necessary” to ensure the availability of Pakistan’s rightful share of water.

US-Iran war and Gaza

Dar also highlighted Pakistan’s role in facilitating a ceasefire between the US and Iran and convening talks at the leadership level between the two arch-enemies after 47 years.

Appreciating the confidence placed in the country by the US, Iran, Gulf countries and others, he said, “These hard-earned achievements through dialogue and diplomacy have created a valuable opportunity to advance lasting peace. We must not let this opportunity slip through our hands.”

He expressed his hope that Pakistan’s efforts to bring peace would contribute to regional stability, as well as the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and the resumption of normal shipping. He called on the international community to reinforce these efforts through sustained dialogue, diplomacy and constructive engagement.

Thirdly, the deputy premier called attention to the ongoing humanitarian crisis in occupied Palestinian territories, calling it “deeply alarming”.

“Our collective failure to prevent the genocidal streak unleashed in Gaza raises serious questions about our collective conscience as human beings, and about our ability to prevent the continued atrocities in the region,” he said.

FM Dar reiterated Pakistan’s support for Palestinian self-determination and the establishment of an independent, sovereign, viable and contiguous state of Palestine based on pre-1967 borders.

‘Common threat’ of terrorism

DPM Dar also highlighted the issue of terrorism, terming it “a common threat and challenge for all of us in varying degrees”.
